An Intercepted Little Letter

From the 'sharp' Będzin 'young men at the groom's side', who have become famous, to the 'dull' in-law from Częstochowa on the bride's side, Reb Henekh.
Mp"h[?] 18 and 13.

The morning after the famous wedding — with its so cheerful-interesting and highly amusing 'reception' (kabbalat panim) scenes, with singing and exotic dances, with coarse[?] jokes and 'tenorish'[?] tongues etc. — which took place last week in Częstochowa, the Będzin 'guest performers', the Ger-Hasidic groom's young men — 'the seraphim and holy beasts' — who had stayed there overnight with the groom's shtreimel in their possession (which they had snatched before the chuppah as a pledge for the demanded 90 złoty 'for wine and travel expenses'), at once in the morning, rousing themselves from their beds on the benches in a Ger shtibl and pouring the 'kiyor' water over their fingernails, empowered the eldest among them (the one who, as the firstborn, had laid the shtreimel under his head...) to write to the said in-law here[?] a letter of warning, which they immediately sent him through a shtibl boy.

This interesting letter, which we managed to copy, read — just imagine — as follows:

'With God's help, Monday of the week of "These are the accounts of the pledge" [mishkon, a pun on mishkan, Tabernacle]... second day of Rosh Chodesh Adar II, in which we increase joy, the year Tsarevet ["heartburn"] by the short count, in the holy community of Czestochowa[?], may it be rebuilt speedily in our days, Amen.

'Listen here, you little in-law Henekh! Let it be known to you, as you well know, that if, God forbid, you defy the holy command which went forth yesterday from our lips[?], and do not pay us, on top of the 30 zł. we already received from you last night, the rest — 60 złoty — until it completes the number of "tsaddik" (90) — know with absolute clarity that all 15 of us "young men at the groom's side" are now, this morning, travelling together straight by the first train home to Będzin (on expenses with which the local "Tseirim" [Agudah youth], may they live, help us after the fact), for we are hurrying back so as to still make it to the great Rosh Chodesh feast taking place, with God's help, today before dawn in the Będzin Ger shtibl (with lots of onions...), and so we will take the shtreimel along with us and [pawn][?] it there for drink (not bad, it is a costly item. It smells of a [—][?]...) or we will take it and simply [give it away][?] for drink for a good cause, namely: we will give it as a present to the Orthodox... headmistress of the Będzin "Beit Yaakov" school, for a collar... (She is a fine Jewish daughter, who of course does not wear such long hanging sidelocks as we do, but only a wig on her head, a "sheytl" in the vernacular; but on the other hand she wears, as we have explicitly checked, a tallit katan under her apron, and besides she has great educational importance (like the mother Sarah Schenirer of Kraków), so she is worthy of a shtreimel, i.e. a collar).

'Listen here, you brazen-faced, beggarly in-law! [—][?] you ought truly to regard yourself as greatly privileged that, with Heaven's help, you got a dear little son-in-law who actually comes from our crowd, and who is one of the firm pillars on which the great edifice of the Będzin holy Agudah [Agudat Israel] leans; for not everyone merits so splendid a vessel as he and his like... A young man who possesses, no evil eye, a handsome... beard (in the vernacular "bord"), who is thus by no means a shaven one, God forbid, nor a Zionist or Mizrachist, heaven forbid, nor a "tsitsialist" [pun on socialist/tsitsit], and it goes without saying not a "Red" (he is barely a "Yellow"...); and yesterday you simply should have counted yourself lucky seeing how at the reception your groom sat truly like a king among his troops, surrounded, so to speak, by a whole [dozen] plus a quarter dozen (explicitly: fifteen) of his "shtibl knights" (exactly half of Samson's ancient "thirty companions"...): young men of whom anyone who looks at them can say that upon each one separately the Shekhinah rests beneath the skullcap, which lies extraordinarily deep down to the nape, and between the rabbinic, broadly branching and dishevelled sidelocks, as well as on the genuine "Kotzk-style" collars of their shirts, which are "transferred from another hide" and without neckties (may [—][?]'s collars be an atonement...).

'Yes, if you had only been a bit sensible, you would have had to settle with us right away yesterday before the chuppah, as is proper... i.e. give the whole sum we demanded as ransom money, "pidyon nefesh", and not cause us to have to pull the shtreimel off the groom's head and therefore be "watchmen until morning"... No, Henekh! That is not how one treats guests, and choice young men at that — such as [—][?] neglected a whole day (of homely wares and holy Agudah work and politics) and dragged themselves, making[?] a special trip from Będzin to here, just to pay our friend [your groom] his last bachelor honour; and with whom we fulfilled here, truly with self-sacrifice, the commandment of "How does one dance before the... groom", dancing around him and with him almost a whole night through, in several "[—]"[?]... whose fervent dances, two and three hours on end, lasted until midnight, heaven forbid (and let it be mentioned in passing to his credit that the groom himself in person, though he was fasting, hopped and sang along — no less than we, who were well fed and well watered — with staring, glazed eyes the [—][?] Rebbe's "And purify our hearts to serve You in tru— tru— truth"...); and were it not for the bitter rush to the chuppah from the in-law women and wedding guests on the one side, and from the officiant on the other side (some religious judge not of our circle, but actually a Radomsko Hasid, God save us... it would have been a great mitzvah to tear out his pointed beard!) — were it not for precisely this, that they, the foolish women with their [—][?] weeping and[?] plain curses, and the [—][?] menfolk, headed by that scholar who has no sense, all pestered us with voices and loudest voices to release the groom already, whom we had — according to the "law of the young men" — firmly barricaded in a corner by the buffet — we would have gone on dancing with him, with this groom, so tipsily a whole full night... because the parting was hard for us: we could not part from him, and he for his part could not tear himself away from us. (The whole strange business of going to the chuppah was, poor thing, altogether unpleasant [Polish "przykre"] for him: to go and stand there with a... a "that", with a strange girl, and... to take into his hand "her" finger — like one of the empty and reckless — and that finger must precisely fit into the hollow of a golden ring... Brrr! God preserve us, not upon us, the Merciful save us!...)

'Now we give you, Henekh, one last warning: if you do not send us at once, through the bearer of this letter, the sixty złoty, it will be, as it says somewhere in a verse in the "Daf Yomi", "and you will groan at your end" — i.e. you will regret it bitterly, namely thus:

Next week, God willing, when the Rebbe, may he live, passes through on his way from the Land of Israel, you, as one of ours, will surely also want to wait for him at the railway together with all the homely crowd — know then that we, the Ger young-men's brigade of Będzin, escorting the Rebbe as far as Kalishik[?], as is always our custom — when the train stops at the Częstochowa[?] station, will run down specially onto the platform and then toss you, the in-law in question, into the air, and in the blink of an eye[sic] we will make you there, frankly and freely, a "great pledge"... in the Ger style — so that your generations may know! And there is no doubt that even the railway guards will not interfere with us in this matter, since we "Tseirim" — like the "Agudah" in general — have in recent years, thank God, been privileged as "close to the government", that is; and the merit of the well-known prince and great man in Israel, our Orthodox deputy, Reb Aryeh Leybele Mincberg, may his Rock keep him, will surely protect us all.

Young men of the true Ger guard of the holy community of Będzin.
Handed over for print by Reb Zelign.'
Three Percent

[Article — Zionism; Keren Hayesod and the building of the Land.] By Yankev Garzalka.

Ussishkin [Menachem Ussishkin] once related on some occasion a very characteristic dialogue that took place before the war between him and Baron Rothschild, "the Well-Known Benefactor" (ha-Nadiv ha-Yadua). The Baron reproached Ussishkin: why do the Zionists always make such a great noise in the world about every trifle?

"I," said the Baron, "do much more in the Land of Israel than you Zionists: I buy more land, colonise more, create and build, but all quietly, without noise, without clamour, while you Zionists beat the drums and parade over every dunam of land, over every smallest achievement, and that is neither clever nor healthy..."

"Yes, you are right, Herr Baron," answered Ussishkin, "I fully agree with you, and I am ready as of tomorrow to change our tactics and adopt your method; only one small question I have for you: would you hand over your chequebook to my keeping?... You must know, Herr Baron, that to get a few groszy out of a Jew one has to beat all the drums; otherwise he does not give..."

Such is the fate of the upbuilding of the Land of Israel. Surely it ought to be otherwise; surely it would be far better, more useful, more constructive and more profitable if the whole Jewish people were in the category of "all of us wise, all of us understanding", if the necessity of an independent Jewish home in the Land of Israel had penetrated deep into every Jewish brain, and every Jewish heart came of its own accord to pay its debt to the building of the Land of Israel, and each kept saying to the other the well-known "Chazak" (Be strong!); how much energy would then be saved on financial propaganda, oral and written, and the money better spent on the direct upbuilding itself!

Our situation would then look very different, both in the Land of Israel and in the Diaspora. It is a simple calculation: on average, altogether about three percent of the entire Jewish people pay to the Keren Hayesod, the chief instrument for building the Land of Israel; and however impoverished the Jewish masses may be, it is still impossible to admit the thought that this percentage is the real proportion with regard to the part of the people that could, with good will and a positive attitude, contribute to the Keren Hayesod — especially considering that precisely among the steady contributors there is always a considerable part which, by its financial means, ought surely to belong among the non-payers: the Zionist-idealist part, which gives away the last bite from its mouth. Those who have taken part in the work for the Keren Hayesod since its founding could tell a great deal about all this, but the fact remains a fact: only three percent in all take part in the building of the Land of Israel through Keren Hayesod donations, i.e. 97 percent of the Jewish people have stood and still[?] stand aloof, indifferent or even hostile to the whole cause of building the Land.

The Jewish situation would look quite different if instead of three percent we had three or four times as many; then over the last 10–12 years we would have had at least another hundred thousand Jews in the Land of Israel, especially from Poland, where the urge towards the Land of Israel has lately grown very strong. The Jewish Yishuv in the Land of Israel would thereby have become firmer and more secure on the one hand, and on the other the air would have been made so much fresher and more room freed for the remaining brethren in Poland. Instead of the one [printed "a a" — doubled] million dunams of land we have so far in Eretz Israel, we would have two or three times as much, and so many more Jewish settlements strengthened, enlarged and consolidated. This is the clear elementary ABC, and like every truth it must be said again and again on every occasion.

And this must happen: if it has not happened until today out of free will, through one's own good will, through the inner urge of the soul, through the inner longing to free oneself from servile exile and build a home of one's own in one's own land, the Land of Israel — it will now have to happen out of fear...

If our clamour has so far not been able to awaken the spark of the Land of Israel in the Jewish heart, our call will nevertheless have to disturb the Jewish reason, the Jewish brain; it will have to understand that there is no way back, that the ground is burning everywhere under our feet, that we are threatened with being swallowed up by the raging waves of general need[?] and Jew-hatred throughout the world, and all the evil winds are driving us with colossal force precisely towards our one and only shore — the Land of Israel.

The problem of the Land of Israel has ceased to be a matter of wanting or not wanting, and has become a question of "to be or not to be".

Three percent of Jewish households made the beginning; with superhuman effort they are holding the positions taken, but three percent alone cannot bear the great burden of building the Land, and they may, God forbid, grow tired and fall halfway. Fresh forces must be created, new building energies; the number of Keren Hayesod payers must be doubled, tripled, and this is the task of our communal workers at the present moment. It can no longer be a matter of merely discharging an obligation; events around us are racing, attacks are coming from all sides — therefore let us mobilise all our forces, strengthen the camp, a mobilisation along the whole front, and let the disgrace of three percent finally vanish from our statistical tables.
Women's Weapons

[Feuilleton — humour; unemployment.] (A small feuilleton.)

In Australia a remarkable thing happened: a few thousand unemployed women came to the Minister of Labour and demanded that he give them work, and if not, they would... strip naked before his eyes.

I do not know whether this threat ["strashunek"] had any effect on the Australian minister, but I simply like the idea of the Australian women.

One of the two: either the women considered themselves great beauties and were sure they would compel the minister with their beauty to find them work, or they held that the minister is absolutely no connoisseur of beauty.

What am I saying this against?

Against the very remedy of stripping naked.

It seems, then, that somewhere in the world nakedness is indeed a charm against hunger and want.

With us, however, I am sure such a charm would not help, and for the following reasons:

Firstly, our women are used to going about naked even in the very best of times. How long has it been impossible to find in Europe, for love or money, a dressed girl or[?] woman? They all went about "dressed naked", so that nobody would be surprised if a delegation of naked women were to come.

Secondly, there is a view that not with all people, even with ministers, can women arouse sympathy and compassion when they are naked. There are people who lose their common sense when they see a naked woman before them, and there are, on the contrary, such as only then come to their senses and do not even want to look at them.

Among the latter there are often ministers too.

You see, if I were a lover of women, I would have given them different advice on how to obtain something from a minister.

Instead of taking off their clothes, they should have come fully dressed and... fired at the minister with[?]... talk.

For if someone may remain unmoved before the mute female body, every mortal must fear the classical and historical nine measures of talk [allusion to the Talmudic saying that of ten measures of speech that came down to the world, women took nine — Kiddushin 49b].

In any case, in the present helplessness, when governments do not know how to fight the bitter plague called unemployment, my remedy, it seems to me, is not bad at all.

It would at any rate be worth trying.

Rebus.
The exhibition of the artists’ group “Independents”

[Sosnowiec — art.] A group of 7 painters is represented with their works at the exhibition in Sosnowiec [?].
S. Cygler [Ziegler] (Będzin) is a painter who is under the influence of the French school.
His palette is rich in colour; he draws from it splendid and subtle colours — gamuts that breathe individual freshness.
Although Cygler's exhibit is varied, his pictures are nevertheless created according to a unified painterly conception.
This means that he knows his own way, and individuality is one of the most important values in an artist.
Besides oil paintings and watercolours, Cygler has also exhibited a series of graphic works, which are very well drawn and composed and stand at a high technical level.
S. Miller (Kraków) has splendid watercolours that rivet the viewer. The artist brilliantly masters the very difficult technique of watercolour painting. His pictures do not suffer from over-exertion and therefore breathe freshness.
Weaker are his oil works, especially in the drawing, which is too stiff; the lines lack the elasticity by which his watercolours are distinguished.
J. Badower (Kraków) operates too much with the banal colours red and green, which is very shocking. His pictures mostly bear a decorative character and suffer from superficiality. Yet he has a few things that have artistic value and give aesthetic pleasure.
Wł. Oraszkiewicz [?] (Sosnowiec) is a painter of considerable artistic culture. He draws a fine play of colours from his brush; his pictures are painted with seriousness and understanding.
Augustowicz-Dąbrowska (Kraków) is represented with only 3 pictures, and that is too few to express an opinion.
The same applies to the painter St. Dąbrowski (Kraków), who likewise has no more than 3 works.
Tadeusz Jeleń [?] (Tarnów) has a couple of pictures that are well composed, but treated too sketchily.
S. R.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week’s portion (Shemini)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Shemini
The Portion
—o—
a) "And they died before the Lord" (Lev. 10:2)
The sin of Nadab and Abihu was "in their drawing near before the Lord" — that they only ever prayed before God. That befits [?] such holy men in the World of Truth... A leader in this world must care more for the people. Rabbi Ishmael ben Elisha, when he entered the Holy of Holies, did not say "And so, put Your fear", but asked for mercy on the Jews: "May Your mercy overcome Your anger"... Moses our teacher, too, erred when he did not want to go to Pharaoh and redeem the Jews before the appointed time. Moses preferred that the Jews suffer a little longer in exile, so long as God's name be magnified — and for that God grew angry with him. Tiferet Shlomo.
—o—
One of the sins of Nadab and Abihu was that "they set their eyes on positions" — that they, as the High Priest's children, occupied all sorts of communal posts... Baal HaTurim.
—o—
b) "Drink no wine nor strong drink" (ibid., 9)
The Land of Israel is, after all, "the joy of the whole earth". Jerusalem is the source of joy. No sadness ever reigned there. (Outside Jerusalem there was a counting-hall, where everyone came to make his accounts, because in Jerusalem one was not allowed to draw up commercial balances, so as not to be sad there... Exodus Rabbah 22.) Therefore, what good is wine there, which only serves to forget in sadness? Kol Yaakov.
—o—
A Hasid who was a drinker was asked: Should a Jew like you drink so much?
"I want to drown my troubles," he answers.
"Well? Have you drowned them?"
"No. The misfortune is that the more I drown them — the better they learn to swim..." From the mouth of the people.
—o—
c) "The camel, for it chews the cud" (11:4)
The camel has one sign of purity — it chews the cud — and one sign of impurity: it does not part the hoof. Yet in its prohibition it is precisely the sign of purity, the cud, that is stressed, because with its sign of purity it is all the more dangerous... "And this points to all those whose inside is not like their outside, the hypocrites who present themselves as upright [?] — and they are without doubt worse than utter villains"... Kli Yakar.
—o—
The Rebbe Reb Bunem used to say:
Do not think that Esau looked like a gentile. He went about in a white silk caftan (like the rebbes of old) and said Torah at the third Sabbath meal... The Midrash says that in the time to come Esau will seat himself at the top, and only God will recognise him and throw him out. And if even in the World of Truth Esau will manage to disguise himself so, how much more so in this World of Falsehood... Siach Sarfei Kodesh.
—o—
d) "Whatsoever parteth the hoof" (ibid., 3)
The "trifles" that a man tramples with his heels — that which among people is not considered much of a sin — precisely the keeping of these very "trifles" is a sign of purity. Noam Elimelech.
—o—
e) "And the swine" (ibid., 7)
A miser is called a swine, because he does indeed "part the hoof": go collecting donations he will — he does not spare his feet to take from others; but "it cheweth not the cud [gerah]" — from his own pocket he will not take out a single grosz... Welts-Hershel.
—o—
A "Yahudi" [a German Jew] comes to a German rabbiner to ask for a penance for a piece of pork he ate on purpose [?]. The rabbiner tells him to recite a chapter of Psalms after prayers.
Next to the Yahudi sat a Polish Jew who was reciting Psalms fluently like water, one chapter after another. The Yahudi wonders:
"Can a Jew like that already have gobbled so much pork?..."
—o—
f) "Whatsoever hath fins and scales" (ibid., 9)
Jews are likened to fish, over which the evil eye has no power, and whose blood is also permitted. But fish are the only creatures in which the big ones swallow the small ones... Olelot Efraim.
—o—
g) "Of the fowl" (ibid., 13)
Rabbi Yehoshuale of Dzików, who was a very shrewd man and a sayer of witticisms, used to say:
How is it that certain rebbes, who make themselves out to be fasters and eat nothing, shout so loudly at prayer and say Torah loudly? Where do they get the strength?
Only: "a bird of the air shall carry the voice".
The fowl they eat between themselves and Heaven, when nobody sees — that is what carries the voice so loud and so far...
—o—
h) "And every earthen vessel" (ibid., 33)
An earthen vessel becomes impure only from the inside. The outer side may be unclean, and it is not impure. The main thing is the innermost. And man is, after all, likened to an earthen vessel...
Rabbi Mendele of Kotzk.
—o—
Haftarah of Parashat HaChodesh.
h) "And when the prince entereth... shall go out by the way of the south gate" (Ezekiel 46 [printed: 48])
North is symbolic of money, south of wisdom. Therefore the way of a prince must go only through the south...
Tiferet Yehonatan.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: The Fate of This Year's Kehilla Passover Campaign Depends on the Kehilla-Tax Payers

[Head of the local page; Będzin — kehilla and Passover relief.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 24 Adar 5692 — piątek 1 kwietnia 1932 [Friday, 1 April 1932].)
Będzin
The fate of this year's Passover campaign by the kehilla depends on the "etat" (kehilla tax) payers.
The forthcoming Passover campaign by the kehilla is turning out this year to be much harder than in all previous years, and there is a danger that the great masses who benefit from the "kimcha" [Passover flour, kimcha de-Pischa] campaign will remain without help, and the Jewish soldiers and prisoners — without kosher food for the holiday. In this connection the kehilla board has issued an appeal to all "etat" payers to pay the "etat" for the year 1932. If not — the appeal says — the "etat" lists will be sent to the magistrate [city hall], in order to collect the "etat" by compulsory means.
A Meritorious Deed by the Presidium of the Board and Council of the Credit Bank

[Będzin — economy and trade; the Credit Bank.]
At the time we reported that, in connection with the fact that, as at all banks, the deposits are gradually being withdrawn from the Credit Bank, the presidium of the board and council — Messrs. Jakub Gutman and L. Rubinlicht (of the board) and Messrs. Ch. Szejn and Izaak Szpigelman (of the supervisory council) — strengthened the bank with a larger sum in order to maintain the money reserve.
As we are informed, this week the same gentlemen repeated the fine deed and again financed the Credit Bank with a considerable sum, so that the bank can continue to fulfil its tasks towards the members.
The deed is worth welcoming, but the merchants' situation would be much better and healthier if a united, solid bank were created, which would be able to ease the present critical situation of the merchants.
A Lecture on the Besht, of Blessed Memory

[Będzin — culture; "Mizrachi".]
On Saturday night, at the premises of "Mizrachi", Dr. A. Gottesdiener will give a lecture on the life and thought of R' Israel Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, the creator of Hasidism. The proceeds are designated for "Keren Aliyah".
To the "Merchants' Association"

[Będzin — trade; card games in the street.]
From a larger group of merchants at the Old Market we have received a letter addressed to the "Merchants' Association". In the letter the merchants complain about the sad phenomenon that from day to day the number of customers who come to Zagłębie from Upper Silesia is getting smaller. This is explained by the fact that among the majority of customers from Upper Silesia the opinion has taken root that in Będzin they are cheated and swindled. As if this were not enough, the card games have again appeared on Czeladzka Street, of which many naive people have been victims. These methods strike fear into the customers, and they indeed avoid coming to Będzin.
The merchants therefore turn, through the mediation of the newspaper, to the "Merchants' Association", which should intervene with the proper authority so that the harmful games in the streets are no longer tolerated.
Taxes in the Month of April

[Taxes — payment calendar, April 1932.]
In the course of the month of April of this year the first instalment of the state land tax for 1932 must be paid.
By the 15th of April — turnover tax from commercial patents [trade licences] of the 1st and 2nd category, and from the 1st to the 5th category for those who keep regular commercial books. By the same deadline — the 1st instalment of the industrial ryczałt [lump-sum] tax for the year 1932[?].
By the 1st of May of this year — income tax in the amount of the sum stated in the declaration (zeznanie) for the year 1931.
By the 7th of April of this year — income tax together with the crisis surcharge on pensions and emerituras. Besides this, the postponed, prolonged and instalment-divided payments whose deadlines fall in April must also be paid, as well as the taxes for which the taxpayers have received assessment orders (nakazy) with a payment deadline in April of this year.
A Soldier — a Brawler

[Będzin — crime; Ksawera.]
On Monday a drunken soldier provoked brawls in Ksawera [a district of Będzin]. He waged his fight with his bayonet. He tried to resist the police who came to arrest him. Only the gendarmerie, which was called in, calmed the fighter down and "quartered" him in custody.
A Daring Bandit Attack

[Będzin — crime; armed robbery.]
On Thursday evening[?] 2 armed bandits entered the flat of Majer Koner on Okrzei Street and robbed 1[—]0 zł. in cash and various goods. After carrying out the robbery, the bandits bound the mouth of Koner's daughter, and Mrs. Koner they locked in a wardrobe. When the bandits had gone out, Miss Koner managed to free herself and also her mother.
Relief Campaign for the Unemployed Extended

[Będzin — unemployment relief.]
At the last meeting of the district committee it was resolved to extend the campaign to support the unemployed. At the same time it was resolved to turn to the local committees asking them to continue the collections for this purpose.
“A Gentile Goes into a Tavern…”

[Zagórze — crime.]
On Monday, the second day of “their holiday” [Easter], drunkards attacked Władysław Madej, a resident of Zagórze, beating him with a stick. Madej then pulled out his revolver and fired several times at the attackers. One of the drunkards was shot dead. The second is seriously wounded.
The Passover Campaign of “Beit Lechem” Is Proceeding Successfully

[Będzin — charity; Passover.]
The fundraising for the Passover campaign of “Beit Lechem” has met with warmth among the Jewish population. The collectors are gladly received, and everyone who has any means at all does not refuse [to give] to the campaign, which is intended to provide food for respectable [needy] families during the Passover days.
Investigation into the Origin of Capital Abolished

[Taxes — Finance Ministry circular.]
The Ministry of Finance has sent out a very important circular to all subordinate tax bodies, concerning the investigation into the origin of capital, that is, the requirement to prove where the taxpayer obtained his capital. The Ministry of Finance instructs the tax offices not to apply the said investigation in practice.
The said regulation was issued because the tax offices, when investigating the origin of invested capital and of real estate — houses, mortgages, building works, bank operations, etc. — demanded from taxpayers explanations about these transactions, and very often recognised the full sums of the transactions as income, on which he was also taxed.
Under the regulation the tax offices no longer have the right to demand that taxpayers prove where they took the money to buy houses, open businesses, etc.
A Premiere of the Będzin “Muze”

[Będzin — theatre.]
Next week the “Muze”, known for its production of “At Night in the Old Market”, will stage “In the Synagogue Porch, in Chains” (“In polish oyf der keyt”) by I. L. Peretz, which has so far not yet been performed in Poland.
In connection with the gigantic production, intensive rehearsals take place daily. The direction is in the hands of Mr.[?] Nachum Melnik.
Artistic dances were rehearsed by the actress Dvora Rozenblum.
The sets were specially designed and painted by the well-known artist-painter Mr. Cygler.
Sosnowiec — The Kimcha [de-Pischa] Campaign Is Under Way

[Sosnowiec — kehilla; Passover flour relief.]
This week the “kimcha” campaign began, which is carried out every year by the kehilla leadership. It is to be hoped that despite the severe crisis everyone will understand that the number of the needy has grown this year, and will help so that the kimcha campaign may have the proper success.
Tragic Death of Two Children

[Sosnowiec, Czeladź — accidents.]
On Sunday afternoon the 11-year-old Adek and the 8-year-old Ślęzak[?] Adek were sliding on the “glinkes” [flooded clay pits] on Barbara Street.
When the children were in the middle of their slide the ice broke and the children went down under the ice. Fortunately a chance passer-by, Mr. Muszyński, saw it; he hurried to the rescue and managed to drag the girl out of the water, whereas the boy was found dead a few hours later.
On the same day a second tragic case occurred in Czeladź. In the courtyard of house[?] Elektralna[?] 1 a 2-year-old child, who was playing without supervision, fell into a cesspit, where it suffocated.
Both facts should be a lesson not to leave children without supervision.
The Constitution of the Board of the “Ahavat Hesed” Fund

[Sosnowiec — relief institutions, free-loan fund.]
On Sunday the constituent meeting of the board of the “Ahavat Hesed” fund took place at the home of Mr. Rzeżak [?], with the participation of the whole board. Elected as chairman was Mr. Chaim Unger; as business manager — Mr. Josef Jakubowicz; as first vice-chairman — Mr. J. Weintrefer [?]; as second vice-chairman — Mr. J. D. Rzeżak [?]; as secretary — Mr. M.H. [?] Szmul Rozengust [?]; treasurer — Mr. K. M. Melc. Also co-opted to the board were Messrs. Pradelski and Judel Fajman.
At the same meeting the following persons declared that they would lend the following sums until after Passover: M. Ferens, S. Grinbaum, J. Rozenfeld, A. S. Jaskerowicz, K. M. Melc — 100 zł. each; M. Waks, H. Notiszarger [?], J. Weintrefas [?], A. Nirenberg, J. Nirenberg, B. Pradelski — 50 zł. each; M. S. Rozengast [?], H. Tabiasz — 25 zł. each.
In general the new board is carrying on intensive activity. Every day new members enrol. Thanks to which the fund will be able to ease their situation by giving them loans.
A Festive Siyum ha-Sefer in Old Sosnowiec

[Old Sosnowiec (Stary Sosnowiec) — religious life.]
On Monday a siyum ha-sefer [celebration of the completion of a Torah scroll] was held in the synagogue in Old Sosnowiec in an impressive manner. Rabbi Hager took part in the celebration and delivered a sermon rich in content. Later a fine [?] festive meal took place at the home of M. Wilbergik [?].
Income-Tax Declarations

[Taxes.]
By 1 May of this year all who hold trade patents (licences) of the 2nd and 3rd category and labour patents up to the 5th category must submit zeznania [declarations] of the income they had in the year 1931.
According to the law, one who holds a trade patent of the 4th category and a labour patent of the 8th category need not submit any declaration of income. He is obliged to do so only when he receives a summons from the tax office.
—o—
Children of Mine Workers in Warsaw
[Zagłębie — welfare, children.]
Last week a group of 75 children from unemployed families in Zagłębie was sent to Warsaw. The children were distributed among families and children's institutions.
—o—
Sad Result of a Wild Ride
[Czeladź–Sosnowiec — accident.]
The local resident Hszysla [?], owner of a motorcycle, invited his acquaintance Helena [?] Morawna [?] for an outing in honour of the holiday. On the road from Czeladź to Sosnowiec the motorcycle ran into a tree; the impact was very strong. Both were thrown onto the pavement and were seriously injured.
Instead of Counterfeit Money — Yeast

[Milowice — police, smuggling.]
In the home of a certain resident of Milowice the police made a search, looking for counterfeit coins. Instead of counterfeit money, 15 kilos of smuggled yeast were found.
—o—
Recruitment Campaign of the Revisionists
[Zionism — Revisionists.]
In connection with the move [?] into the new premises the Revisionists have proclaimed a recruitment campaign. In the bulletin issued by them it is said that only one who recognises the Herzl programme may belong to the Revisionist organisation.
The programme of local activity lists, among other things: a people's university, intensified work for the funds Keren Kayemet, Keren Hayesod, Keren Tel-Hai, creating retraining cooperatives, spreading Tozeret ha-Aretz [produce of the Land of Israel], propaganda for the Betar movement, a library, a reading room, etc.
Preparations are already being made for the conference of the Revisionists of the Kielce voivodeship, which will take place in Sosnowiec during Hol ha-Moed Passover.
—o—
Grodziec
[Grodziec — Zionism, youth.]
A week ago a “Gordonia” organisation was founded here, which is developing very nicely. Great disturbances [have come] from a certain fanatical group, which is waging a “holy war” against us; taking part in the “war of mitzvah” especially are Messrs. Berkowicz and Zysman, who by no means want to allow the organising of the Zionist youth. But we will overcome the disturbances and continue [?] our work.
R-n.
Who will be able to file an appeal concerning the ryczałt turnover?

[Taxes — merchants.] The tax offices have already drawn up the lists of the merchants to whom the "ryczałt turnover" [lump-sum turnover tax] will be applied. They have now begun sending out the payment orders [nakazy płatnicze], which will state how much each merchant must pay in each quarter of the two years 1932 and 1933.
Merchants who do not receive a ryczałt order in the course of the next[?] few days must take the trouble to find out for themselves at their tax office [urząd]. One should simply go into the office and find out why no order for the ryczałt tax was sent: whether this is by chance, because they have not yet managed to send it to everyone, or whether it is by mistake, or even because one was not entered in the list of ryczałt payers.
It goes without saying that only those merchants who in the years 1928, 1929 and 1930 had an assessed turnover of less than 35,000 zł need go to the office to find this out.
Merchants who learn at the office that they were not included in the ryczałt list will be able to file appeals if they themselves consider that they have thereby been wronged, i.e. that in their opinion they should indeed pay the turnover tax [obrotowy] according to the ryczałt.
Appeals may also be filed by merchants who consider that they were assessed a higher ryczałt than, in their opinion, is due.
———
There are very, very many merchants who will have to file appeals, because for various reasons they will not be entered in the ryczałt list.
According to the law, the ryczałt turnover tax must be applied to merchants who in the years 1928, 1929 and 1930 had an average turnover of not less than 35.000 zł.
If the merchant did not trade in the year 1928, that is also fine — the average turnover is then calculated from the two years 1989 [sic, for 1929] and 1930.
—o—
[Będzin — court.] 9 months' prison for stealing three hens.
Tomasz Tyrek, an unemployed man, having no money to buy cinema tickets for himself and his fiancée, stole three hens from Mr. Ch. Szwarcberg. This week Tyrek was sentenced by the Będzin court to 9 months' prison.
—o—
[Ząbkowice — fire.] A fire in a cinema.
At the People's House in Ząbkowice a fire broke out on Monday in the film projection booth. The firemen on duty put out the fire. Part[?] of the films was burnt.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — culture.] Great success of Miriam Orleska in Sosnowiec.
On Monday evening, in the premises of the Revisionist organization in Sosnowiec, a recitation evening was held, performed by the well-known artist Miriam Orleska. The impression was tremendous. After every number the artist was showered with stormy applause.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — memorial.] A memorial for R' Yitzchak Eizik Wolfson of blessed memory.
In connection with the first yahrzeit of R' Yitzchak Eizik Wolfson, may he rest in Eden, a memorial will be held next Thursday evening in the building of the Sosnowiec "Talmud Torah".
—o—
[Sosnowiec — Betar.] Betar instructors' course.
In recent days an instructors' course in physical education was opened in Sosnowiec, in the Betar premises, under the direction of a graduate of the Betar instructors' school, Mr. Mandelbaum.
At the festive opening Mr. Klarman lectured on the importance of physical education. Messrs. Triger and Jasny also spoke.
The course will last about 2 months. During this time various lectures will be held, among others also on hygiene. The last lectures will be given by doctors.
—o—
[Sosnowiec — politics.] A great "people's trial of Revisionism"
will be held next Sunday evening in Sosnowiec in the "Angielski hall", with the participation of members of Poale Zion (Ts. S.): editor L. Szpizman, M. Hampel, M. L. Kozłowski (Będzin), M. Trefer (Dąbrowa), L. Lenczner and A. Kleinberg (Sosnowiec).
—o—
[Będzin — WIZO.] Tuesday — opening of the WIZO library.
Next Tuesday, the 5th of this month [5 April 1932], the library will be opened in the premises of the Będzin "WIZO", Kołłątaja 33. The library contains a large number of books in Hebrew, Yiddish, Polish, German and law, from the old and the new literature. Books will be lent from the library, which will be open on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, also to non-members.
—o—
[Zagłębie — unemployment.] The "Jowisz" coal mine is to be closed.
Another 1.500 unemployed.
All the workers of the "Jowisz" coal mine received notice on Wednesday that as of the 15th of this month [15 April] they are dismissed from work. The mine is to be closed down entirely.
—o—
[Gdynia — antisemitism.] Antisemitic agitation in Gdynia.
Our Gdynia correspondent, Mr. L. Makowski, writes to us: the "Gdynia newspaper" is conducting a vehement antisemitic campaign. The paper, which constantly brings articles under the title "Zaraza żydowska w Gdyni" ["The Jewish plague in Gdynia"], appeals ceaselessly to the population of Gdynia already "to drive out all the Jews while there is still time".
The anger of the paper's editors stems from the fact that a local[?] resident, a certain Mr. Słomnicki, held a circumcision. Well, how can one tolerate Jews being fruitful and multiplying even in Gdynia — so pitch and brimstone are indeed poured upon the Jews of Gdynia. The articles appear in huge ("Kiddush Levana") letters, such as "Historyczny dzień w Gdyni" ["A historic day in Gdynia"], "Pierwszy Żyd urodzony[?] w Gdyni" ["The first Jew born in Gdynia"], etc.
The paper also turns to the police, asking it to keep an eye on the "Judeo-communists"[?] who come to Gdynia to build synagogues and ritual baths...
—o—
[Zagłębie — labour.] Conference at the labour inspector's on new reductions.
Under the chairmanship of the labour inspector in Sosnowiec a conference was held with the participation of representatives of a number of coal mines in Zagłębie.
At the conference the question of new reductions [lay-offs], which are imminent, was considered, as well as the fact that some of the mines are threatened with being closed down entirely.
The inspector declared that he would intervene in the matter in order to find a way out, so that there would be no further reductions.

[Dąbrowa — kehilla.] Yesterday the Jewish gmina [community] received the new kehilla budget, approved by the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
The following changes were made in the budget:
All subventions were struck out. The subsidy for the "Talmud Torah" was reduced to 1.000 zł. (the preliminary figure had been 3,000 zł.
The subsidy for poor emigrants to Palestine remained untouched...
—o—
Stormy demonstration at the "Zawiercie" factory.
[Zawiercie — labour.] Because wages had not been paid on time, the workers of the "Zawiercie" factory organised a demonstration, which took a stormy course. A larger police detachment dispersed the demonstrators.
—o—
Today, Friday — judgement day for the Dąbrowa budget.
[Dąbrowa — municipality.] The Dąbrowa [Górnicza] budget for 1932/33 is being considered today, Friday, at the Kielce voivodeship office.
To defend the budget, the president [mayor] Dr. Madeyski[?], the chairman of the city council Dr. Pitowarc[?] and the head (kierownik) of the finance department Mr. Szykarski travelled there.
—o—
Festive Trumpeldor academy in Sosnowiec.
[Sosnowiec — Zionism.] Very festive was the Trumpeldor academy [memorial evening] held last Sunday by the Revisionists in their premises. The whole hall was draped in blue-and-white and black crêpe. By Trumpeldor's portrait a grave [symbolic tomb] was set up with artistic taste. After the young, talented singer Comrade Szymon Płatkiewicz sang an "El Male Rachamim" and the Betar choir sang "Tel Chai", Mr. Klarman opens the academy amid deathly silence. The speaker dwells on the significance of the day and talks about the substance of the pride that Trumpeldor instilled in the Jewish people. The speaker also illuminates the substance of the "Chalutz" type that Trumpeldor created and that is realised by Betar, which is raised in his spirit.
Mr. Lewi Ingster dwells on the importance of a legal self-defence in Eretz Israel. — He therefore considers the Keren "Tel-Chai" fund a necessity and calls on the youth to follow Trumpeldor's example. Dr. A. Gotesdiner gives a survey of the heroic deeds of Jewish heroes and speaks of the surging spirit which has fallen[?]. Heroism has always played a role in conquering Eretz Israel. He holds that Betar must also not forget the Jewish book. In closing Mr. Klarman lectures on the ideology of Betar, explaining that among Betar's 3 hachsharot [trainings] the spiritual hachshara also has its place. With the singing of "Hatikvah" and in an elevated mood the first part of the academy is closed.
The second part was filled by the artist Miriam Orleska, who recited Bialik, Peretz, Asch, Papiernikov, Kulbak and others. The artist was rewarded with thunderous applause.
A Stain Must Be Removed.

(Boxed sub-heading:) Trade in the Old Market and the "Ślązacy" [Silesians from Upper Silesia].
In the previous issue of our paper we reported in a short notice the letter which Będzin merchants of the Old Market sent us with the request to turn to the "Merchants' Association" (Sokhrim-Fareyn), so that it should react to the shameful deeds of all sorts of individuals who bring harm to honest trade; and it is characteristic that things have reached the point where inhabitants of neighbouring Upper Silesia are afraid to come to Będzin to make their purchases, because here they get cheated.
Yes, this is a vexing, a painful truth. But one must reckon with it as [—] a truth; a pure truth it is, and that ought to be enough for the Będzin merchant community to react to the dangerous phenomenon, which has taken on such a character that it further clouds the already [?] sad economic situation.
Had people here properly understood our economic interests — our, if one may so express it, economic pains and aches and all the complications caused by the gravity of the times and by the dangerous situation in which we find ourselves; had we understood all this, had people here at least been willing to understand it — the matter would not have taken on this character, which brings so much harm into everyday economic life. Unfortunately it is not considered important even to want to put the question on the agenda [?], which confirms that here people do not want to understand at all that this matter must be dealt with just as one must deal, let us say, with the question of where to draw a livelihood [?]; and because people here do not want to deal with all these "side issues", things have come to the present harm, that "Ślązacy" are afraid to come to Będzin because they are cheated here.
We know that this is exaggerated; we know that merchants do not want to conduct their business under the motto [?] of swindling, from which one is to pay [?] because the customer does not give the proper price; but it is still not enough that this suffices in order not to let these stains — with which Będzin would be crowned — fall on oneself. One must surely try to repel the bullets aimed at harming the merchant community as such. The honest merchant can by no means console himself [?] that, as long as he is honest, it does not concern him that his neighbour behaves otherwise, and that someone who bears no responsibility towards anyone cheats the customer from head to toe, or that a "Ślązak" is lured into a corner and talked into "bargains", or that the money with which he came to make all kinds of purchases is pulled out of him — be it with the help of cards.
Of course these are not merchants; these are shady persons who hang around those who want to buy and make them miserable. These are charlatans, scum, individuals who must be removed; and as long as the merchants take no interest in these harmful elements, it is no wonder that the stains also fall on their heads, and so their economic basis is undermined as a matter of course. Had a clear account been rendered of this in good time, things would not have reached a state in which naive people [?] are afraid to come to Będzin to buy goods.
After all, people do not say that some piece of scum swindled the Upper Silesian customer out of his money, whether with the help of cards or with imitation goods; instead they do say that in Będzin one is robbed, that in Będzin one is fleeced and defrauded. So it is addressed to the merchant community of Będzin as a whole, and that should not have been allowed, it should not have been brought to that. For such deeds the swindlers ("combinators") ought to have been handed over to the police, and let them deal with the harmful elements according to their deserts.
The fact that such deeds are tolerated, that they are looked upon with indifference, burdens [?] the Będzin merchant community, and people say that the merchant as a rule cheats and causes an unbearable situation. That is precisely why Będzin must protect its brand, why the Będzin merchant must guard his prestige. In this case the individual plays no role; the merchant is taken as a collective, as one uniform whole, as one entity. Individuals then [?] do not come into consideration; however honest and decent they may be, they are not noticed at all.
Of course, the Old Market committed a crime against itself [?] when they watched all this and kept silent. Had they not done so, it would not have come to this. But as the Jewish proverb says: better late than never. It is good that they have now turned to the "Merchants' Association" for help, good that they demand today to be protected from the dangerous disease; let the "Merchants' Association" now set about reacting to the morbid phenomenon.
It must not be allowed that the opinion should take root about Będzin that here the "Ślązacy" are cheated, both with the help of cards and with the help of all kinds of schemes or forgeries.
The "Merchants' Association", together with the merchants, must apply every means to uproot the dangerous microbe, which has begun to break, like mice, into every corner and to harm decent and honest commerce.
The merchants themselves must strive to clean the air, which is being polluted around them thanks to the various swindlers and scum who constantly think only of how to earn money the easy way. True, one must be on guard against them; they are found everywhere and anywhere. But here they already rule on a larger scale, so that every means must be adopted to destroy them radically, root and all. Only then can salvation come, for as long as it is known that they rule and are popular, so long will the masses of Upper Silesia be afraid to come to Będzin to buy goods. And the mere thought — being afraid to come to Będzin because one will be cheated — this very thought ought to be a disgrace for mercantile Będzin. It must not be allowed that Jewish Będzin, the merchant town of Zagłębie, should be stained in such a way. Ugliness, stains and parasites we must remove and destroy with all our strength.
Had we not, from the very beginning, turned a blind eye to the phenomenon, it would of course not have come to this shameful degree. But our trouble here is that we tolerate everything as long as it does not stick out. Because of that the Będzin merchant community now has to fight to remove the disease, without which [?] one could easily have managed, and which, with proper conduct, would not have led to Będzin being crowned with such a shameful stain. One must not forget that the antisemites in Upper Silesia will seize on this like a roast delicacy and will operate with this aid.
But it is a lost cause; yesterday cannot be brought back — so let us now do [?] what is within our power. Let no merchant think that this is not his business, that it does not harm him and the question does not interest him at all, because he takes no money from the "Ślązacy". What is at stake here is removing a stain that has indeed fallen on the heads of the Będzin merchants as a whole, and everyone is obliged to do so, both for himself privately and for mercantile Będzin, which plays such a respected role in Zagłębie and in Upper Silesia to this very day.
The "Merchants' Association" must energetically set about, together with the members concerned, the useful work of uprooting; and then, with strong will, the matter can — together with the help of the authorities, should it be needed — be radically solved.
R. Les.
To the Youth Who Want to Go Abroad to Study.

[Notice — Jewish students, academic emigration.] The Central Outgoing Committee (Ausfir-Komitet) of the Union of Organizations of Jewish Students from Poland Studying Abroad informs the youth who want to go abroad to study that the Academic Emigration Bureau, which exists at the Aid Society for Jewish Students from Poland Studying Abroad, handles all matters connected with leaving to study abroad.
The Academic Emigration Bureau is active all year round; it gives information, deals with all matters connected with admission to foreign institutions of higher learning, arranges translations of documents into foreign languages and legalizations at the consulate, issues international academic student cards (C.I.E.) and also arranges academic visas.
The Academic Emigration Bureau, as the only such institution of the Jewish academic youth, enjoys a whole series of discounts in handling all kinds of matters connected with leaving to study, and in this way works to reduce the travel costs abroad.
The A.E.B. possesses rich informational material and is in direct contact with the university authorities and academic centres abroad.
The academic youth is called upon to apply to the A.E.B. before taking any step in connection with going abroad to study, in order to obtain exact information and thereby avoid what are often very great losses.
Written information is given after sending 2 zł. in postage stamps.
In all the above-mentioned matters one should apply to the Academic Emigration Bureau, Warsaw, Elektoralna 8, tel. 307-73.
Heard and Seen.

[Sosnowiec — feuilleton/sketches.] By Ben Amotz.

A Sure Remedy...
The end of the current school year is approaching; the candidates — or rather the female candidates — for the matura are already living through restless days and sleepless nights; they are afraid of the Day of Judgement...
It goes without saying that besides one's own work, the maturas are often "settled" by other means, above all — orientation... But the method used by one of the Hebrew teachers at the Sosnowiec girls' gymnasium is, in our opinion, the "surest" of all the known remedies that are topical at matura-examination time.
The teacher was on an excursion in Kraków with the pupils of the 8th class of the Sosnowiec girls' gymnasium. Among other things the group also visited the grave of the Rema. And standing with the pupils around the grave, the teacher remembered that the time of the Day of Judgement, the time of the matura examinations, is drawing near, and she
— well, guess: what?
— did the same thing all Jews do when they go to the Rema's grave. She wrote kvitlekh [petition notes]... for every pupil. — A separate kvitl with the prayer that "Feigl daughter of Rachel shall, God forbid, not stumble when she stands before the earthly tribunal, before the examination board, and that she come out in peace with a matura with distinction"...
— And I am sure — my informant assures me — that all the pupils of the Jewish girls' gymnasium will receive the best maturas this year...
— A sure remedy...

The "Chazakah" Should Be Changed...
In the whole town he is known as a merchant; he does not run the big businesses, but in the merchant world he does play a role, and he figures as one who lives a decent life...
Always, when he meets me in the street, he tells me with bitterness about various injustices [?] that keep growing in our homely hodgepodge [?]. Fine [?] — he says — let it stay as it was, but one wants to speak one's heart out, it becomes — easier...
The last time we met, the merchant no longer spoke to me as always [—]
were his words, broken off, unclear, as if he had a raised temperature...
On taking leave of me he spoke clearly; it became clear to me that he wishes us to write in the newspaper that this year the Kimcha [de-Pischa, Passover-flour] Commission should change its chazakah [established practice] so far and penetrate more deeply into the real situation of a large part of the merchants, who a year ago were among the first givers, and today...
— here his tongue failed him again, his eyes filled with big tears like diamonds... today should
— "the chazakah be changed...

Perhaps After All?..
The football season has already begun. The first "battle" for the right to get into class "A" has also already been held. Right at the start it nearly came to a real battle between Sosnowiec "Maccabi" and its opponents. There, in Tel Aviv, among thousands of others, the flag of Sosnowiec "Maccabi" is also flying, and here, on the sports ground in Sosnowiec, "Maccabi" itself stands with clenched [?] fists against the better goal-masters, against those who have [—]
And a board member of Sosnowiec "Maccabi" complains to us: How much longer — he asks — will we waste so much time and make so many sacrifices for the brutal sport that is called
— football!
We Maccabeans — he says — have been playing for several years now, and what have we achieved? Morally and physically broken we leave every football match. What do we bring to Jewish society?... And even when one does achieve the title "A" — in what [does it help]?
To tell the truth, we were "afraid" to touch the whole matter; after all, we will be condemned forever as uncultured, as having not the slightest sense for modern art, for the demands of the time... But as Yeger once said: "Perhaps after all"?... Perhaps you, Jewish sports clubs in Zagłębie, will leave the honour of shooting goals to others... and will guard your tasks? The tasks that are marked on the banners of "Maccabi" and "Hakoach"?
Perhaps after all?

And a Meeting Was Held...
The town notables came together to take counsel on finding a [—] in the premises of "Maccabi", but because of the sports season the kitchen must vacate the premises.
And it was decided to do as the [wise men of Chełm] once did
— to hold a meeting.
They considered this way and that, and it was decided that the kitchen should be set up in the building of the "Talmud Torah".
And when the "experts" came back from the T"T and said that in the T"T there is no floor, it was decided
— to hold a meeting...
And it was decided to look for craftsmen who would make the floor free of charge and merchants who would give timber.
And when the "experts" came with the answer that both for the timber and for the work one must pay, it was decided
— to hold a meeting...
The board of "Maccabi" threatens to evict the kitchen; hundreds of poor families will suffer from it, but when one asks the town counsellors: why don't you provide another place? they answer: we did what we could, and
— we held a meeting...
Notes of the Week

[Notes of the Week — abroad and Palestine.] A Jew and an Arab have been found murdered in Jerusalem. Jewish–Arab relations have grown more tense.
—o—
The election campaign in Germany has flared up again. In a number of places there have been bloody incidents between Hitlerites [Nazis] and Hindenburg's supporters.
—o—
In Galicia several rivers have overflowed. Dozens of villages have been evacuated.
—o—
A fire broke out in the White Cross hospital in Moscow. Many people were burned.
—o—
For failing to appear as a witness at a trial, Asher Kohn has been sentenced to 3 months' arrest.
—o—
Wild Deeds by Recruits on the Train to Częstochowa.
[Poland — antisemitism.] On Tuesday in the daytime a band of recruits travelling from Zawiercie to Częstochowa went on a hooligan rampage[?] against the Jewish passengers travelling on the train.
The hooligans beat the Jewish passengers, snatched[?] their hats off them, and threatened them with death with knives in their hands.
Among the passengers was also Mr. Alver[?] [perhaps Alter] Feldman of Będzin. The recruits wanted to slaughter him. He was rescued from danger by the Christian passengers who were in the same carriage. On arriving in Częstochowa, Feldman intervened with the policeman on duty at the station, who took three of the hooligans to the police station, where they received the appropriate punishment.
—o—
Pension Supplement of the Czeladź Commissioner Not Approved.
[Czeladź — municipality.] The commissioners' council[?] in Czeladź raised the commissioner's pension by 200 zł. a month. The supplement was not approved by the voivodeship.
—o—
Clothing Campaign of the Dąbrowa "Malbish Arumim" for Passover.
[Dąbrowa — charity.] The board of "Malbish Arumim" [Clothing the Naked] in Dąbrowa has received many requests from respectable people asking for holiday clothes for themselves and their children. Despite the institution's bad financial situation, the board has decided not to refuse the requests and to meet their demands as far as possible.
It is therefore a sacred duty of the Jewish public in Dąbrowa not to make light of the institution's work and to come to the board's aid at every call, so that it may be able to fulfil its tasks.
—o—
A Kimcha [de-Pischa] Committee Formed in Czeladź.
[Czeladź — Passover relief.] Year in, year out, ma'ot chitim [Passover flour money] was collected here too, as in all Jewish communities, but from this collection the greater part of the Jewish population of Czeladź got barely enough for maror and charoset...
This year a special kimcha committee of householders has been elected, who are responsible for seeing that the money collected is distributed properly.
The Jewish public of Czeladź need only respond warmly to the kimcha campaign and make it possible for the needy to be supported.
—o—
Woman Murdered over a Robbery of 90 zł.
[Będzin district — murder.] In the village of Szjemian [Siemonia?], Będzin powiat, Mrs. Fajer[?] was found murdered not far from her home. In the hands of the murdered woman were found shreds of her clothing — proof that she resisted the bandits with her last strength.
The investigation established that the woman, who had been visiting her husband, who works in Upper Silesia, had 90 zł. on her, which she had received from her husband.
—o—
Break-in at the Olkusz Town Court.
[Olkusz — crime.] In the night from Thursday to Friday the deposit room[?] of the town court in Olkusz was broken into. The thieves, looking for money, destroyed various files and took 2 counterfeit zlotys.
—o—
Tragedy of a Couple in Love in Bobrowniki.
[Bobrowniki — suicide.] In Bobrowniki this week a bloody tragedy took place on romantic grounds.
The neighbours of the shoemaker Gajewski heard loud groans from Gajewski's room. When the door of Gajewski's room was broken open, they saw that Gajewski and his sweetheart had committed suicide by poisoning themselves with hydrochloric acid.
The reason for the double suicide is that the sweetheart's parents would not allow the match with the shoemaker.
—o—
People of Czeladź, "Kasher [for Passover] in Good Time! A Sanitary Commission Is Coming to You.
[Czeladź — sanitation.] In the coming days a special sanitary commission will carry out a general inspection in Czeladź. It is in the general interest to keep the sanitary condition in the best order.
—o—
The Delegate of "Yachin" in Zagłębie.
[Zagłębie — Zionism and settlement.] After the delegate of "Yachin", Mr. Y. D. Beit-Halevi, carried out the campaign of recruiting members for the colony that "Yachin" is organising on land which the National Fund [Keren Kayemet] has designated for this purpose, in a number of towns in Poland, he has now, shortly before his departure for Eretz Israel, come to Zagłębie.
The Jewish middle class will surely make use of the opportunity and take an interest in the favourable opportunity to secure an existence in Eretz Israel by means that are not difficult.
The delegate will stay several days in Będzin; afterwards he will visit Sosnowiec and Katowice.
—o—
A Cycle of Lectures by Dr. Meladiste at the Betar Instructors' Course.
[Sosnowiec — Betar.] Among other lectures being given at the Betar instructors' course in Sosnowiec, Dr. Meladista [Melodysta?] is also giving a cycle of lectures on hygiene and physical education. These instructive lectures are given in a very popular and attractive form.
—o—
A Farewell Evening of Miriam Orleska.
[Będzin — culture and theatre.] This Friday evening the last farewell word-concert of the beloved artist of the Vilna Troupe, Miriam Orleska, is being held[?] at the Będzin "Kultur-Lige".
Miriam Orleska [printed "Ablesk"], who is already well known to local theatregoers from her brilliant roles in the rising years of the "Vilner", has recently begun her artistic triumphal march with the power of the bare word alone. The carefully assembled reading material (mostly of social content), performed before the audience with piano accompaniment, makes an unforgettable impression on the listener and evokes the thought: must one really have the whole clatter of strange, incomprehensible sets, colourful costumes, neck-and-nape-breaking by the actors, in order to call forth emotions in the spectator? Are make-up and blinding lights really needed to stir our feelings and intellect, so that we feel and grasp[?] everything as simply and plainly as Orleska simply and plainly sits at the table, her head propped on her hand, and recites? And perhaps this is to be a turning point and a new way of artistic self-expression for the actress and of artistic enjoyment for the listener? Who knows!...
A small part of the local public already knows Orleska's appearances in the small premises of "WIZO"; tonight all of us will have the opportunity to hear her once more and to bid her farewell.
—o—
Visit of the Prosecutor of the Warsaw Court of Appeal.
[Zagłębie — courts.] This week the prosecutor of the Warsaw Court of Appeal, Mr. Rudnicki, visited Zagłębie and acquainted himself with the prisons in Zagłębie.
—o—
Abuses at the Post Office in Zawiercie.
[Zawiercie — crime.] At the Zawiercie post office abuses committed by a postman have been discovered. The postman kept for himself the money for bills of exchange collected through the post. In addition, he forged various postal documents.
What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — chronicle.]
The deeds of the press blackmailers have been uncovered.
For many months a newspaper called "Śląski Głos Publiczny" appeared in Katowice. The "editors" of this blackmail rag extorted dozens of people from Upper Silesia and from Zagłębie as well. Their work consisted of this: the firms or persons from whom the "editors" could not squeeze money were smeared and reviled in the paper in the lowest manner.
This week "the bomb burst": the authorities in Katowice finally took an interest in the gang, and at the request of the investigating office the "editors" and their helpers, such as K. Perlsztajn, Simcha Fiszer, Tadeusz Tenenbaum-Jadłowski and Tarnowski, were arrested.
The investigation so far has revealed that the blackmailers squeezed 15 thousand złoty out of Dr. Wilimowski, 2,500 zł. out of the mayor of Żuriec [?], 5 thousand zł. out of the restaurant "Lokana" [?] in Sosnowiec, 500 zł. out of Jerzy [?] Fürstenberg, 500 zł. out of the Katowice merchant Kingcligner [?], and others.
Their representative in Zagłębie was a certain Czekalski, who managed to disappear.
—o—
The wage struggle in the zinc industry.
The struggle over wages in the zinc industry is sharpening anew. Last Tuesday the managements of the zinc works in Upper Silesia notified all workers that work in the industry will continue only until the 20th of this month. But if the workers agree to the 12 per cent reduction in wages, the notice will be withdrawn; if not, all zinc works will be shut down on the 20th of this month and 10 thousand workers will be left without work.
The announcement caused unheard-of agitation among the workers.
—o—
A woman's revenge.
On Monday the owner of the "Hela" confectionery in Katowice, on Kościuszko Street, was attacked by his own wife, who out of revenge threw pepper in his eyes. A group of "supporters" also came to the woman's aid and afterwards wrecked the premises of the confectionery.
—o—
Theft at the post office in Königshütte.
At the post office in Königshütte (Królewska Huta) a larger sum — 400 zł. — was stolen from a man who had come to pay it in. The police, who were called, arrested a certain Chaim Kimelfeld [?], a resident of Łódź, who is suspected of the theft.
—o—
"Alkusz" is closing.
The management of the "Alkusz" aluminium factory has informed the labour inspector that, owing to a lack of orders, the factory will be closed until the 9th of May this year.
As a result 1,500 workers lose their jobs.
—o—
Meeting of the Dąbrowa town council.
This Saturday night, after the Sabbath, a plenary meeting of the town council will take place in Dąbrowa.
On the agenda — various economic questions.
Sport

[Sport — football and table tennis in Zagłębie.]
For the Class "A" championship
On Sunday a series of football matches for the Class "A" championship took place on the sports grounds of Zagłębie. The results are as follows:
Policyjny [?] K.S. — "Hakoah" [printed "Hapach"] 1:3.
The match took place on the ground of "Unia" in Sosnowiec. In the first half both clubs were on the same level. In the second half the opponent had the upper hand.
Zagłębianka — Brygita [?] 1:2
Zagłębie — Makabi 2:4
The course of the match, which took place at the municipal stadium in Dąbrowa, was interesting. "Makabi", which turned out with several fresh players and a capable [?] goalkeeper, had the upper hand in the first half. In the second half "Zagłębie" takes over the initiative and holds on to the 2:4 victory in favour of "Zagłębie".
C.K.S. — "Ruch" 0:4.
"Unia" — "Sarmacja" 1:2.
—o—
Victory of the ping-pong section.
On Sunday a championship of the ping-pong section took place in Sosnowiec, at the premises of "Makabi".
The match gave unexpected results, and beat the ping-pong champion of Zagłębie.
