Heard and Seen.

[Będzin — weekly feuilleton.] By Ben Amotz.

Be a little lenient...
...One goes out, another comes in — from day to day the number of merchants who come into the editorial office to pour out their bitter hearts over the countless wrongs and chicaneries committed[?] against the merchant class keeps growing.
To the hard torments of the past — they say — a new trouble has been added, with a brand-new name
— „the notary's trouble“ [rejent, Polish for notary]...
In the merchant world it was regarded as a great concession that one could redeem a bill of exchange at the notary after the third day from its due date. Out of the „three days of darkness“ the merchant still had the opportunity to keep his prestige, and more than once it actually happened that when, during the three days, things became a little „brighter“, many „evil thoughts“ melted away, and
— honour was saved...
But for some weeks now the Będzin notary, the very same one [misprinted „velber“ for „zelber“] who was received with so much affection, has reconsidered and acts according to the „Shulchan Aruch“...
— Well, what do you want from us; we are not going to be against the person[?] who upholds the law...
— Yes, yes, we know and understand that this is how it must be. But even in the strictest, harshest law one can still find a dispensation to be lenient, and especially in the present bitter time, when the merchant class is waging a struggle of life and death — free breathing is so very necessary...
— Write about it — they beg — perhaps the notary will be a little lenient, and not be so punctilious according to the laws of the „Shulchan Aruch“...
— Be a little lenient...
—o—
„The crisis has weakened“...
It is possible that for many readers the „good tidings“ that „the crisis has weakened“ will come as a surprise, but make no mistake: the crisis in general grows stronger and stronger; only in one position of our kehilla muddle[?] has the crisis weakened. — The crisis
— in the Będzin synagogue...
As is known, the „crisis“ burst in there when the „Torah-loyal“ began to fortify Jewishness in the town... Over time the worshippers in the synagogue went through various epochs. Over time there „ruled“ the „36 Righteous“, the „4th vadn“[?] and above all — 32 dozors [synagogue board members, Polish dozór]...
— The result? — Lawlessness, demoralisation to the highest degree, until the „people“ itself distanced itself from the guardians up to now and took power into its own hands.
— The improvement?
— Decency is gradually being restored. True, the task is a hard one; one cannot uproot the bad all at once; it is also necessary that those on duty at the bimah should have a „far-sighted look“, so that the buzzing during prayers should also stop...
The „amud crisis“ [the squabble over who leads the prayers] has also been removed; one no longer hears the shouts of „nu, nu“ before the prayers, but a prepared, pleasant prayer leader takes his place, and behind him — a choir, still a crude one, not even trained, but he satisfies; in a pinch [misprinted „harchek“ for „hadechak“] such a choir is as a remedy for the wound...
— If only it gets no worse — a worshipper at the eastern wall tells me — let the gmina leave us in peace, assign the interim[?] cantor a pension, even a minimal one, and decency will be restored in the synagogue. The proof is that in the short time that the „people“ has been ruling — „the crisis has weakened“ already..
—o—
What would have become of them...
... „We have the honour to invite you to the performance in the premises of the women's „ochronka“ [children's home] in Będzin“.
An ironic smile appeared on my face as I read this invitation. — „A performance in the premises“ — which premises? In the one and only little room, which is the dining room for some thirty-odd children of the ochronka?...
Later, sitting in the „theatre hall“, only then did I see that they had made a „mistake“, since half of the little room had been taken for the stage, and there were still enough free seats... a sign that the initiators of the performance had calculated in advance that only those would come who take an interest in their fate not only on holidays... And indeed, who among our „notables“ takes an interest in the fact that in Pletner's house on Kołłątaja Street some forty orphan girls are being brought up?...
— The programme? — A whole pukh[?] of revues is not worth one song sung by the small, gifted children. Upon my life, it would be no disgrace at all if some of those who regale the public every Monday and Thursday with theatre performances came to take lessons from the children and learn from them how to recite, and a free stage bearing...
While the children sit down around the nicely laid tables, Mrs. Dr. Weinzieher explains to us the children's skills: that one is a manicurist [misprinted „manikiushistke“], the second a seamstress, the blonde one, who was taken in as a cripple, is a furrier, and this little one is going up to the 4th class of the gymnasium, this one, this one...
— Yes, madam [„tak, panie“, Polish], it costs a good deal of work, but otherwise what would have become of them?
— Yes, yes, I repeat after her the same words:
— „What would have become of them“...
—o—
A child of today complains...
When two children talk between themselves, I am the third — I have such a nature, a strong craving to listen to children's conversations...
This time too I did not miss out, listening to the conversation carried on by two girls, 13—14-year-old children of well-to-do parents.
— You know — says one to the other — although your parents are not as rich as mine, and you are not as nicely dressed as I am, nevertheless I envy you.
— For example? [„na przykład“, Polish] — asks the friend.
— I envy you, because your daddy [tatuś] held „sedery“ [Seders]...
— And my[?] daddy didn't?..
And she tells:
All the years „sedery“ used to be held at our home too; the whole Passover eve I already hoped that daddy would come back „from the synagogue“ [z bóżnicy] and sit down to conduct the Seder. Oh, how pleasant is the time when the whole „family“ [rodzina] sits around the richly laid tables, bright and lit up in every corner, and daddy would „pray“ [modlić się], I asked the „questions“ [pytania — the Four Questions], and it was so delightful, so sweet[?] — „you can't imagine“ [nie możesz sobie wyobrazić]...
— And this year?
Ah! Don't ask how unhappily I spent „those evenings“ [te wieczory]... Daddy did not go to the „synagogue“, but sat down to eat supper [kolacja] as on every other day...
— When I went up to him and begged: „Daddy! make a Seder, why do all people make Seders?“ [Polish: zrób seder, dlaczego wszyscy zrobią sedery?]... he shouted at me, saying that he no longer holds with the „old superstitions“ [stare zabobony]...
— „So you did not hold Seders at all?“[?]...
— After supper I went and stood at the window of the neighbour who lives in the basement flat [suterena]; there such joy reigned, and from outside I took part in their holiday...
— — — — — — — — —
I went away quickly, not wanting the girl to see me, and thought to myself:
— What a child of today complains about..
Katowice (On the 50th Jubilee of „Hibbat Zion“)

Mosze Fajnkind (Moshe Feinkind).
The „Zaglembier Tsaytung“ reported that a group of Zionists intends to gather in Katowice to celebrate the 50th jubilee of „Hibbat Zion“.
This notice awoke in my mind a sea of „memories“ about the town of Katowice in connection with the celebration of the 50th jubilee of „Hibbat Zion“.
For us veterans of „Hibbat Zion“ of the old cut, Katowice is, after all, more than a former border town to which we Polish Jews used to travel to buy cheap trashy goods and smuggle them across the Russian border at the risk of our lives, etc.[?].
For us veterans of the Zionist movement Katowice is the cornerstone of the Hovevei-Zion organisation in the whole world; in that town our masters and teachers laid the foundation, the basis for the Jewish national revival, for rational and purposeful Jewish colonisation in the Land of Israel — in one word, for the ingathering of the exiles.
I will not exaggerate if I say that „Katowice“ was the first stage on the road to Basel, where the Land of Israel was formulated and proclaimed as the national home for the Jews at the First Zionist Congress (1897).
„Ask thy father and he will show thee, thine elders and they will tell thee...“
On this occasion I wish to share with the Zaglembie reader my few memories about „Katowice“ of 50 years ago.
My task here is not to describe the present-day town as it looked then; if describe [sic, ?], I want to speak only about Jewish Katowice, in which the first conference of the „Hovevei Zion“ of the whole world took place in the month of Heshvan 5645 (November 1884).
At that time there was already in Katowice a „Hovevei Zion“ society, headed by the teacher Moritz Moses.
This society was grouped around the B'nai B'rith lodge „Concordia“, whose president was the ardent Jew Mr. Lewinger.
The „Concordia lodge“, unlike the other German B'nai B'rith order lodges, had in its programme, among other things, also the emigration and colonisation of the Eastern Jews, i.e. the Russian Jews; for these „B'nai B'rith“ members had seen with their own eyes in Katowice, as a border town, the great tragedy that took place in Russia in the eighties, and the Jews driven to wander as fugitives wherever their eyes led them.
It must be stressed that Katowice was the only town in Upper Silesia that rose to the height of its task in helping the Russian „persecuted“ in those catastrophic years.
The dear teacher Mr. Priwal, who was the editor of the „Kolonist“ in Katowice, S.[?] Friedländer, S.[?] Moses and others devoted all their free time to and stood up for the emigrating Jews and those wandering through Katowice.
Therefore, when the „Hovevei-Zion“ were preparing for their first organised meeting, they indeed had no more suitable place than Katowice.
There they already found understanding for the holy cause and true[?] hospitality.
Some thirty-odd delegates gathered there in secret, with R' Shmuel Mohilever, R' Dodl[?] Karliner, Dr. Pinsker and ShPR at their head.
The historic conference took place (11 Heshvan) in the beautifully decorated meeting hall of the B'nai B'rith lodge „Concordia“. They[?] were warmly welcomed by the lodge president Mr.[?] Lewinger. For that time it was already a great historic event that the president of a „B'nai B'rith lodge“ in Germany should welcome „Zion-enthusiasts“ (Zionsschwärmer), as the Hovevei-Zion used to be called then — and in the lodge's own premises, at that, where people spoke of a Jewish people, of national revival, of „auto-emancipation“ and the like.
R' Shmuel Mohilever, who was honorary president of the conference, delivered his famous and impressive speech on „the dried-up and again reviving bones“; Dr. Pinsker spoke on the aims of the conference, arguing at length for his „Auto-Emancipation“, and so on.
It was truly a joy to see how next to the strictly pious rabbis sat the editors of „HaMagid“, David Gordon, and of „HaMelitz“, Alexander Zederbaum, with skullcaps on their heads, and next to them again the free-minded Warsaw attorney Izydor Jasinowski, Dr. Joseph Chasanowitsch, the Orthodox Davidsohn, Wissotzky and others etc.[?]. They all poured out from their hearts the sorrow and pain, the torments and persecutions that their brethren have to endure in exile even now, in the age of civilisation and emancipation, for which there is only one remedy: the settlement of the Land of Israel.
True, here too the philanthropic character of the remedy was underlined and strongly accentuated, and in this sense the resolutions of the conference were also adopted; yet between the lines one could read that Dr. Pinsker's „Auto-Emancipation“ spoke out of them.
One must not forget that most of the delegates were from Russia, and one had to reckon with the hard conditions that prevailed there in the 1880s because of the nihilist assassination of Alexander II (1881) — so that on returning home they would not be thrown into the Tsarist prisons...
And in that year the first world organisation for the settlement of the Land of Israel was created at the Katowice conference, with a central committee at its head.
And since it happened to be the hundredth jubilee of the first practical Hovev Zion, R' Moses Montefiore of blessed memory, the union of the „Hovevei Zion“ of the whole world was given the name „Mazkeret Moshe“, and at the same time several money subsidies were set and allocated for the colonies already existing in the Land of Israel.
To tell the truth, the Katowice conference, because of its so very cautious tactics, did not arouse much enthusiasm among the masses at the time; they had hoped to hear quite different words from Katowice in answer to the slaughters of Jews in Romania and in Russia.
The lecture of ShPR (Shaul Pinchas Rabinowitz), the translator of Graetz's History into Hebrew, on the pogroms, which he delivered at the historic conference, did indeed contain very rich collected historical material, but again, for political reasons, it was heavily veiled and a bit too cold-blooded.
The then rebellious, nihilistically minded student youth would not or could not understand, and did not want to know of, the dangers that would[?] have threatened the participants of the conference over open words as soon as they returned home to Russia.
And like the course of the conference, so the whole Hovevei-Zion work was a quiet, calm one — more precisely, a bourgeois one; only later did it come alive and take on an open, stormy political character, and Basel had its say...
But without „Katowice“ there might have been no „Basel“; the quiet, well-trodden path of Katowice led, willy-nilly, to Basel.
For „Hibbat Zion“ was the springboard[?], the driving spring that led the Hovevei-Zion to Basel at the call of Dr. Herzl, may he rest in peace, despite the position and misgivings they then had towards and about political Zionism...
And Katowice goes on forging[?] the history of „Hibbat Zion“: the local Zionist society under the leadership of the so amiable and respected Arnold Wiener, who went on forging[?] there the golden chain of the Jewish renaissance, organised in November 1909 the 25th jubilee of the Katowice conference.
With some 400 delegates from Germany, Austria and Poland, the celebration is opened with a splendid speech by Nahum Sokolow, by Dr. Joseph Klausner and others.
We see there several more veterans of the first conference, such as Davidsohn (Warsaw), Pines and others. Before an audience of 1500 people fiery speeches are delivered in the great Reichshalle by Dr. Klee, Adolf Stand, Dr. Thon („From Katowice to Basel“) and others.
From their mouths one now hears quite different words, open, bold speech; no one speaks any longer of colonisation and philanthropy in the Land of Israel, but of the Basel Programme: a national home (homestead) for the Jews in the Land of Israel. Herzl now speaks out of their mouths. The youth storms, it is carried away; the Jewish German academics who came to greet the jubilee in their blue-and-white „trouser“[?] uniforms with the inscription on the breast „Mit Leib und Wehr, für Judas Ehr“ („With body and arms, for Judah's honour“) saluted with drawn swords, swearing meanwhile „If I forget thee [O Jerusalem]“...
Never in my life will I forget the impression that festive moment in Katowice made on me.
We, who went through the whole toilsome and hard road from Katowice to Basel, the long road from humiliation[?] to Zionism, from European progress to the Jewish renaissance — we greet with all our hearts the initiative of the Zaglembie and Upper Silesian Zionists to celebrate the 50th jubilee of „Hibbat Zion“ in Katowice, where the cradle of our revival stood.
After the Holiday...

[Feuilleton — a merchant's letter; Będzin, the economic crisis.] (A Merchant's Letter)
By Yosef Perlmutter.

My friend! Never before has the holiday made itself felt so much as precisely this year... Hard, very hard it was for every Jew to bring Passover into his home, but precisely because it came so hard, it was very noticeable, both in the street and in the synagogue; such a holiday mood as prevailed among the merchants I have never yet seen. First of all, the shops were closed eight full days: no tax executor, no komornik [bailiff]. No one to be afraid of... A true „season of our freedom“! Anyway[?], one was more or less[?] provided for; putting away the shop keys is, in these times, not one of the great misfortunes either. Everyone did it with a light heart. For in any case the takings do not cover the expenses. And it is not such a great misfortune. Nowadays it is rather a misfortune for a merchant when he has to open the shop...
Well, the weather helped too, so people went out for a stroll... While strolling I indeed noticed how my merchant acquaintances „shed one form and put on another“: they took off their weekday, worried, darkened faces and put on an altogether different appearance. And now I began to understand the Gemara, what the sages once said: „The Jerusalemites asked the Babylonians“ — those who lived in Jerusalem once asked those who live in Babylonia: why, wherefore are the festivals in Babylonia [printed „שבבל“] joyful, why are the holidays in Babylonia somehow merrier? Do you know what they answered? Simply: „because they are poor“ — because they are poor. The rich man allows himself to make a holiday every day, but the poor man, who lives, lehavdil, day in, day out like a dog, bows and scrapes before everyone, and every morsel comes to him with self-sacrifice — for him the holiday has an altogether different taste and a different charm. And therefore, because, for our many sins, we are all great paupers, we really felt and received the holiday mood this year more than in all the years before...
But, my friend, now, you see[?], it is bad; after such a holiday mood — back to cheder... And that is not one of the very tasty morsels... The matzos eaten, the wine drunk, the eggs chopped[?], and now there is nothing to start with. One feels like a kest-son-in-law [a young husband boarding with his in-laws] leaving his kest. And meanwhile a whole pack of payments has piled up: rent, turnover tax [obrotowe], income tax[?] [dochodowe], premises tax [lokalowe], Kasa Chorych [health-insurance fund], telephone... „The ledger is open and the hand writes“... And the executors want to know nothing... Holiday mood — all over. And now, „bzl and bzl, mb, ḥb“[?]... and the shop is meanwhile emptied; nobody has any money, after all, the bit of goods has been eaten up, and there are no credits for fresh goods, because the old ones are not yet paid... So what does one do next?
I think everyone will have to do as my grocer did. Here, I will tell you how my grocer gave me a lesson right on the evening the holiday ended, how business will be run among us from now on...
Even before I had finished drinking the Havdalah wine at the end of the holiday, in comes Reb Itshe, the grocer, still in his holiday velvet cap, but in his weekday, worn[?] kapote — a sign that he is already getting down to business. Enough rest... And here he asked a small thing of me: since I will surely want to eat bread and rolls in the morning, I should pay him for it right now; he will carry the money straight to the baker, the baker will give him baked goods; if not, I will have neither bread nor rolls, because the baker no longer wants to give credit and he has to pay first; and since he has no money, he must collect the money from all the housewives [gospodynie], so that the baker will supply him with baked goods...
— Reb Itshe, say I, since I have been buying from you for ten years now and I am a good friend of yours, I will do you a favour: I will go over with you to the baker and vouch for you for such a sum as a day's baking comes to... Good!
And without thinking long, I am already running with Reb Itshe to the baker. We come in — the oven is cold, not heated, no sign of any roll-flour, and no baker either. Where is Reb Nosn? And where is Reb Nosn's wife? — asks Reb Itshe.
— „Surely a strike — you don't want to work?“ — I turn to the journeymen...
No, Mister, if only there were that much work; we would work even twenty-four hours a day. But since the flour merchant no longer wants to supply any flour, because Reb Nosn has several times not paid, and now over the holiday he ate up the last few złoty of the „credit“ — so he is running around now — he from one side and his wife from the other — to all the little shops, asking them to pay in advance for the baked goods; the money will be brought to the flour merchant, and then they will be able to start baking...
And as you know, my friend, I am after all something of a public figure; well, shall I let[?] Będzin, God forbid, remain without rolls and without bread? I immediately grab one of the journeymen, and off we go[?] — all together to the flour merchant...
We come in to the flour merchant and find him sitting at the telephone, dressed for the holiday, and he shouts: if you leave me money now, I will ring the flour representative, and tomorrow I will be able to give you the flour...
— Perhaps you can tell me, Reb Aron, who the representative is?
— Mehikhi teysey [why not, of course], Reb Aron answers me, — if you will be so kind. Why not...
And without dithering long, we are already sitting in the tram and riding to the representative. Coming in we find a house full of guests. At one table they are playing „telephone“, at the second „king“ [card games], and in another room sits the representative at a conference with many more flour merchants, and they are deliberating how to go on trading... For there are no credits, and no confidence either... And flour there is in plenty, only they are looking for ways to make the flour move from its place and start wandering[?] — first of all to the merchant, then to the baker, to the grocer, until it comes into my home..
What came of the deliberation there I do not know; a fact is that bread, rolls and challahs were no longer lacking. But for me, my friend, the story got stuck deep in my head, and who knows whether this is not the main trouble of the whole crisis from which we all suffer so badly. There is always everything in plenty, and perhaps there is no lack of customers either. The trouble is only that the merchant has become impoverished, and there is no one to tie[?] both ends together... I am convinced that if only the merchant were put back on his feet, you will see how everything will start moving, and „the Jews“ [shall have light and gladness]..
Greetings from the Zagłębie Colony in Tel Aviv

[Eretz Israel — letter from Tel Aviv; the Levant Fair; natives of Zagłębie.]
(A letter from Eretz Israel.)
We had barely managed to sober up from the "Adloyada" (carnival) when we already had a second celebration here, and no smaller one: the "Maccabiad", which in its whole scope and execution was a huge sporting enterprise that its visitors and spectators will not forget. And we had barely managed to talk over the outcome of the competitions and sporting contests at the Tel Aviv Olympiad, when the local municipal administration, in partnership with the "Mischar w'Taasia" [Commerce and Industry] company, prepared [?] a third holiday for us: the Levant Fair (Oriental Fair) and the "Taarucha" (exhibition), which close this year's festivities of the Eretz-Israel spring.
The "Taarucha" is a splendid picture, demonstrating the economic forces of the young Jewish Yishuv not on canvas and in colours, not in figures and statistics, but in tangible objects of which the eye cannot get its fill. The entire production of Eretz Israel — agriculture, industry and commerce — is represented here, giving the impression that the visitor is not at an exhibition at all but in an industrial centre where an economically productive life pulsates. The 24 nations taking part in the Oriental Fair seem to be a "League of Nations" in miniature, which has gathered in Tel Aviv not for the sake of politics and diplomacy, but with the aim of creating and building.
From the last exhibition in the year 1929 to the present fair the Yishuv has progressed greatly in the economic field, and one sees clearly that the work in Eretz Israel is a fact which the whole international world reckons with. While great want and despair reign in the Jewish settlements of the Diaspora, Eretz Israel stands before new work opportunities and plans that can absorb new thousands of chalutzim [pioneers], who are a necessity of the greatest importance for our work. The Palestine government permits no workers' immigration, on the grounds of "economic equilibrium" in the country, but Jewish diligence will open the gates for the Jew who wants to go to Eretz Israel. The ever newer, larger planted orange-grove areas, the ever-growing orange export, the soon-to-be-completed Haifa port, the exploitation of the Dead Sea and of the "Hot Springs of Tiberias", Rutenberg's already completed works at Tel Or, the Haifa—Baghdad railway line, the Haifa—Mosul oil pipelines, the ever-improving communication between us and abroad — all this makes Eretz Israel an important factor in the Near East.
The fairground covers a large area, on which up to 1,200 exhibits are displayed, compared with 300 at the previous exhibition, and 24 nations take part in the fair, showing the products of their countries. The fair, which was advertised under the sign of the "HaGamal HaMeofef" (the Flying Camel) as the symbol of the reviving and expanding Near East, did not disappoint and can boldly measure itself against similar European exhibitions.
The ceremonial opening of the "Taarucha" took place in the presence of the High Commissioner, who in his inaugural speech praised the industriousness and ability of the Jews of Eretz Israel. Once again one saw the English "gentleman" who, in the name of his government, did not stint us fine words and promises — which, however, remain unrealized.
During the opening the platform of the exhibition hall was occupied by all the senior government officials, consuls, diplomats, clergy, the "Va'ad Leumi", the Zionist Executive, all in festive dress, in frock coats and top hats.
After the English and Jewish anthems, played by the British orchestra of the Jerusalem military regiment, the pavilions are opened, to which one must devote many hours in order to get to know them thoroughly. The U.S.S.R. (Soviet Russia) presented itself well and showed the sum total, the results of the "Pyatiletka" [Five-Year Plan]. The Eastern countries: Turkey, Egypt, Cyprus, Syria, Mesopotamia, Persia and Japan stand out with their exoticism. The pavilions of Romania, Switzerland, Austria, Germany, Lithuania, France and Belgium are also well visited. Eretz Israel shows its own production in the "Palace of Industry"; the "moshavot" (colonies) show in special kiosks the development of the plantations, and the "Histadrut HaOvdim" [General Federation of Workers] shows the fruitful activity of the Eretz-Israel workers.
The Polish pavilion, built in the form of a Zakopane "chatka" [hut] with the Polish coat of arms at the entrance, did not this time show — because of the short time left to the Polish–Palestinian Chamber of Commerce — the many-branched Polish production, so that it is hoped the pavilion will in future be better set out and represented.
In honour of the Polish pavilion the "Hitachdut Olei Polania" [Association of Immigrants from Poland] arranged a special ceremony, in which the Polish consul, Dr. Zdzisław Kurnikowski, took part; he spoke with appreciation of the Polish citizens in Eretz Israel who are building their old-new home. On this occasion the consul bade farewell with a Hebrew "Shalom" to the sportsmen from Poland in the "Maccabiah", who left the country in these days, having won the championship in football, boxing, light athletics, gymnastics and water polo. The Polish trade representative in Eretz Israel, Dr. Bernard Hausner [printed Hojzner], spoke about Polish–Jewish relations, expressing the wish that a greater exchange of goods between the two countries should take place between Poland and Eretz Israel.
The "Luna Park", brought specially from Paris, added much beauty to the fair with its many colourful popular amusements. The "Luna Park", which was set up [?] on the model of the "Prater" in Vienna, has great success among the young visitors of the fair, and serves at the same time as a place of entertainment.
A sensation was also caused by the Tel Aviv radio station, whose waves carry across all of Eretz Israel and the neighbouring countries. This station, which will operate only for the duration of the fair, is the beginning of a large radio network that will link Eretz Israel with the whole world by electric waves.
The Oriental Fair in Tel Aviv has closed, and may its success move the Yishuv to new conquests and gains through work and peace.
—————
At the close of today's letter I wish to pass on to the readers of the paper the news that the landsleit from Będzin and Sosnowiec living in Eretz Israel are organizing themselves into an association of "Olei Zaglembia" [Immigrants from Zagłębie], whose task is to serve with advice and deed those Jews of Zagłębie who wish to settle in Eretz Israel.
The initiators of the idea called a larger meeting at the home of Mr. Shoham (Steinfeld), which was attended by many Zagłębie Jews and tourists, among whom were also the "shlemim" [?] of the Sosnowiec "Maccabi" and the widow of the late Israel Moshe Winreb.
Mr. Shoham — one of the first Będzin pioneers, who came to Eretz Israel 25 years ago — shows great interest in the Jews of Zagłębie, although he has been away from his old home for so long. The hospitable house of Mr. Shoham-Steinfeld serves as a meeting place for the Tel Aviv Jews from Zagłębie.
At the above-mentioned meeting Messrs. Shabtai Weiss and Shmuel Krysztal discussed the importance of the association of "Olei Zaglembia". Mr. Abraham Hampel (Będzin), who has only just settled in Eretz Israel, described the sad situation of the Jews in Poland and their urge towards Eretz Israel. Mr. Meir Landsman (Sosnowiec), who stayed here as a participant in the "Maccabiah", took his leave in the name of the Sosnowiec "Maccabees", who represented themselves well at the Olympiad, and expressed great satisfaction with the visit to Eretz Israel.
Such "pgishot" [gatherings] of the "Yotzei Zaglembia" [natives of Zagłębie] will bind together and bring closer our landsleit, who at the same time think of the fate of their relatives and friends in Zagłębie.
Through the columns of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" the Zagłębie colony in Tel Aviv sends greetings and encouragement to the Jewry of Zagłębie.
Mordechai Hampel.
(Tel Aviv—Rishon LeZion).
The Enforced Double Sabbath

We have grown so used to our troubles that we have already stopped reacting. Nevertheless, when we see that on top of all the afflictions sent by Heaven come further special afflictions inflicted by man, when we see that even the small measure of air still left to us to breathe is also too much in their eyes, and that they try to pump the air out of there so that we should suffocate — we cannot keep silent about it.
The enforced second Sabbath is a terrible plague for us. It simply means that our livelihood is reduced by one sixth: while Christians can work and trade 6 days a week, we can do so only 5 days. In no other country in the world do Jews have this trouble. In some countries Jews have already abandoned the Sabbath; in other countries, where Jews live in compact masses and do not want to desecrate the Sabbath, they are treated with kindness and the authorities turn a blind eye [lit. "look through the fingers"]. There is even a country, Holland, where the question of Sabbath rest has been settled by law in the most liberal way for Jews. We shall acquaint our readers with this matter separately.
But here in Poland, especially in the "Jewish" towns, or in the Jewish quarters of the non-Jewish towns, Jews do not want to and cannot desecrate the Sabbath; they keep the Sabbath with the greatest self-sacrifice, even at the price of their bite of bread. And the decree of Sunday rest is enforced here with such strictness that it truly recalls the Middle Ages, just as if religion were still today the sole regulator of the general life of the country!
Not to speak of public life, where open[?] shops and all kinds of businesses might offend someone's religious feelings! But even in closed premises, where nobody sees and nobody hears, one may not desecrate Sunday either. And not merely a prohibition on paper: police agents are sent out to carry out raids [obławy], to search and to rummage, in case, God forbid, someone is breaking the law — and then there is but one sentence for him!... Reports, and being dragged into fines, until life becomes loathsome:
They go to artisans in their homes. One may not thread a needle, may not drive in a nail — a Sabbath of Sabbaths! Everyone knows[?] how bad things are today for the Jewish artisan, how hungry he is for a złoty's livelihood, and if a bit of work turns up and one hurries to finish it so as to have something to eat, then no: go and put your teeth on the shelf for a day [i.e. go hungry]!...
Lately they have taken on the banks: they go from one to the next and draw up reports. Here it is no longer only the entrepreneurs who suffer, but the masses too. A merchant town cannot live without a bank; money operations are the most vital[?] nerves of trade and industry — when the bank is closed for two days, commerce falls into a "higer-ples"[?]; it cannot move. And whom does one harm if one sits at the desk on Sunday? Whom can it hurt if one has the opportunity to prepare on Sunday so as to be able to pay the tax or the bill of exchange on Monday? Why are the Jews so sinful here that they must lose a whole sixth of their freedom of movement?
And this under the present government, which is supposedly favourable to us, which supposedly wants to show us a friendly face!
Very well, give us something they cannot — but why break into our own four cubits and here too block the narrow little channels from which thin little drops of livelihood still trickle to us? Why?
P. K.
Rasputin and His Jewish Beloved

(23) A historical novel by Boris Maksimov.
— Do not listen to anyone's advice any more... Believe in the power of my prayers, and your son will live and will be healthy and strong!
— — — — —
Rasputin left a tremendously strong impression on the boy Alexei. Even when he had already left the room and the door had already closed behind him, the boy still gazed with cheerful, shining looks at the door through which the good man with the big black beard and wild eyes had disappeared. He gazed like this for a while, then he turned to his governess, Maria Vishnyakova, who was standing silently by his bed, and asked her:
— Maria, who is he?
— A "holy" wanderer! — answered Vishnyakova, and she herself was still surprised and dumbfounded — he is a "holy" man, who will drive every pain away from you and will make you healthy... God Himself sent him here[?] to help you.
The boy whispered[?], smiling and dreamy, feeling sleep overpowering him:
— A "holy" man... he is a "holy" man...
His eyelids grew heavy. His eyes closed. It did not take long and he sank into a calm sleep... He felt no more pain.
Was it a mere coincidence that the "naslednik" [heir, Russ.] got better precisely when the Siberian muzhik was there, or perhaps the hypnotizing power of Rasputin's eyes acted upon him and drove the pain away?...
— — — — —
The Tsaritsa led Rasputin into the Tsar's study, where Vyrubova was waiting for him. On entering, Rasputin's sharp, practised eye noticed at once: Vyrubova was embarrassed; she was a little flustered and her face was flushed with passion... He smiled quietly... The Tsaritsa, however, noticed nothing; with quick steps she went straight to the Tsar, who had risen when they came in, and with tears of joy[?] in her eyes she told him that the "naslednik" was better. The pains had let up, he was now talking, smiling, and had fully come to himself.
Joy appeared on the Tsar's face. His eyes lit up brightly. He went straight to Rasputin, took his right hand in both his hands and pressed it with warmth and gratitude:
— I thank you from the depths of my heart, "holy father"!
Rasputin remained calm and erect[?]. He astonished[?] the Tsar and said with assurance:
— Rely on me... I shall make the "naslednik" healthy...
And after Vyrubova too had taken leave of the Tsar and the Tsaritsa, Rasputin left the imperial palace together with her...
• • •
Sitting in the carriage next to Vyrubova, Rasputin was in very high spirits: the shrewd, cunning muzhik felt and understood that with his visit to the imperial palace a career was beginning for him such as he had never dared even to dream of. Vyrubova too was lively and cheerful: now she knew that her plan had succeeded. Rasputin had been a success, the "naslednik" was better, and the Tsaritsa had asked Rasputin to come again tomorrow. Archimandrite Feofan, who had intrigued against her, was already as good as completely removed from the court. Now her position would be strengthened. She and Rasputin would be the only ones with a strong influence at court.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Kedoshim)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parshat Kedoshim
The Portion
a) "Turn ye not unto idols" (19:4)
"Elilut" [idolatry] — this means foolish, crippled piety, from the word "alyah" [tail]... and the tail is the farthest from the head and has the least connection with reason. That is why a pious fool is titled with it. Mei Shlot [?].
b) "Thou shalt leave them for the poor and the stranger... Ye shall not steal" (ibid., 19:11)
Usually the "shayger" [?] Jew justifies himself that he steals and goes bankrupt in order to be able to give charity, to do good deeds with the money; but even for all that — "ye shall not steal"! One may not steal in any case... Tiferet Shlomo.
c) "Ye shall not steal" (ibid.)
In the Ten Commandments it says "Thou shalt not steal" — in the singular, while here it says in the plural: "Ye shall not steal" — because here it speaks of commercial dishonesty and theft. And here the theft is mostly [?] a double one: the seller gives false goods and the buyer pays with false cover... Or Olam.
d) "The wages of a hired servant shall not abide with thee" (ibid., 13)
The Aleksander Rebbe, R' Yechiel of blessed memory, before he became a rebbe, was no great rich man. Once a shoemaker brings him a pair of repaired [?] shoes, and he has nothing to pay him the two roubles' wages. So Rabbi Yechiel went about the whole night borrowing the money and did not want [?] to go to sleep earlier. Only after midnight did he manage to get the money, and he himself ran joyfully to the shoemaker, who was already sound asleep and had not expected [?] to be woken by such a guest. Eser Nifla'ot.
e) "Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment" (ibid., 15)
Yes, one can commit the cruellest wrongs, the most terrible injustices — in judgment; and so that it should, as it were, be wrapped [?] in the mantle of law, carried out according to all the rules of justice — unfortunately much "unrighteousness in judgment" happens. Kokhav mi-Yaakov.
f) "Thou shalt surely rebuke thy neighbour" (ibid., 17)
"Thy neighbour" ["et amitekha" — also "with thy neighbour"] — you should rebuke yourself along with him when you rebuke your fellow. You should also keep yourself in mind while you reprove your fellow... Tiferet Uziel.
g) "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" (ibid., 18)
"Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself — this is a great principle in the Torah" — in Torah, in spiritual matters, one loves one's fellow as oneself, [for] one wants to bring merit to another too. But in plain earthly matters — "your own life comes first"; a person himself comes before everything... Torat Moshe.
—o—
And even in Torah, in spiritual matters, it says only "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" — as oneself. But one need not love the other more: in this respect [?] — more than oneself, wanting to endow him with piety more than oneself... No'am Megadim.
—o—
At "thou shalt love thy neighbour" the verse ends: "I am the Lord". For only God knows who truly loves his fellow. For man himself it is hard to recognise his true, honest friend. Sefer ha-Brit (Rav Tzvi Hirsch Kalischer).
—o—
"As thyself" — even when your fellow is of the same trade as you, you should love him too... Kerem Binyamin.
—o—
Haman told Ahasuerus that the ten thousand talents of silver which he was giving in order to destroy the Jews "I will pay into the hands of those that have the charge of the business [osei ha-melakha — literally 'those who do work']" — by this he meant that the Jewish craftsmen themselves would supply him the money so that he would destroy their competitors... Attributed to the Warka Rebbe.
Avot, Chapter Two
h) "And be not wicked in thine own esteem [bifnei atzmekha — literally 'by thyself']"
This means those who before the world are righteous and "by themselves", when nobody sees, are what they really are: wicked...
About such a hypocrite the Gemara tells (Moed Katan 24) that when he died [?], pigs devoured his body. Why pigs of all things?
— Because the pig, too, shows the world a kosher foot... Beit Yitzchak.
i) "Three things drive a man out of the world."
The author of "Tiferet Shlomo" was once a guest in Dembitz [Dębica] at the local rabbi, R' Reuven Horowitz. The latter honoured the Radomsk Rebbe and asked him to be the first to wash [his hands] for the meal. But the Rebbe does not want to: "the master of the house breaks bread first". An argument ensues, until R' Reuven exclaims: "Whatever the master of the house tells you, do — except 'go out'". You must therefore obey me.
The sharp-witted Radomsk Rebbe answers him:
"Except 'go out'" means: except for those things about which it is said "they drive a man out of the world", among which honour is also counted... For the sake of a little honour you will not drive me out of the world.
The Fashion Revolution

[Feuilleton — fashion and the crisis.] (A short feuilleton)
Have you a wife? A couple of daughters too? Then I shall announce good tidings to you:
The almighty King of Fashion has abdicated — without civil wars, without bloodshed.
This very king, who ruled mercilessly over the women... when he fancied seeing the women's legs of the whole world, he issued a "razkaz" [order, from Russian], that short little dresses be worn. When he fancied shoulders — out came a "razkaz" to open the "shoulders" in the dresses. When he desired women's bosoms, he ordered the dresses to be cut out at the front.
His word was holy to the women and girls; at once there was a rush to the dressmakers, and every one wanted to carry out the king's command as precisely as possible.
Now it is all over with the King of Fashion, just like Spain.
The latest women's journals report that today fashion has gone out of fashion.
And do you know why? Precisely because of the crisis!
Fashion and the crisis could not live together [?] — go and make a new lady's dress every day when the men's pockets are empty...
The latest cry of fashion is: no fashion. One will be able to wear whatever one wants.
A woman will go up to the wardrobe, pick out [printed "eyzukhn"] a dress from five years ago, a coat from six years ago and a pair of "meshtn" [?] from ten years ago. What is there to say? "Every man did that which was right in his own eyes"; whoever wants can wear anything.
It's true — when you go out into the street on Saturday afternoon, you will see, strolling in all sorts of colours, long dresses with short coats, long coats with short dresses, small hats, large hats, the crown of the hat ["denke", Polish denko] up, the crown down.
— Whom should one fear? The king has, after all, already abdicated!
But...
I have scant faith in this revolution.
I am still afraid. The women will yet track down the King of Fashion somewhere in Honolulu and set him back on the throne.
For what won't a woman do for the sake of fashion?
Yosef.
What Imre Ungár Will Play at His Saturday Concert in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — culture; concert.] With great excitement the Saturday concert at the "Pałac" of the blind Jewish-Hungarian pianist Imre Ungár is awaited; he distinguished himself at the last International Chopin Competition in Warsaw.
As we learn, the programme of the concert is as follows:
Bach — Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue; Beethoven — Sonata in S-major [?] (Op. 10 [?]); Schumann — 1) In der Nacht, 2) "Ini-ovng" [?, probably Aufschwung]; Chopin — 1) C-sharp minor Nocturne, 2) two Mazurkas and 3) Polonaise in A-flat major; and Liszt — Twelfth Rhapsody.
Ungár's speciality is Chopin; but now we shall have the opportunity to hear how the great master performs Beethoven, Liszt and Bach.
Most of the tickets for this interesting concert are already sold out.
The Problem of Physical Education (Air and Sun)

[Education — health.] With the approach of summer, old dreams awaken that for several[?] months had been sunk in a winter sleep. Whoever can begins to get ready to leave the city — the city of polluted air, of troubles, of worries and of the constant "oy-ha". With nervous impatience everyone waits for his day to get away[?] — one to his land of mountains, another to the seashore, and some to famous spas or to a modest summer dacha. The warm rays of the sun penetrate the heart and awaken a closeness to nature, to the sun, to the air. A desire to throw off the superfluous clothing. To nestle closer to, and bond with, the whole natural surroundings. It is not only the longing for wider horizons, new landscapes, fresh colours — it is an inner, organic striving to rest the weary body in the lap of Mother Nature, to calm the frayed nerves, to refresh the whole organism. And indeed, those whom circumstances allow to satisfy their striving come back as a rule refreshed, strengthened and rejuvenated, armed with fresh juices and strength for the further fierce[?] struggle of life.
These blessed results are brought back not only by those who, under medical supervision, took specially prescribed baths or some remedies or other, but by mere "dachniks" [summer-cottage holidaymakers] who did nothing whatsoever except spend a while, day and night, outside the city. This is first and foremost the effect of the good, clean [printed "reyger"], unspoilt air.
In breathing, a person inhales various elements of which the air consists and which are necessary to sustain human life. Unfortunately, however, city air contains various impure and harmful substances, and on the other hand it lacks many [elements]. Without which the organism finds it hard to manage. The air by the sea, in the mountains, in the forests, free of smoke and of various harmful vapours, cleanses the blood and acts on its circulation.
But there is also the effect of the sun. The sun is, after all, the source of all life. Under the effect of its rays everything blossoms and grows; where its rays do not reach, everything withers and rots. As far as man is concerned, it acts not only on his physical but also on his mental state. That is why sun baths were known already in the most ancient times. Herodotus already has things to tell about them, and Cicero tells us with how much love the Romans used to devote themselves to these baths. In those times sun baths were prescribed against a whole series of diseases; today they are used mainly in the fight against the various bacilli that lie in wait for human health and life.
Bacilli are so small that on the smallest area of one cubic millimetre 600 million can be found, and they multiply at enormous speed. Scientists have established that ordinary daylight halts the development of the bacilli. Direct sunlight destroys them completely.
Bacilli are a plague for everything that has any connection with life. From this alone it is already clear that the light of the sun influences the whole organic and inorganic world. Under its effect the plants turn green, the birds sing; under its influence falls man.
From what has been said so far, the enormous importance emerges already of merely staying [outdoors], and all the more so of physical exercises, games, recreation and sport in the free, fresh air and under the blessed rays of the sun.
A factory worker or miner seldom looks fresh and healthy. His face is usually sickly and pale. These people are not easy to help, though this is greatly to be regretted. Not so is it, not so should it be with the young, and especially not with schoolchildren. At school age the young must prepare themselves for later life. But preparing means not only sharpening the brain, arming oneself with a good number of mathematical formulas and historical dates, but — at least to the same degree as the mind — forming, strengthening and hardening the body. It often happens, however, that in their great zeal quite a few teachers forget this simple elementary truth and load the children with work beyond measure; in harmonious cooperation, as is only proper, these teachers are helped by the parents, who want [often?] the child to sit until late into the night, bent over his work, so that, God forbid, he should not enjoy a bit of air and sun.
— "Later, when you finish, you'll have your fun."
The children "finish", leave the schools, and look worn out and emaciated, as if they were rising from a severe typhoid fever, and recovery after many years of exhaustion does not come quickly, sometimes never. Not only during the school year do the children have no time to catch their breath — even the dream of "summer life" comes out blurred for them. For even during the holidays they often have small, so-called "quiet"[?] assignments, and in connection with them big, gnawing worries. Recently I met two girls, two friends, who complained that they constantly suffer from headaches. Dr. M. told them it was migraine, coming from exhaustion, from depletion. "We are still so young," they said in broken, piercing little voices, "and we already suffer from migraine."
No. It is high time to roll away the stone with joint forces. To create the springs of physical health and inner happiness for our youth. More important than any lesson are air and sun. Every child, every pupil must in any case have the opportunity to spend two hours a day carefree in the open air and under the sun.
Teachers are usually friends of the young. As is well known, only people who love pedagogy, following[?] an inner calling, devote themselves to it. But even the righteous go astray. Therefore public cooperation is always a necessity. Therefore in such a case it is chiefly the parents' committees that must fulfil their duty. It is concern for our young generation that guides our pen here; it is the sufferings of our youth that dictate to us these harsh words.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin

[Będzin — local news.]
Cantor Avraham Yitzchak Szerman Is Coming.
As we are informed, the former cantor Mr. Avraham Yitzchak Szerman has accepted the proposal of hundreds of synagogue worshippers to come back here and take over the office of cantor.
Mr. Szerman's arrival is expected within the next few weeks.
—o—
The Gabbaim of the Chevra Kadisha Will Complete the Mikveh Building.
This week a meeting took place of the kehilla administration together with the gabbaim (wardens) of the Chevra Kadisha (burial society), who are taking it upon themselves to finish the new mikveh building.
For this purpose an expert will be engaged, who is to assess how large the capital must be so that the building can finally be completed.
—o—
A New Jew-Baiting Organ.
On Tuesday, the 3rd of May of this year, the first issue appeared of the organ of „Rozwój“ [a Polish antisemitic association] entitled „Nasza Era“ [?; printed „נאזא ערא“], edited by Aleksander Mieszalski [?].
In the paper's platform, which comprises 29 points, Polish society is called upon to boycott Jews; among other things it says that: 1) a Polish citizen can only be one in whose veins Polish blood flows. Therefore a „Żyd“ [„Jew“, here pejorative] cannot be a member of Polish society and must be regarded only as a guest, to whom the rights of a foreigner [obcokrajowiec] apply. 2) The government must expel all foreigners, in order to secure the existence of its own citizens.
3) To confiscate all the property of Jews in time of war. 4) To begin an internal and external struggle against the Semites, and 5) above all, not to buy from and not to support Jewish trade and crafts.
The Jew-baiting issue is also furnished with a series of advertisements, among which the well-known cosmetics firm „Fuls“ [?] of Warsaw advertises itself...
—o—
By Car to Eretz Israel.
A group of Jewish sportsmen is organising itself to make a journey to Eretz Israel by car. According to the calculation, such a trip should last about 3 weeks.
The group has approached the world union „Maccabi“ about this, for various instructions and also for support for the interesting journey.
—o—
The Etat Lists Will Be Sent to the Magistrate
Because of the critical financial situation of the kehilla treasury, the administration has adopted a decision that the etat [annual kehilla tax] arrears, also for the year 1932 [?], which despite the demands made so far have still not been settled, will be sent to the „Magistrat“ [Będzin municipality] to be collected together with enforcement costs.
—o—
Contact Between the Parents and the Management of the Public Schools.
In the large halls of Public School [szkoła powszechna] No. 4 a large parents' meeting took place, before which the headmistress, Mrs. Podlińska [?], reported on a series of school matters, above all on establishing permanent contact between the parents and the school where their children study.
Mr. Sz. Fridler, who welcomed the initiative, added that a special parents' committee should be created, in which every class should be represented, and the committee together with the school management should carry out the proposed programme.
—o—
Tragic Death of a 2-Year-Old Child.
On the Dąbrowa — Ząbkowice railway line, the 2-year-old Czarnecka girl was playing. At that moment a passenger train passed, which struck the child on the head. The child was taken to the Będzin hospital, where it died a few hours later.
—o—
Registration of Those Wronged in the Turnover-Tax Assessments.
The local Merchants' Association is conducting a registration of the merchants who were wronged in the turnover-tax [podatek obrotowy] assessments for 1931.
The registration takes place today, Friday, on Saturday night and on Sunday evening at the association's premises.
—o—
Commission of Inquiry into the Events of the First of May.
In connection with the bloody events in Zagłębie on the 1st of May, a special commission of the voivodeship [województwo] was here last Tuesday and acquainted itself with the details of the events in Dębowa Góra and in Strzemieszyce.
The commission established that the police used firearms [?] only at the most dangerous moments, when their lives were threatened.
It was also established that the number of wounded policemen reaches up to 30.
—o—
League for Labour Eretz Israel
This Saturday afternoon an extraordinary general meeting of the League for Labour Eretz Israel will take place at the premises of „Hitachdut“.
—o—
Conference of the Youth Organisation „Sinai“.
On Sunday a gathering of all „Sinai“ youth organisations took place. After the greetings and lectures a businesslike discussion developed. The conference was closed with „Techezakna“ and „Hatikva“.
—o—
A Bridegroom Honours His Father-in-Law with a Stool to the Head...
This week a din Torah (rabbinical court case) took place at the local rabbinate between a local father-in-law and his bridegroom.
During the pleadings the bridegroom „honoured“ the father-in-law with a stool.

Sosnowiec: The Presidium Elections of the Kehilla Council and Board Annulled / General Meeting at the „Hitachdut“ / General Meeting of the Bank for Small Traders and Artisans / From the Keren Kayemet Committee in Sosnowiec / Staff Cuts at the Magistrate / A Big Theft in the Middle of the Town

[Sosnowiec — kehilla, societies and institutions; six short news items.]
The starosta [district head] has notified the kehilla board that the presidium elections of the new kehilla council and board are annulled. At the same time it is ordered that new presidium elections take place within 8 days.
The elections will thus take place next Sunday. In the morning the presidium of the council will be elected, and in the afternoon the presidium of the board.
—o—
General Meeting at the „Hitachdut“.
On Thursday the annual general meeting took place in the society's own premises, with a large number of members taking part. Mr. A. Mulsztajn opens the meeting and gives the first word, for the general report, to Mr. A. Kahn. Treasury — Warojsl Uska [?]. Press — Brojner, library — Fajgenbaum, Keren Kayemet — Szatenfeld, and League for Working Eretz Israel — Józef Kerner.
Because of the late hour the meeting was broken off. The continuation takes place this Saturday; on the agenda are further reports, discussions, a lecture by Mr. A. Kahn, election of a new committee, and free motions.
—o—
General Meeting of the Bank for Small Traders and Artisans.
There is in our town a Jewish financial institution which came out of the „storm-and-stress period“ undamaged and carries on its solid and honest activity to this day.
That is the Bank for Small Traders and Artisans on Targowa Street, which next Sunday at 4 p.m. will hold its annual general meeting in the „Sala Angielska“ [English Hall].
It is desirable that the sovereignty of the bank should remain as it has been so far. The members must strive to bring greater revival into the bank, so that the small Jewish merchant and artisan may have an institution of his own that will sustain his existence.
—o—
From the Keren Kayemet Committee in Sosnowiec.
These days the representative, head of the Central Bureau of the Keren Kayemet in Warsaw, Mr. Bloch, stayed in Zagłębie.
Taking advantage of his presence, the local committee convened a larger meeting of representatives of all organizations.
After the discussions Mr. Bloch lectured on the topic „Our Land Policy in Eretz Israel“.
On Sunday, 1 May of this year, the KKL committee organized throughout the whole town an inspection of collection boxes (pushkes), whose task was also to recruit [?] new box-holders.
Almost all the senior members of every [?] organization took part in the inspection.
—o—
Staff Cuts at the Magistrate.
As of the 1st of this month, several officials of the Sosnowiec Magistrate (town council) have been dismissed for reasons of economy.
—o—
A Big Theft in the Middle of the Town.
Thieves got into Mr. Grynbaum's flat on Piłsudski Street in Sosnowiec, where, in the absence of the household, they made themselves at home and took various clothes, linen and silver objects.

Olkusz / General meeting of the 'Folks-Bank' / A big fire / Personal news / A general Talmud Torah committee founded / A 115-year-old woman has died / A theft / An assessment commission for the budget appointed / Donations received at the editorial office

[Olkusz — community and local news.]
General meeting of the "Folks-Bank" [People's Bank].
On Sunday the annual general meeting of the "Folks-Bank" took place in the premises of the Artisans' Association. In the presence of about 100 members, the chairman of the supervisory board, Mr. A. Blum, opened the meeting with a short introduction in which he stressed that, despite the severe crisis, the bank had nevertheless overcome all obstacles.
Mr. Reuven Dafner was elected chairman of the meeting, and Messrs. Aharon Podalski and Hershel Gliksman as assessors. Reports on the activity to date were given by the president and vice-president of the management board, Messrs. Berish Meisles and A. Muszkatblat, who described with statistical figures the bank's strenuous activity in the past year. The report of the supervisory board was given by Mr. A. Blum, who declared that the management's balance sheet agrees with reality. After a short discussion, in which S. G. Kerner, H. Szarf and others took part, the reports were taken note of and the council and management were granted a discharge (absolutorium). Because of the crisis the current budget has been cut by 60 per cent and amounts in total to 10 thousand złoty.
Finally, supplementary elections to the management board took place, and Mr. A. Muszkatblat was re-elected with almost all the votes. Three new members were elected to the supervisory board: Messrs. Avraham Persal, Moshe Shmuel Szwarcberg and Reuven Dafner.
The next day the constituent meeting took place. Mr. A. Muszkatblat was elected president of the management board, Mr. Avraham Persal president of the council, and Mr. Akiva Kaushma[?] vice-president.
—o—
A big fire.
On the night of the last day of Passover a terrible fire broke out in Mr. Talerman's buildings by the sawmill (tartak) in the Kraków suburb [Przedmieście Krakowskie].
From an unknown cause the fire started in a room and within a short time engulfed the 3[?]-storey building, which burned down completely. The occupant of the house, Mrs. Feuerstein, was carried out unconscious from the burning flat. Some belongings were rescued and the rest burned. Local firemen and those from the surroundings took part in the rescue operation.
The next day a charred wallet containing an undamaged 50-złoty banknote was found among the ruins.
—o—
Personal news.
The Starosta [district governor] has accepted the resignation of the dozors [kehilla board members] Messrs. M. Szwarcberg and A. Paluch and confirmed their substitutes, Avromele Banker and Chaim Danciger, who are already taking part in the kehilla meetings.
—o—
A general Talmud Torah committee founded.
With the participation of town activists, a committee has been founded at the gmina [municipality] to establish a general Talmud Torah, where children of all strata of the Jewish population will study.
—o—
A 115-year-old woman has died.
Last week the childless Reizl[?] Granek died at the age of 115.
Until a few days before her death the deceased had been fresh and healthy.
—o—
A theft.
On Friday night thieves got into Avromele Kerner's tavern and stole 50 bottles of vodka and 26 bottles of Carmel wine. Part of the stolen goods has been found.
A. B.
—o—
An assessment commission for the budget appointed.
At a time when the new budgets have already been approved in other kehillas in Zagłębie, the local kehilla budget is still in swaddling clothes. Because of this situation the Starosta has appointed a commission to prepare the apportionment (rozkład) of the budget. The commission consists of Messrs. L. Szwajcer (chairman), L. Zendel, A. B. Wingsztok and, as representative, Mr. Iczke Zaks.
Mr. Zaks does not accept the appointment. In his reply to the Starosta, Mr. Zaks explains that he declines the office for the following reasons: 1) he, a long-standing member of the kehilla board, has been appointed as a representative at a time when Mr. Wingsztok has not yet been officially confirmed as a board member; and 2) in such an economic crisis he does not want to take part in the assessments being made within the framework of the budget increased by the council.

Donations received at the editorial office.
For the orphanage of the Jewish Charitable Society in Będzin we have received — 5 złoty.

The Present Situation in Poland

In connection with the newly created economic "Sejm", which recently held its deliberations in Warsaw, Prof. Rybarski writes in the "Gaz. Warsz." [Gazeta Warszawska]:
"This 'Sejm' adopted a series of resolutions which aroused no enthusiasm among the government group. The deliberations of the economic circles were above all a protest against etatism [state control of the economy] in its various forms — a conspicuous and decisive protest. We have heard more than once how this or that government representative spoke out against etatism. But even if he said it sincerely, his voice carried no decisive weight. In the government camp there are etatists and opponents of etatism, since almost every possible conviction can be found in this department store. But the foundations on which the camp rests, its right to exist, lead directly to etatism. Etatism flows from the notion of a strong government, from the slogan 'Everything for the State', which in practice means: everything in the hands of the authorities, everything under their control. The 'etatism' of the ruling group is not some ideology, but simply a result of its system of self-preservation, of the will to hold on to power.
"The representatives of big industry who work with the government call out to it: break with etatism. But this call, translated into realistic language, simply means an appeal[?] to the government: go away!... This explains why the present governments cannot break with etatism."
The former Finance Minister Matuszewski also deals with the problem of etatism and cartels, but on a much broader and deeper scale. Mr. Matuszewski writes in the "Gaz. Polska" [Gazeta Polska]: "There is now taking place throughout the whole world a great war over how to divide the social income.
It is not a question here of the well-known Marxist theory of the struggle between capital and labour. The struggle is between two economic systems: a bound economy and an unbound one, a monopolistic and a free one — an economy that is regulated by prices, and an economy that tries to regulate prices.
The monopoly system today represents the programme of impoverishing the world; the 'anarchic' system — the programme of improving the situation.
"In the [—] economic difficulties, the rationing of sales causes a reduction of the [—]. [—] monopolistic economy is always an economy that socialises its losses. A cartel makes the buyers of its goods pay for its mistakes. The difference between a monopolistic and a non-monopolistic economy consists, accordingly, also in this: that a private entrepreneur goes bankrupt in a crisis, i.e. he loses what he earlier received from society. A monopolistic economy, on the other hand, lays its losses upon the whole of society.
The monopolists make use of the fine phrase 'organised economy', but organised economy means[?] above all: limiting production and raising prices. Present-day Russia cannot be taken as an example; true, a monopolistic economy rules there and at the same time there is growth of production. That is because in Russia there are millions of hectares of land that have never yet been cultivated. But once the 'piatiletka' [Five-Year Plan] ends, there too overproduction will have to come, and consequently a limitation of production. In the further part of his very interesting article Mr. Matuszewski shows that the monopolists' whole theory of maintaining equilibrium by limiting production is false, because the peasant is against it. The peasant ploughs and sows and wants to get as many products as possible out of the soil. And precisely because of this peasant, equilibrium will not be maintained by the monopolists, but only by cheapening prices, by setting the factories in motion again, producing as much as possible and settling for the most minimal profits. This is the only way that can lead the world out of the present severe crisis."

What the Będzin butchers have to tell.. / „Dairy“ signs to be introduced... / Fell off the tram. / Committee to promote domestic products. / New circular (okólnik) on the reliefs for „zaległe obrotowe“ (turnover-tax arrears).

Last Tuesday evening the Będzin kehilla board held a meeting. In the middle of the meeting a delegation of butchers came in and began recounting very „fine“ facts about the Będzin shochtim (ritual slaughterers) regarding their duties.
In connection with this, a meeting of the kehilla board on the matter will take place next Sunday. The shochtim are also being invited to that meeting.
—o—
„Dairy“ signs to be introduced...
On Sunday the milk dealers were summoned to a meeting of the Będzin rabbinate and the gabbaim of „Shomrei Shabbat“, who informed the milk dealers that the rabbinate and Shomrei Shabbat had decided that every milk dealer must have a ne'eman (supervisor) to watch over the kashrut of the milk. In addition, every milk shop is to be provided with a „kosher dairy“ sign... The fee is to be 2 groszy per litre...
When the milk dealers spoke out against the regulation, arguing that the milk suppliers hold hechsherim (kashrut certificates) from the local rabbis of their own places, the representatives of „Shomrei Shabbat“ threatened that „the milk will be declared forbidden“.
The candidates for the supervisor posts are the „editors“ of the „Monthly Bulletin“ („Khoydesh-bletl“)...
—o—
Fell off the tram.
The priest Mazurkiewicz, while getting off the tram in Dąbrowa, fell onto the cobbled street and was slightly injured as a result.

New circular (okólnik) on the reliefs for „zaległe obrotowe“ (turnover-tax arrears).
Owing to the doubts raised by the Finance Minister's decree on paying turnover-tax arrears (zaległe obrotowe) in instalments, the Ministry of Finance has issued a new circular, number
L. D. U. 17912.
The circular states:
As turnover-tax arrears covered by the relief decree are counted all turnover-tax arrears (zaległe podatki obrotowe) up to 1 April (kwiecień) 1931, as well as all advance payments (zaliczki) that were due by 1 April 1931.
Thus the reliefs apply to the turnover-tax advances that had to be paid [in] 1980 [sic; read 1930], as well as to the advance of 15 March 1931.
On the other hand, the reliefs will not apply to the difference between the advances that had to be paid and the amount of the payment order (nakaz płatniczy; printed „zakaz“) received on 15 April 1931.
Wholesalers (hurtownicy) who pay monthly advances will have counted as arrears the advances they had to pay in by the 38th [sic; read 28th] of February (luty) 1931.
Persons who owe no tax arrears at all that were due before 31 March 1931, and who owe only the tax from after 1 April 1931, will have these tax arrears from 1 April 1981 [sic; read 1931] to 1 April 1932 deferred[?], on condition that they now pay punctually the turnover [tax] they owe under the new payment order (the advances are called „zaległe“); for each advance and for the remaining turnover [tax] they will be credited with 33 per cent of the amount paid, as an instalment towards the tax arrears.
These reliefs are really very important and [printed „of“] one should take advantage of them.
To the turnover-tax amounts due for the period from 1 April 1921 [sic; probably 1931] to 31 August (sierpień) 1932, which will now be collected by distraint (egzekucja), the same reliefs provided in the decree will be applied. That is, from every amount collected a part of the taxes will be deducted as a bonus (gratification) at the rate of 50, 35 or 25 per cent.

[Będzin — livelihood and employment; letter to the editor.] At the present time, when hunger and want rage in the Jewish street, when thousands of Jewish families are without a livelihood and have no means whatever of sustaining themselves and their families, one must think and seek various counsels and devices for saving the surviving remnant. The means used so far within the framework of philanthropic help are no longer enough; firm positions must be found for the broad Jewish masses.
One of the most important positions is — work for Jews. The deep-rooted false notion that Jews are incapable of work must be eradicated. The best answer to it has been given by the Polish Zinc Works in Będzin, where a large number of Jewish workers are employed, with whose work the management of the factory is highly satisfied. Moreover, I heard something from my esteemed friend, the well-known philanthropist, director R' Szymon Fürstenberg (may he live long), which ought to be a moral lesson for all Jewish manufacturers, also outside Zagłębie: that they should change their tactics up to now — to give Jews alms and the work — to non-Jews...
Mr. Fürstenberg's great deed consists in the following: in the present hard time there are [printed "undertetter" — doubtful word] Jews who are ready to do the hardest work, but one thing hinders them — the Sabbath. They are ready to go hungry with their families, so long as they do not violate the holiness of the Sabbath. For this reason I turned to the director, Mr. S. Fürstenberg, with the request that the Jews working in his zinc factory should not be forced to work on the Sabbath.
My request met with no difficulty whatsoever. In my presence an order was given to the factory manager to grant equal rights to the Jewish workers who do not want to work on the Sabbath. I therefore express to him in this way my heartiest thanks and "yasher koach".
So, the beginning has been made; now a further step must be taken. The Jewish feeling of compassion must awaken among our employers, mindful of the saying: "Whoever sustains one soul of Israel, it is as if he sustained a whole world; and some acquire their world in a single hour." It is a matter of saving Jewish souls from death by hunger — "give bread to the hungry". Employ Jewish hands, with which you will be satisfied, and at the same time you will sustain Jewish livelihoods.
Respectfully,
Mendel Rosensaft.
P.S. I am ready at every call to work for the good of the cause, and I ask those interested to come to an understanding with me about it. The above.

Resolution of House-Owners in Zawiercie to Abolish Tenant Protection.
On Sunday a meeting of house-owners took place in Zawiercie in connection with the new law on a moratorium on the dwellings of the unemployed. At the meeting, attended by 1500 people, speeches were made by the deputy Mrs. Peplowka[?], advocate Kosto[—] of Sosnowiec and others.
The resolutions state that the government should be approached to abolish tenant protection and to restore the level of rents according to their pre-war value.

An Old Man Run Over and Killed.
On Tuesday evening on Piłsudski Street in Katowice the 69-year-old Adamczyk was run over by a car; he died on the way to the hospital. The driver has been arrested.

A Reception for the Italian Guests.
The Italian delegation of the "War Volunteers" association was received in Katowice with ceremony.
Representatives of the authorities and of municipal and public institutions took part in the reception.
When the train with the guests arrived at the station an orchestra played the Italian and Polish anthems, and they were greeted by the vice-voivode and the school inspector.

Died on the Train.
While travelling on the train from Mysłowice to Katowice the 67-year-old Mrs. Rabsztyn of Mysłowice died of a heart attack.

The Situation in Industry Is Worsening.
The series of reductions[?] in Upper Silesian industry does not stop. This week the "PAT" [Polish Telegraphic Agency] announced that a large number of workers are being laid off from the "Królewska" steelworks.
In this connection the Chief Labour Inspector, Mr. Golat[?], received in Warsaw a delegation which described the present situation in Upper Silesia.
Mr. Golat declared in reply that the main blame lies with the former director of the works, who did not take the trouble to obtain government orders.

From the Sports Movement

[Sport — Zagłębie.]
“Hakoach” — “Zagłębie” 1:3.
On Thursday a championship match between “Hakoach” and “Zagłębie” took place on the “Hakoach” ground.
The match was an interesting one and showed how much it matters when the Hakoach players go out onto the field to play with ambition.
Play such as “Hakoach” played in the second half has not been seen in Będzin for a long time, and it will long remain in the memory of the supporters. Motl Rozen distinguished himself better as a half-back than as a forward.
The game is opened by “Zagłębie”, which carries out continuous fine attacks on Hakoach’s goal. During this time the “Hakoach” defence has a great deal of work, from which it emerges victorious. Nussberg in goal distinguishes himself with his calm and his good positioning. Several counter-attacks by “Hakoach” are beaten back [?] by the good defence of “Zagłębie”. In the 25th minute Adamen [?] of “Zagłębie” succeeds in shooting a goal from 10 metres. A great share of the blame for this lies with the half-back line, which did not cover the player well. In the 33rd [?] minute the referee sends off, for brutal [?] play, the half-right of “Zagłębie” and... Engbergen [?] from the goal. His place is taken by Yankelevitsh 2.
After half-time “Hakoach” sets energetically to work and for the whole time does not leave the opponents’ goal. In the 20th minute Gutman shoots the equalising goal. This gives still more courage to the Hakoach players, who do not leave the opponents’ goal. In the 25th minute Gutman shoots the second goal. Soon afterwards Hampel shoots the third and at the same time the finest goal. Referee Mazur — not bad.
“Hakoach” — “Unia” 2:1 (1:1)
The game is opened by “Unia”, which carries out one attack after another; already in the 5th minute Margala [?] shoots into the right side and “Unia” leads 1:0. The goal was hard to stop. “Hakoach” carries out several attacks, but because of the shouting of their own players they do not know to whom to pass the ball, and they would sooner give the ball away to the opponent.
In the 30th minute the referee awards a free kick against Unia. Motl Rozen kicks. The Unia goalkeeper catches the ball and falls with it into the goal. 1:1.
“Unia” carries out a fine attack and from 20 metres the half-left gives a fine shot at the “Hakoach” goal, which, however, is held even more finely by Nussberg.
After half-time “Hakoach” has another opponent, namely the wind, against which the Hakoach players are physically a little too weak. The guests have the upper hand the whole time, and from a fine combination the half-right shoots the second and last goal.
The best on the field: Rozen 2. The weakest: Kokotek [?]. Referee Biecki [?] — good.
“Kraft” [?] — “Unia” [?] 2:1
According to the course of the game “Kraft” [?] should have won by a bigger score, but the unusual failure hindered them in this. Both goals were achieved from “eleven-metre” kicks (penalties).
“Hakoach” II — “Unia” II 3:1
In the “Hakoach” team the old, well-known Itsek Abramovitsh played in goal, and he distinguished himself quite well in his first debut.
“Maccabi” (Sosnowiec) — Ts.K.S. 1:2
