Pasekh-Shin: I'm Renting a Dacha...

My wife says to me this week — Mendel, what will be the end of it?
— A proper end indeed — I answer, woe and alas to us, the shop is empty, the sequestrator [tax distrainer] is shaking us and the creditors are pestering.
— Always the same answer, Mendel — my beautiful Beyle makes a sour face — I'm already sick of hearing it. Better think, my gold-spinner, about something like a dacha [summer cottage] for the children.
— What are you talking about, woman — I'm already beside myself — who thinks about a dacha today, it's a sin even to utter it; today one thanks God that one is allowed to sit at home, and altogether, I say, it's a completely superfluous thing today.
Here in Będzin, to this very day, the air [powietrze] is nothing to sin against either.
Look, I say, what a quiet, what a calm has set in. The machines don't pound, the chimneys don't smoke, the “dragnove” [?] wagons don't move, and even the “zhimne d...” [?] no longer gives off its bad smells.
So why, I say, must one travel abroad, when here we have everything right behind our nose. —
And if, I say, there was still one factory with its harmful smoke, they shut it down too, just to ease and sweeten our life, and the woman goes around with such sinful thoughts.
Having heard out my answer, mine says with a little smile: — Well, and our five grown-up daughters, have you forgotten them already?
— A parable for a “sarbe flekker” [?] — I answer — our daughters can pass their test [?] here too. The Górka [the hill] and the music can still do for them, and if that's too little for them, they'll find it also in the dark alleys on the Małobądz road.
Oy, what a gentleman — my beautiful Beyle bristles [?] — a man who wants to know of nothing, who understands nothing in women's matters; have you read the paper?
— Yes, what?
— Didn't you notice anything?
— What is there to notice? — I ask — today's papers, so to speak [?] — all Hitler, von Papen, reparations and stagnation...
— There's a man for you — my beautiful Beyle laughs — what good is your Hitler to me; did you read about “Reitshe” [?]?
Hush, what, has somebody drowned there again, God forbid?
— Listen, Mendel, you're a fool, no offence [?], “Reitshe” is now becoming a “first-class resort”. There will be a beach [plaża] with playgrounds, with music and with all good things; well, do you understand now?
I don't begin to understand, I say; if it's about a bath, I say, the kehilla bath is more worthy. There it's both cold and warm — and as for music, I say, I forgo it, it plays enough in my head already... You see, if one could arrange some little livelihood there — why not..
— There's a man for you — mine has already got angry — he thinks only about himself, while he has 5 grown-up daughters whom one could already put all under the wedding canopy on a single day; about that he is hardly moved —
— But tell me, woman, how can the dacha help them?
It can help them a great deal, you should know that today's young men like girls much better on the beach in bathing costumes than dressed — and by the way, such “Venetian nights” take place there, that is, people amuse themselves whole nights, music plays, couples dance, and you understand that in such cases it can happen that our daughters catch their true match..
— Well, if so, I say, if in our times there are still such “fentakes” [?] who can let themselves be veiled [led to the wedding], maybe you're right, women really are more practical in this respect; but tell me, where will we take the “sweets” [the money]?
— God will help, Mendele, today dachas are going for half-nothing, food there is also cheap; here, I'll make you a calculation: socks, shoes, dresses, blouses one doesn't need, the daughters will lie whole days in their bathing costumes on the beach. Now [?], instead of wood we'll heat with pine cones from the forest.
Berries and sorrel [szczaw] we'll pick ourselves; chives [szczypior], radishes and other vegetables the peasant of the dacha will give; poultry we'll raise ourselves, set a brooding hen on eggs, and you've got a ready livelihood.
Then you'll already be provided with meat, and “fire” [?] is left over; the bit of dry bread one takes on credit — you should have seen, Mendel, my crown, what greasy ledgers the bakers have... with them everything's on the book...
Well, and pay for the dacha? I still don't give in.
— See how a man can't find any way out: go into the Rescue Committee and take the loan, not too bad, they can give; [?] their loss on us has been promised [?]. Remember, Mendel, when one has grown-up daughters one must gird oneself well, and by the way, one must do it not only for oneself but for the other. May our enemies burst and split..
In short, why should I chew it over with you at length — the wife talked me round, and I'm already getting ready, with good luck, to rent a dacha...
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Behaalotcha)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Behaalotcha
The Portion
—o—
a) "And this was the work of the menorah" (Num. 8:4)
In the books it is said about this: "Moses had difficulty with the making of the menorah." The question arises: why could Moses not understand the making of the menorah? Is it so incomprehensible?
The menorah had to be entirely of beaten work, hewn out of one piece of gold. The cups, the flowers, the knops — everything had to be of one piece. Therefore it is a symbol of Jewish unity: both the flowers of the people and the scantier parts must be cast together.
That is what Moses did not understand: is it really possible that Jews, too, should be cast together like that? Is it really possible among our Jews?... Imrei Shefer.
—o—
b) "And Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families" (Num. 11:10)
The rich man dresses more finely than the poor man not only because he wants to look finer; he eats better than him not only because he wants to eat better, but also because he wants to eat differently from the poor man, to dress differently from him... It is a psychological truth.
The manna, as is well known, contained every taste one wished to feel. Well, so the poor man could also allow himself the taste of a turkey and the like. That is what the rich wept over, "concerning family matters" ("ʿalei" as printed). The vanished difference between poor and rich — everyone eats alike — that the rich could not bear...
Ahavat Yehonatan.
• • •
"Concerning family matters."
They wept over the prohibition of brothers marrying sisters and other relatives. They wept because they knew that with it the dowry misfortune begins... Had brothers and sisters been allowed to marry, there would have been no dowry problem — with the marriage prohibition of close relatives the dowry misfortune began, and that is why they burst into such weeping...
Ohel Yaakov (the Dubno Maggid).
• • •
When the marriage law was given, the Jews wept and quarrelled. That is why no wedding passes without quarrels and tears. Talmud (Shabbat, 130).
—o—
c) "As a nursing father carries the sucking child" (ibid., 12)
A nanny bends down over the child and lifts it up to herself. If she does not bend down, she will harm the child while lifting it. If, again, she stays bent over the child, she will get a hunchback...
And so too a leader: he must bend down to the people for a while — and only for a while — and lift them up straight away. Yalkut Peninim.
—o—
d) "And Joshua [printed: Yehoshiya] the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, answered" (ibid., 28)
A characteristic saying on this by Rabbi Yosef Shaul Nathansohn in his "Divrei Shaul":
"In our times, too, some pass themselves off as saints and pure ones; although once one had to go through many mortifications and fasts until one reached the level of a Hasid, today one becomes a rebbe overnight"...
That is why Joshua, Moses' servant, was so angry when he saw that Eldad [printed: Eldar] and Medad became prophets overnight, for he had indeed seen how hard his master Moses had worked to be worthy of the title...
—o—
e) "Would that all the Lord's people were prophets" (ibid., 29)
The Rebbe of Sobota [?] once told R' Yehoshuale of Kutno, in the name of [?] Rebbe Elimelech of blessed memory, that in the future, when "the earth shall be full of knowledge", every Jew will be like a rebbe: pious, possessing the holy spirit; and with that the rebbe concluded with the verse: "Would that all the Lord's people were prophets."
Whereupon the Kutno rav, something of a Misnaged, caught him up: "u-mi yiten" — and who will GIVE? Who will give a pidyon [the payment to a rebbe], "all the Lord's people prophets", if all Jews are rebbes?...
————
One Hasid asks another:
— Supposing there were no money at all, what would people give the rebbes as a pidyon?
He replies:
— Fool, if there were no money, there would be no rebbes either... A Misnaged anecdote.
—o—
f) "And Moses withdrew into the camp, he [printed: "she"] and the elders of Israel" (ibid., 30)
A calamity was about to come here because of the people's rebellion, so "And Moses withdrew into the camp" — Moses mingled with the camp: if there is to be trouble, let us all suffer... (see Rashi; in the Sifrei an opposite interpretation [?]). Likkutim Hadashim.
—o—
g) "For you have wept in the ears of the Lord" (ibid., 18)
God's vexation is not because you want meat, but because you say "for it was well with us in Egypt": the fish and onions of Egypt you remember, but the lashes and the blood — not...
Kiflayim le-Tushiya.
—o—
The Haftarah
h) "And Satan standing at his right hand" (Zechariah 2 [should be 3])
Yes, Satan often stands on the right... eyes piously rolled up, pious words on his lips — but although he stands "at his right hand", he is Satan..!
Shaar Bat Rabbim.
—o—
Avot
i) "Torah study is good together with [printed: "if"] worldly occupation" (ch. 2:2)
It is good that during worldly occupation — while he is trading — he should study; that is: he should trade honestly, not steal, not tell lies, so that his trade becomes Torah study...
Kedushat Levi.
—o—
j) "Not everyone who engages much in trade becomes wise" (ibid., 6)
"Not everyone" — do not all who engage much in trade become wise?
— It is not about becoming wise, but about "makes wise" — making others wise, who look at them and become wise from it, take a moral lesson from them... Tzafenat Paneah.
—o—
Me and Kaiser Wilhelm.
(A short feuilleton.)
Who am I and who is Kaiser Wilhelm?
I am a writer for a newspaper in the Jewish language [Yiddish], dependent on only a Jew reading me.
Kaiser Wilhelm is, even in writing, my "colleague"; he has already written and printed many books, but when he writes something [?] the whole world reads it.
A very small analogy even exists in the fact that I am in exile and he is in exile. But even the exile — for the two of us — is not the same.
Kaiser Wilhelm sits, after all, in Doorn under his vine and under his fig tree. From Germany he receives a very large pension a year; besides that he has estates, factories and brickworks in Germany, which bring in very large revenues — and never will anyone say that Kaiser Wilhelm has nothing for the Sabbath — — whereas with me...
And if one wants to reckon up lineage — there is likewise no comparison at all.
My grandfather — may his merit protect us — was a little rebbe in a small shtetl, small and dried up like Rabbi Zadok's fig. He fasted all the fasts, mortifications and purifications, fasted perhaps twelve "pyatiletkas" [five-year plans] in his life, and died in borrowed shrouds.
Wilhelm's grandfather, Frederick the Great, certainly fasted no fasts and ate meat even on the Christian fast days.
My grandfather certainly never had a stray thought — and Frederick the Great — certainly did...
My grandmother Rachele, peace be upon her, was a modest and pious woman — and about his grandmother I have my doubts...
Therefore I say:
I believe with perfect faith that Jewish blood flows in my veins...
But.
When Prince Joachim of Prussia, Wilhelm's uncle, now shouts to the whole world that Jewish blood flows in Kaiser Wilhelm's veins, that really is a sensation...
I am very curious to know who the Jew was and what the fellow's name was... Piuhach [?].
—o—
48 hours alive under rubble.
In a village near Ogrodzieniec the following incident occurred: a peasant from the village was digging in a well 45 metres deep. At a certain moment a wall in the well burst, and stones and sand buried the peasant who was there. Hundreds of people took part in the swift rescue, and after 48 hours they succeeded in getting the peasant out of the rubble.
It took 15 minutes before the peasant could utter a word.
Rasputin and His Jewish Beloved (30)

[Serialized historical novel — Russia, Grigori Rasputin; installment 30.]
A historical novel by Boris Maksimov.

Most of the inhabitants of the monastery belonged to the sect of the "People of God" [the Khlysty], who did not believe in the rules of the Orthodox cloister.

Little by little Rasputin learned about the teaching of the sect, which preached that the customs, prayers and other rites of the cloister are needed only by simple people, by lowly creatures who are far from understanding God's ways; that the cloister with its high priests had not found the way that leads to God, and that only the "prophet" of the secret sect is able to show his followers the true way to God. For: the Orthodox cling like steel and iron to the written word, and the written word is a dead thing. The "prophet" of the sect, however, receives his inspiration directly from God Himself... The man who has come close to God and is bound up with the "Holy Spirit" — that man no longer needs the rites and forms of the "Holy Scriptures", which were written by men... He no longer has to obey them..

The sectarians told Rasputin that Danila Filippovich [printed "Filipitsh"], the founder of the sect, had at first also believed in the "Holy Scriptures", but later, when God's grace descended upon him and he came close to the "Holy Spirit", he gathered up all the "holy" books, threw them into the Volga (a river) and said:

"Not in the dead letters of the books can one find the way to God.. The way to God man must seek only in the 'golden book of life'..."

According to the teaching of this sect it follows that every man who lives on earth is able, at any time and in any place, to unite with God, and God's spirit will descend and settle in that man. The birth of Jesus, of the "Son of God", who became a man, did not happen only once — it happens every time.

But in order for man to unite with God, the sinful man must first die the "mysterious death", after which comes the "mysterious rebirth". One can die the "mysterious death" through absolute self-denial and complete submission to the will of the "Holy Spirit", suppressing every lust within oneself, for the "mysterious rebirth" is possible only when the man has completely overcome every sin within himself. The man who has gone through the "mysterious rebirth" — he can perform miracles, can heal the sick and can make everything happen exactly as he demands. He can do this through the power of the "Holy Spirit" that dwells in him. He can bring the dead to life, he has the power to punish and to redeem, to save sinners from Gehenna and lead them into Paradise. He becomes a new creature, which is God and man together...

Such a man may do anything his heart desires; his sins are no sins, for he is, after all, always inspired by the spirit of God. When such a man does the ugliest things, the vilest sins, it is more pleasing to God than the best deeds done by an ordinary man. He who has gone through the "mysterious death" and the "mysterious rebirth" stands above all laws.

Rasputin was inspired by this faith and became a devoted sectarian. In this teaching he found everything he had dreamed of since his early childhood. If only he could succeed in uniting with God, in going through the "mysterious death" and the "mysterious rebirth", then he could do anything his heart desired. He could sin as much as he wanted and it would be no sin. Everything he did would, after all, be done with the consent of the "Holy Spirit" and would be counted by God as good deeds. And Rasputin began to long for one thing only: to unite with God and become an exalted man, according to the teaching of the sect of the "People of God".

Rasputin spent a long time in the monastery. Before he left the monastery he decided to visit the holy "starets" Makary, who lived in a hut in the forest not very far from the monastery; none of the monks left the monastery without first visiting the "holy" Makary and receiving a blessing from him...

The "starets" Makary was famous [?] throughout all Russia. Men and women of various classes and estates, from near and far, came to the "starets" Makary to pour out their hearts before him and tell him of their sufferings. People went to him from all sides; for days on end they wandered through fields and forests, barefoot and bareheaded [?] they went, with a bread-sack on the shoulder and a wanderer's staff in hand they trudged to him — and no one left his hut without a kind word, a consolation or good advice.

From his secret "brethren" Rasputin learned that the pious [?] "starets" Makary had once lived a sinful, dissolute life. He had denied himself no lust, had tasted every kind of debauchery and had renounced no pleasure whatsoever. He had been a great sinner, had spent his life in the wildest orgies, had raped women, defiled girls, and so he had lived until not a drop of sin remained in his blood. When he had already sinned out all his sins and had become purified, and no lust at all remained in him any more, he devoted himself entirely, with all his senses and with a purified heart, to God...

(To be continued).
When Did Jews Get the First Cemetery in Saxony?

Specially for our newspaper, by Z. Haber.

Exactly two hundred years ago, in the year 1732, the few Jews who then lived in Saxony began to petition the local king for a Jewish cemetery of their own.
In the archives of the Leipzig Fair Office (Messamt) there is much interesting material, which deserves to be passed on.

If a Jew died at the Leipzig fair or on the way, the dead man had to be carried across the German border to Bohemia or even to Poland. In Germany one was not allowed to bury him.

As early as December 1715 Bernard Lehmann [Behrend Lehmann], the greatest communal leader of that time, received permission from King August to bury Jewish dead in his garden, but barely two months later the permission was withdrawn, because the Protestant clergy would not allow ceremonies to be held at Jewish funerals, arguing that if this were permitted to the Jews, the Catholics would also demand a cemetery of their own; so the Jews were again forbidden to bury their dead..

Nevertheless the Catholics — at the request of the Austrian Empress Maria Theresa — received their own cemetery in 1719, and the Jews had to wait until the year 1751.

In the year 1732, when several Jews had permission to live in Leipzig a few weeks before the fair and a few weeks after the fair, they had to bury several dead. While they were being carried across the border, there occurred, God forbid, an accident: the wagon overturned while driving uphill [?] and the dead man was left lying in the mud. Then the Jew Michel Samuel, in the name of the privileged Jews, petitioned the king, pointing to the disgrace for the living and still more for the dead; he asked, "like our father Abraham", that the Jews be granted a plot outside the city "about a hundred ells long and a hundred ells wide, where they could bury their dead".

For this plot he undertook in the name of the Jews to pay "in two instalments" three hundred thalers, although "it is not possible to collect such a large sum"; in addition they would pay thirty thalers in taxes every year.
For twelve years the request went from one office to another. At first they did not even want to hear of it; later no suitable place was found, because around the city the king had to go hunting with the noblemen, and those places could not be given up for a Jewish cemetery.

Later, when a place had been found, it did not suit the Jews, because they wanted to have a river nearby, where they would have water for the ritual purification [of the dead].
Then they began to bargain over the price: the government demanded a thousand thalers to be paid at once, and in addition 15 thalers for every dead person for the Protestant church fund (5 thalers for a child).
With great effort the Jews collected 600 thalers, but the government insisted on a thousand thalers. Again it took a long time until the Jews who used to come to the Leipzig fairs contributed and borrowed the remaining 400 thalers. These thousand thalers brought the Jews into great debts, which they paid off only in the year 1786.

Only in the year 1751 did they receive the plot, far from the city, on condition that they employ a Christian "gravedigger"; in addition they must "perform the ceremonies at the holy place and not in the city".

This permission was granted on 23 February 1751 to the Jews Yitzchak Meir, Michel Samuel, Ephraim Levi, Aharon Shlomo Israel and Shimon Bando, after they had deposited the thousand thalers "for themselves and their families"...
And already on 25 April 1751 the wife of Yitzchak Meyer was buried there, and a Russian Jew, Baruch Mordechai, who had come to the fair in Leipzig and died there.
On this Jew a hundred thalers were found, which were kept in the "Jewish fund", then established, as burial money...

The "Jewish fund" afterwards took high burial fees for every foreign dead person, because they argued that only the Jews who lived there had received the privileges... Only in the year 1804 was the cemetery opened to all Jews without fees.
In the meantime the government withdrew its permission for the Jewish cemetery. The government argued that the plot had only been leased to the Jews, not sold, and could therefore be taken back any day.
For years the Jews litigated, and only in the year 1794 was the verdict issued that the Jews had bought the cemetery plot and that it belonged to them for all generations...
To the Public of the Jewish Population of Będzin!

In the pre-Shavuot issue of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" a great many respected householders protested against the machinations being carried out in smuggling in 2 "freshly baked" little shochtim [ritual slaughterers]; it was also told there that when a larger number of householders were at the Rabbi's and claimed the right of R' Yechezkel, may his light shine, son of R' Mordechai, shochet and examiner of blessed memory, demanding a din Torah [rabbinic court hearing], the Rabbi said that "he has no din Torah, and R' Yechezkel will not be a shochet in Będzin", and when the householders demanded a reason for it, the Rabbi said... thus I decree! I have a reason for it...

It has surely greatly interested a large part of the local Jewish population what could be the reason for the Rabbi's decree, but at last the cat [?] is out of the bag... for, as one hears, it smells of... bribery: namely, the 2 freshly baked little shochtim are paying a large sum of dollars, which is divided up, "the great according to his greatness and the small according to his smallness", and that is the true reason for the decree; this also explains the words the Rabbi said at the time to 2 local householders about the same matter: "Nowadays, when one takes on a shochet, one has to give... a 'dray' [?]; without a 'dray' it doesn't work".

Jews of Będzin! Such deceitful deeds must not be tolerated — that a rabbi should say he has no din Torah, and that communal matters should be settled with the help of bribery. And although now is a time when, because of the crisis, nobody has the courage to raise his voice even when great injustices are done, we must not allow [anyone] to trample on the heads of the holy people!

A group of Będzin householders.

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Presidium Elections to the Kehilla Board and Council for the Third Time

[Head of the local page; Będzin — Kehilla.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 20 Sivan 5692 — piątek 24 czerwca 1932 [Friday, 24 June 1932].)
Będzin
For the third time presidium elections to the kehilla board and council.
Sunday — new elections.
In the last issue of our paper we had only just reported the result of the presidium elections of the kehilla board. But barely 8 days have passed and once again a new change has come about.
Last Monday the starosta [district head] notified the kehilla board that, since the presidium elections of the council and of the board took place in contravention of the law, the elections are annulled.
At the same time it is ordered that by the 30th of this month the presidium elections of both bodies, the council and the board, must take place.
On the basis of the order, the members of the council and of the board are called to meetings, which will take place next Sunday at 11 in the morning, for the purpose of electing the ordered presidiums.
As is known, the kehilla council had already for the second time elected Mr. Icchak Wygodzki as chairman. But now this candidate no longer comes into consideration, because the board includes the person of Eli Ber Werdiger, and Mr. Wygodzki, who is Werdiger's son-in-law, may not be a member of the council.
As we learn, the "Agudah" has already worked out a plan for disqualifying, on grounds of kinship, the person of Mr. Buchweitz as a member of the board.
The plan is this: the parnas Silberfreund resigns his mandate and in his place Mr. Berisz Liwer enters.
The latter is also to resign, and then into his place will enter the parnas Mr. Icze Majer Szenberg, who by force of law will push his son-in-law, Mr. Buchweitz, out of the board...
In short, a series of new elections is beginning, just so that the Jews will have something to keep them busy during the cucumber season [the slow summer season].
On the Day of the Wedding the Groom Went Off to a Match

[Będzin — A wedding that did not take place.]
The next day the bride's side says "hashivenu nazad" ["bring us back" — Hebrew hashivenu plus Polish nazad, "back"]...
Last Sunday the following interesting story took place in our town.
On Zawale Street a wedding was [to] take place; the groom is from Będzin, the bride — from L. The dowry of 4,000 zł. was to be paid off by the bride's side before the wedding. But for [various] reasons the whole sum was not available in cash, and the bride's father offered to give 3,000[?] zł. and to give a guarantee for the remainder.
On Sunday, the day of the wedding, the bride and the in-laws from L. came to Będzin, where the wedding was supposed to take place. But the groom, having been egged on by his intimates to declare a "strike" over the 4th thousand zł., went off to the match that took place that same day.
When they set about the wedding preparations, they realised that the groom was not there; a search began through the whole town, but "the lad is gone" — the bird had vanished. The bride's side, in a desperate state, went up to the rabbi and raised a great outcry: is it possible? To shame a Jewish daughter on her wedding day? How can this be allowed? A new search began; the beadles of the rabbinate also rolled up their coat-tails, but the clock had already struck 12 and the "jewel" was not found...
One can easily imagine what scenes played out among the in-laws of the bride's side; the whole celebration was turned into mourning, which dragged on into broad daylight...
The next day, when the groom's side realised what they had done, they repented and sent messengers to the bride that they now agreed that the wedding should take place without the 4th thousand... But the bride said — no. A groom — she says — who runs away on his wedding day over money, she does not want to marry.
And so indeed it was: the bride and all the in-laws travelled back home, and
— the groom goes around as a "denounced one"[?]...

[Będzin — Attempted suicide.]
On Monday afternoon the 22-year-old Sztaka[?] threw herself under a passenger train, which cut off the suicide's left foot and severely injured her whole body.
The cause of the drama is as follows:

The New School Building for Jewish Children Has Also Been "Eyed"

[Będzin — Education.]
As we have already reported, the commissioner of the magistrate (municipality) decided to liquidate the school premises in the town for Jewish children who study in the public (powszechne) schools; the premises are to be rented out, and with the rent money school premises are to be rented for non-Jewish children in Koszelew and Grzychów. But, as we are informed, the present management of the magistrate is not yet content with the school premises, but has also cast an "eye" on the new school building of School No. 2. Several rooms of that school are to be taken over, in which courses for non-Jewish children are to be held.
The question of liquidating the municipal school premises for the Jewish children has aroused strong indignation among the many Jewish parents, from whom the magistrate has colossal revenues. The "Merchants' Association", the "Small Traders" and the "Artisans' Association" should also take a stand on the great injustice that the magistrate is committing against Jewish children.
Jewish Children to the Summer Colony

[Będzin — Children.]
Next Thursday the first group of schoolchildren, numbering 170 girls, leaves for Sławków, for the summer colony of the magistrate (municipality).
— The parents of the boys who have been approved to go to the colony are reminded that next Sunday is the last date for paying the fixed fee at Public School No. 2.
General Report Meeting

[Będzin — Artisans.]
Under the chairmanship of the president, Mr. Ch. D. Grossman, a report meeting of the Artisans' Association was held on Saturday on Modrzejowska Street.
Messrs. Zerach Lemberg and Note Weller were invited to the presidium as representatives of the bakers' section, which has been created within the association.
The chairman gives a report on the work of the delegation in Kielce, where a memorandum with a series of demands on behalf of the impoverished artisans was handed in.
Mr. Kleinman speaks about the committee to combat the illegal workshops and stresses that the artisans have good chances of obtaining cheap credits from the government, and that the director of the Chamber of Crafts has promised to intervene with the government so that means be found to combat unemployment among the craftsmen.
Small Traders Protest against a Project to Restrict Peddling

[Sosnowiec — Trade.]
In the hall of the "Hotel Polski" a general meeting of the local small traders was held on Sunday.
With 169 members present, the president, Mr. Aliner, opens the meeting. The chair is handed over to Mr. Yitzchak Dafner. As assessors: Noach Abramczyk, Yosef Grachowina, Hirsh Rozyner and Alter Majerowicz; secretary — Yosef Langer.
The report on the year's activity is given by Mr. Aliner, who says that the board has used every possibility for the benefit of the members.
Mr. Aliner reports on the question of the latest tax reductions [?], on the ryczałt (lump-sum tax), and informs about the question of granting credits to the small traders, etc.
Mr. Dwinski gives the treasury report and reads the draft budget for 1932/33 in the amount of 7,600 zł. After the reports a discussion developed, whose content consisted of "complaints simply into the world at large"...
Then the following protest resolutions are adopted: 1) against the high price of electricity and meters, 2) against the high fee for bringing in goods, 3) against the high fee for water and sewerage, and 4) against the project to restrict peddling in the country.

When Children Are Left Alone at Home..

[Czeladź — Fire.]
In Czeladź a family went out, leaving several small children in the house, who while playing set fire to the straw mattresses (sienniki), from which a fire broke out. Fortunately neighbours noticed it in time and managed to put out the fire.

A Policeman Comes to Break Up a Jewish Wedding

[Sosnowiec — police, wedding.]
In a house on First of May Street (ul. 1 Maja) in Zwonsza [?] a wedding took place in the evening [?]. After the chuppah couples began to dance, as a result of which [plaster] began to crumble from the ceiling (sufit) at the landlord's...
The landlord called a policeman, who, on entering the wedding hall and not knowing what was going on there, ordered the crowd to leave the premises...
Because of this the guests went to the landlord, and after the assurance that “there will be no more dancing”, the policeman left.

A Murder on the Beach in Mysłowice.

[Upper Silesia — crime; followed by seven news items: Będzin (Chofetz Chaim yeshiva, matura, School No. 8), Sosnowiec (Chamber of Commerce), Dąbrowa, Łazy, tobacco monopoly.]
On Wednesday evening at the "Stadium" in Mysłowice a lieutenant shot dead a Silesian, a certain Emil Winterstein.
The lieutenant has been arrested.
We are given the following details about the murder.
At 5 o'clock in the afternoon, in the restaurant at the stadium in Mysłowice, a group of officers of the 23rd Regiment from Będzin took a table. Opposite them sat a group of young people, sportsmen from Mysłowice and the surroundings; among the group was the sportsman Emil Winterstein of Mysłowice.
At a certain moment, as is reported, an insulting word fell from the youthful group addressed to the officers who were sitting opposite.
Later, at the bathing pool[?], a sharp incident arose over the insult between Second Lieutenant Kucharski and Winterstein; the incident, however, ended very tragically. Kucharski fired a revolver at Winterstein, who fell unconscious and died in hospital.
When a terrible panic broke out at the stadium and the agitation among the crowd grew strongly, the lieutenant then declared:
— I killed him, and I am responsible for what I have done.
—o—
"With Candles in Their Hands" They Searched for One Torah-True Jew at the Meeting on the Campaign for the "Chofetz Chaim's" Yeshiva.
As is known, a delegation of the Chofetz Chaim's yeshiva in Radun is staying in Będzin with the aim of carrying out a relief campaign.
About 60 persons were invited to the meeting, above all the element that enlists the great Gaon's help during an election campaign... But nobody came — apart from the kehilla president — not a single one...
The meeting also dealt with the question of permitting the rabbis to speak in the synagogue on behalf of the yeshiva. The president did not want to give the permission, arguing that "apart from the local rabbi nobody may speak in the synagogue".
Against this Mr. Buchheitz[?], who was present there[?], came out sharply; with a candle in his hand he searched under the table for at least one man of the "Agudah", which enlists the "Chofetz Chaim" for "political" victories...
After lengthy deliberation by the representatives of the rabbinate, the rabbis were permitted to speak in the synagogue on behalf of the yeshiva campaign.

Mr. Prezerowicz, Have You Forgotten the Verse "Ye Shall Not Afflict Any Widow or Stranger"?..
Mr. Israel Josef Jurkiewicz of Dąbrowa comes into the editorial office and relates: My mother, a poor widow, has been renting a flat for 20 years already in Prezerowicz's house in Dąbrowa. Because[?] I am now unemployed, my mother wants to pay 3 złoty a month as until March of this year. For this he inflicts severe torments on my mother and me; his household resorts to the lowest means, such as throwing vermin in through the window, smashing panes, threatening to inform on us, throwing themselves on us to beat us, etc.
— And where are the police? — we ask.
— The police — he says — have already drawn up reports. There will also be a trial, but until then our sufferings are unbearable. Why should we be tormented like this?
Besides the narrator, a second man from Dąbrowa also testifies; he reports terrible facts about the behaviour of Mr. Prezerowicz and his household towards the poor widow and her children.
— And you, Reb Josef Dawid! Have you really already forgotten that "ye shall not afflict any widow or orphan"? You are, after all, one of the "Torah-true".

An Assault by Teachers on the Director of the "Mizrachi" School in Będzin (Communiqué of the Board of Trustees and the Parents' Committee)

Jewish Będzin will no doubt be shaken by the news that the well-known scholar Dr. A. Gottesdiener was attacked in a corridor by the teachers Eisenberg, teachers of the Polish subjects at the school, who beat him murderously.
We truly do not know what to call the deed that has happened among us. One of the most famous and best-loved Jewish personalities of religious-national Jewry in Poland has been injured in such a hooligan manner because he wished to protect the honour of a Jewish school and to share in the Jewish troubles. Not many know what sufferings Dr. Gottesdiener went through during this school year at the "Mizrachi" school, how many sacrifices he made for the school and how many more he still wanted to make just to save its existence. With complete self-denial he cared [printed "gevargt", apparently a misprint] precisely for the teachers alone, and the reward for it is this baseless, vile and shameful deed.
Already in the middle of the winter Dr. Gottesdiener came with a proposal that he was ready to reduce his salary by 35 percent and the teachers should forgo 10 percent, in order to keep the school in existence, but his proposal was not accepted because the teachers would not agree to it. Now it was a matter of issuing the school certificates. Dr. Gottesdiener again proposed that he would commit himself [to give up] his pay for three months, provided the school year could be finished in good order. It was on this ground that the anger broke out. All the other teachers apart from the assailants did indeed declare that they are "outraged" (?) over the affair — in theory; but in practice the "Związek" [the teachers' union] goes on protecting the interests of the brothers Eisenberg. Dr. Gottesdiener will keep his word — the Jewish children will not suffer for Jewish need and poverty; to be beaten up — that is the lot of all who are true leaders and lovers of the people. Finally, a few words to the man who was beaten: — Hon. [?] Dr. Gottesdiener! We know your heart, which burns with love of Israel; we know that you, with your truly humble soul, feel joyful that you took the blows for the sake of the troubles of Israel. But not you alone — all of us, we, the Jewish public of Będzin, to whom you gave so much spiritual pleasure during the winter, and we assure you that we will use every means to respond to the insult done to you.
With respect,
The Board of Trustees and all the parents of the "Mizrachi" school in Będzin.
Results of Sunday's Town Council Elections in Wolbrom

About 10 months ago town council elections took place in Wolbrom, which then produced a Jewish majority — 13 Jews and 11 Christians. Naturally, a Christian mayor was elected — but a Jewish deputy mayor with two ławniks [members of the town executive] was elected too; this did not please the local Christian population — especially the antisemites so well known to us. A trifle — that in Poland a town council should be Judaized like that? There is simply a lurking danger that soon one would have to come to a Jew for him to give a Christian a "ślub" [wedding ceremony]! With such old wives' tales they indeed fed the undeveloped Christian population of Wolbrom. Only when the Christian mayor was suspended from his rights for judicial reasons did the fear grow even greater — a Jew is going to run the town?... Thereupon all the Christian councillors resigned.
"Self-evidently", new elections were "immediately" approved, and they did take place on Sunday the 20th [?] of June this year.
The election campaign on the Christian street was steeped in the vilest antisemitic poison; one publication, which had already gone beyond all measure in its antisemitism, was indeed confiscated by the local commandant (naturally, after it had been distributed...). The editor of the publication, a Christian, is known there by the name "Soyfer" [scribe]; he used to deal in Torah scrolls — stolen ones, of course — and indeed had legal troubles for it, but that does not stop one from riding the antisemitic hobby-horse. And so the Christian street went to the ballot box concentrated and with 100-percent participation.
On the Jewish street ambition took over and a miracle happened: Agudah, the Zionists and the artisans formed a bloc — but these are our brethren after all... The Pińczów Hasidim were not satisfied, and neither were the Aleksandrów Hasidim, headed by Mr. Tarla. Thanks to the 3 Jewish lists the Jewish bourgeois street indeed lost a mandate.
On the Jewish proletarian street, too, the bloc did not come about, owing to the distribution of mandates, and so 2 Jewish proletarian mandates were lost.
The new council is now made up with a majority of 10 against 14, which is far from matching the proportion.
The result is: list 1 "Bund" 139 votes, no mandate; list 6 Left Poale Zion 197 votes, 1 mandate; list 7 Right Poale Zion 103 votes, no mandate; list 10 Aleksandrów Hasidim 476 votes, 3 mandates; list 11 Pińczów Hasidim 92 votes, no mandate; list 12 United Bloc 893 votes, 6 mandates.
It is worth noting that 96 per cent of those entitled to vote took part in the elections.
Yosef V—s.
