On Guard Against a Catastrophe

[Essay — economy, the Jews of Poland and the crisis; series, part XIII.] By L. Szpigelman.
(XIII) World crisis and Jewish crisis. — Existence and downfall. — What force can save the situation?
If the crisis has engulfed various countries and continents, if the economic situation has become unexpectedly catastrophic — it has above all found an echo here in Poland, and first and foremost among us Jews.
True, all citizens of the country suffer from the crisis; the machines and the factories have long since rusted, and as time goes on more enterprises are liquidated, so that this increases unemployment. But be that as it may, there poverty does not yet strike [?] as hard as with us. Thus, for example, when officials are dismissed from a factory, a certain time passes and they manage to obtain a government post — something which for us Jews is out of the question; we cannot even dream of such a thing, in spite of the fact that we have all civil rights in the country. Besides, the Jewish community in Poland finds itself in entirely different circumstances.
Of what elements does the Jewish population in Poland consist? Altogether it can be divided into two parts: merchants and artisans — that is all. If we break these elements down, it will turn out that among the merchants there are also petty traders, so that at a critical time the two categories can be mixed together, and among the artisans there are also small industrialists, who are likewise at present in one and the same situation. What sort of industrialist can he be, when he has had to dismiss his people and has stood himself at the workbench; he can barely still count himself among the fortunate ones, and he has to do the work himself when there is any. Is that not simply a plain worker? So we have nothing more than merchants and workers as the bulk of the Jewish population in Poland. True, there are a few officials, workers and big industrialists, but they are such a minority that as such they do not come into consideration at all.
Moreover [printed "אין דעריבער"], when factories are liquidated, when workers and officials lose their posts, they pay no taxes; the housing question, too, does not arise for them, because for the most part they live in the factory houses, and as unemployed they also receive support from the existing bodies, which help them out a little in a time of trouble.
Quite different is the situation with us Jews. We are, after all, merchants and artisans. Our merchant is never unemployed — even though he may be able to sleep for several days and nights on end in his shop. Hardly has he opened it, and he carries all the civic obligations on his shoulders. The same is true of the artisans or small industrialists: they cannot hang locks on their enterprises, because, first, many of them are located together with their private dwellings, and secondly, even if not, they think to themselves: it is enough that we have no people. Perhaps, when some piece of work does come along, one is able to carry it out oneself; and therefore this category, too, does not count as unemployed, so that the tax screw keeps on squeezing him. And we know, after all, that the greatest share of the taxes is loaded onto the urban population.
Thus, for example, we know that many enterprises have had to liquidate because of the large tax obligations that weighed on their shoulders. Had they been able to free themselves of these taxes, they could still somehow have run their businesses; and so they went off the stage, lost their credit and the confidence, and had nowhere to draw their livelihood from.
But if we think that this has already come to a halt, that it already belongs to the past, we are greatly mistaken. It is an epidemic that keeps on spreading. It has, unfortunately, reached the stage where there are firms which we think are still healthy, iron-solid, sturdy — while inside everything is already tottering. When the root is already rotten, and it goes without saying that such a firm still pays the high taxes, and at the "urząd" [the tax office] they think it can still conquer the world, and there they reckon that however much it is burdened, one may presume it is too little, that it is cheating its way out.
And therefore the Jewish merchant and small trader in Poland finds himself in quite different conditions from the non-Jew. The Jew remains burdened with his taxes, which he is in no position to pay; moreover, he has no possibility of reducing his budget, because if he lives in town he must pay rent, electricity, water and everything a living person needs. That foodstuffs cost him less could indeed have saved the situation, if only he were earning, if only he saw a live groschen before his eyes. But that is the trouble [printed "אין" for "איז"]: he neither earns nor has the possibility of earning. For, let us say, the merchant could for once actually sell something — he has no goods, because on a bill of exchange he gets nothing, and a bank where he could have a bill discounted he does not have either; so that with the best will in the world he is frozen [?].
Roughly the same applies to the artisan, the craftsman, the small industrialist: none of them receives on credit the products they need. So from what are they to draw their livelihood, and how are they to be able to exist, when they have nothing to lean on, when the foundation breaks and drags down with it the whole edifice that was created and built over tens and tens of years?
We do not give ourselves any account at all of where we stand in the world. Had we drawn a parallel between the past and today, had we paused calmly over the dangerous situation, only then would we have been in a position to see in what manner we are sinking, with what giant strides we are fighting our way towards the abyss.
But what comes of it is that we do not allow ourselves to consider with full attention and seriousness this situation, which advances with terrifying speed to tear out everything that still remains in our energy.
Do we then possess the authority, the mighty force, that would have the ability to review all this and find out that this or that category, this or that stratum can be saved and must be saved from downfall? Can we then persuade ourselves that we are so strong materially and have such a mighty power that would stand up against all this? Or are we then in a position to carry out such a kind [?] of review, after which we could establish this and that, determine thus and so? Are these then not utopian ideas? When we speak about this: and if not this, if we are not to think how to create real help, then what is left for us to do? Can a people then stand by and look on indifferently as one keeps going under, as one loses position after position, at a time when fresh positions do not come into our possession and we do not even have the strength to aspire to them, because all roads are barred to us and we remain helpless and resourceless, both materially and in everyday life?
From outside, outside the Jewish camp, we are heroes and mighty men, and our wit, our strong will, our acumen and sharpness of mind are admired — while among ourselves we are helpless creatures and cannot save ourselves when we are drowning, and when the catastrophe has reached the point of "the waters are come in unto my soul."
Competitors — A Present-Day Sketch from the Street

It is not important here to name the street and the names of the competitors. Whoever has a „smykałka“ [knack, flair] in his head may guess. But that is not the main thing; what matters is the present day.
...There sat a Jew, a merchant, in his shop for quite a few days („kama yamim“), earning his living by hard work.
But a second Jew, one without a livelihood, grew envious of him and said to himself: why should I keep breaking my head over the question of what to take up? Here is a Jew who has „bread with a knife“ [a ready livelihood] — I will do the same.
And it did not take long at all before, exactly opposite, face to face, literally window facing window, on both sides of the pavement (trotuar) two shops of the same kind began to glitter from their display windows (vistaves, wystawy) and call out to the passers-by.
And here the real story begins. Both merchants have t h e s a m e friends and acquaintances, so the friends and acquaintances now find it hard to enter either of the shops. If one buys from this one, the other shouts; if he goes in to the other, the first gets angry. So the friends avoid the little street altogether — and it is a third one who takes the money. How does the saying go? When two quarrel, the third one profits.
And so both competitors stand, their pointed noses flattened against the display windows, eye fixed against eye, watching out for a customer — and they take satisfaction in the fact that he does not stray to the one opposite either.
Gr.
Our Panorama

(The vermin [lit. „mouse-swarm“] has spread. — The crisis liquidated in sanctified purity. — 25 women free of charge — The miracle at Kolonia Reden. — Facing the mikveh. — The „wartość“ [value] of „Maftera Junga“ [Maftir Jonah]. — „Strongmen“ with official competence[?].)
For all diseases there is a cure; even those who commit offences are helped by an amnesty. Only for one plague are there no remedies — for our vermin...
For quite a long time now we have not filled this column, because we were of the opinion that perhaps after all, perhaps after all the „material“ would be exhausted; but we were mistaken. The results were different: the vermin has grown so much in length and in breadth that we do not know to whom to give „Kohen“ [the first aliyah] and with which creatures we should make the beginning..
But after lengthy „deliberation“ we did reach agreement that the head of the list belongs to
— the holy community of Dąbrowa Górnicza („bak״k Dombrova Gorna“)...
For just show me one more town or shtetl in our country that can point in any real way to something having been done there to ease the crisis in sanctified purity?
The only exception in this field is the one kehilla in Dąbrowa, which published the following notice to its holy flock:
„With God's help. A great announcement, important for the poor: in order to remove a stumbling-block we have prevailed upon R' Zisza Luksenberg to make the mikveh cheap for women in the following manner: 1st class 1 zł., for the „namente“[?] 50 gr.; 2nd class 70 gr., for the „namente“ 30 gr.; 3rd class 50 gr., for the „namente“ 25 gr. Besides this he undertakes to let 25 women in every month entirely free of charge“...
Well, what do you say to this amnesty? Even in this amnesty there are a number of incomprehensible „paragraphs“, for example the classification of the classes... But be that as it may, it deserves a warm welcome, especially when „25 women will go in entirely free of charge“...
———
Second place, in our opinion, must go to the suburb „Kolonia Reden“, and we firmly believe that when the Reden mikveh is revealed through us, people will flock here from the four corners of the earth to immerse themselves in its holy water...
A trifle, the Reden mikveh? Why, Elijah the Prophet immersed himself there...
The „miracle“ happened back in the Ten Days of Repentance.
Around 4 in the morning, when „Reden“ was still sunk in deep sleep, Elijah the Prophet came into the mikveh; naturally he was disguised as a „Deitsch“ [a Jew in European dress], he spoke only Polish, and after the immersion (according to Kabbalah...) he disappeared in the direction of the „Flora“ mine (kopalnia)...
This was seen by eyewitnesses, the finest Jews of „Reden“; their mouths spoke with him, with Elijah the Prophet, and their eyes saw how he vanished in a cloud of smoke...
And from then on an ordinance was issued: „Anyone who comes out alive from the Reden mikveh must keep his eyes turned towards the water, not towards the public“... because
— one must show respect to Elijah the Prophet's „mikveh“...
———
An honourable „place“ has also been earned by the Olkusz dozors [members of the kehilla board]. They, the Olkusz dozors, do not neglect the interests of the kehilla but stand on guard to defend the honour of the community even before the starosta [district head]...
The Torah reader in the Olkusz synagogue holds a customary right (chazakah) to Maftir Jonah; that is his entire honorarium for the reading. But this year Satan the accuser set upon him, upon the Torah reader, and incited one of the dozors to develop an appetite for this „fat morsel“.
And since the Torah reader set himself against the decision of the gmina and did not want to give up his right, a letter went off in the name of the Olkusz prayer leaders (shlichei tzibbur) to the starosta, stating that:
„Ten Czaczysza[?] w' Radalu[?] [garbled Polish] should be suspended from his office, he harms („szkodzi“) the kehilla treasury and arbitrarily („samowola“) sold that Maftir Jonah („tego maftera Junga“), which has a very great value („wartość“)“...
———
And last but not least. A short report, but with deep content, lies before us from the „sharp“ young men of the Ger shtibl in Będzin (of the small one...).
The „fiery ones“ of this shtibl have introduced among themselves the old custom that existed in Będzin in the days of the rule of the wild youths. In the old days, when a stranger came to Będzin looking for work, he had to buy himself free from the band of „strongmen“ (shtarke); if not, he had to wander back to wherever he came from...
The same force was applied by the above-mentioned young men against a young married man, also a Ger hasid, who spent the second days of the festival in Będzin.
Between Shacharit and Musaf, when the hasidic fervour of the young men was spraying fire, a special commission sat in deep deliberation and issued a ruling:
— that So-and-so son of So-and-so, the young man from Sosnowiec, must pay 32 gulden! And if not
— he shall go home without his coat (palto)...
And so it was: the poor young fellow had to go home „dressed up“; his little wife, seeing her „king“ in the torn — borrowed — „garment“, simply had a „spasm“. For the family the festival was spoiled, but the „sharp ones“ rolled about with joy..
Only at the close of the festival did people barely manage to persuade the strongmen to „reduce“ the price to 15 gulden, and then the coat was released...
Ben Amoz.
What Must Be Done for Jewish Craftsmanship

[Article — Jewish craftsmanship.]
First of all, a wholly different spirit must be instilled among the Jewish craftsmen, so that the craft itself acquires its proper importance in their own eyes. Everyone — the craftsman and the non-craftsman alike — must finally understand that every Jewish workshop is a holy of holies. In a word: the craft itself must gain due esteem among our Jews, and its perfection and its conquests in Jewish hands must become a truly national task for everyone who still bears the name Jew.
Carrying out such a psychological transformation among the masses lies in the hands of our better societies and organizations, and especially of the Jewish press of every place. The latter must in general stop looking upon the work of the Jewish trade schools as some private matter, and see them rather as institutions that play a first-rank role in the future of Klal Yisrael in Poland.
Secondly, special free courses must be created in every place for the adult Jewish craftsman, in Yiddish, which would train him to some extent and develop him in his craft. In order that the courses truly bring a blessing to the Jewish craftsman, endure, and not be turned into yet another Jewish institution on a rotten "shlishi and bench" foundation [i.e. honours and seats], of which we are already so rich, they must from the outset be built, and afterwards also run, with the same idealism and reverence with which our fathers and grandfathers created and maintained their societies: "Mishnayot", "Ein Yaakov", etc. We still have enough forces for this. One need only have a good organization that will take them in hand properly and compel them to do it. The Jewish craftsmen's organizations, which until now have done nothing apart from their harmful politicking and quarrels — now they have the floor!
Thirdly, we must hurry a little with creating short textbooks, small handbooks for the craftsman in all trades in Yiddish, adapted to him and taking into account his deficient theoretical preparation. We already even have several technical textbooks in Yiddish, but they are cut out specially for the technical secondary schools, so that the Jewish craftsman cannot use them at all. So something practical must be created specially for him — material to be worked through for the job. The Jewish technician and educator now have the floor.
Fourthly, a special publishing house must be established on secure foundations, which would publish all the editions of technical books for the Jewish craftsman, or at least subsidize them. The Jewish kehillot of all Poland, and especially the Jewish craftsmen's organizations, which must surely at last, once and for all, justify their existence — they have the floor on this!
I know that the old, well-known excuse will come: "There are no means, there are no forces." But that is really quite false. It is not means that we lack, but the sincere will to create, and honest people devoted to the cause to organize all this. The necessary means and forces must be found, and will be found!
After all, we have a press of hundreds of Jewish papers and little papers in all the towns and townlets of Poland. So why should not one single publishing house be able to exist for a few technical textbooks for the Jewish craftsman?
Let us first see how large the budgets are of all the Jewish kehillot together, of the craftsmen's organizations, of other societies for the productivization of the Jewish masses... It seems. If the charity boxes of every kind make such a din here that one goes deaf — and what is done with the money? It is painful to talk about it. But if we still find money even for the devil and the demon, it must not be allowed that a whole class of people, who should and must be the pride and ornament of the whole people, should collapse merely because the few groszy needed for it are lacking...
It is not true that we lack the necessary living force. How many thousands of Jewish students are scattered across the whole country. How many hundreds of Jewish engineers of every speciality wander about the Polish towns and townlets. If even only a small part of this great mass of technically trained and experienced Jews were to lend a single finger to the holy work — a grandiose edifice would grow up!
It is not right that the Jewish student and young academic of today remembers his people only when he himself needs the people's help, and does not want to know of it while the people is in need. No, it is not they who are to blame for not coming to the work, but you, the leaders of the craftsmen's organizations — because you do not call them to the work.
The Jewish engineer and technician, the Jewish teacher and student, children of the people, who have themselves tasted need and are experienced in the struggle for their own existence, are waiting for you, the leaders of the craftsmen's organizations, to mobilize them for the service of the people — for the mass of declining Jewish craftsmen. At your first call they will report, not as generals but as simple soldiers, not in order to grab "benches" [posts] from you, but for work that you have neglected until today.
The Jewish craftsmen's leaders now have the floor. If on this present day they remain like the one "who does not know how to ask", others — to whom the cause is truly dear — will have to begin to speak. If the craftsmen's leaders can do nothing at all even at the last minute, then the Jewish kehilla will have to do it, for the last hour has struck, and it must be done!
Eng. Abraham Benenson.
Profits and Crisis.

[Essay — satirical feuilleton, the economic crisis.] I recently read a study by a professor, a researcher on the subject of the brain [printed “mard”, read “markh” — brain/marrow]. According to his assertion the brain is the most precious article in the world. It goes without saying that he is not talking about ox or sheep brains, and he is not out to incite the butchers to raise the prices of this grey matter.
Talking and talking, the professor speaks of the human brain, and he complains that the man of today does not use even a tenth of his brain-capital.
This assertion of his made a very strong impression on me, and I set about pondering, thinking, reflecting, brooding, wrinkling my forehead — and it worked. In the course of a few days my whole brain was shaken up [?] and my mind was stirred [?]...
In all the cells of my intellect-apparatus a powerful activity began; all its little wheels and little screws and little hinges [“zavyaskelekh”, from Polish zawiasy] began to move quickly, noisily, stormily, so that in my head there arose a dreadful whirlwind of ideas, a terrible tempest of thoughts.
And when a few more days had passed, over the whole surface of the skull, from right at the temples to the back of the head [“potilitse”, Polish potylica], lay heaped up giant piles of plans for how to cure the present-day world of all its ills.
How to liquidate the conflicts between China and Japan over Manchuria, how to root out Hitlerism in Germany and antisemitism in the whole world, and how to abolish the crisis and bring satiety to all people on our planet.
I was already ready to turn to the League of Nations, lay all the plans before it and urgently ask it to carry them out forthwith. But meanwhile, before you could say “what”, I went on thinking further, because I trembled at the professor's warning against leaving my brain unoccupied for even a minute.
And do you know what the end was? — Here is what: as soon as I stirred my brain, new thoughts, fresh plans came rushing at me, which razed the first ones to the ground and showed me plainly that they were foolish and that I was, begging my own pardon, a fool for letting them near me even for a minute.
Well, I sent the foolish thoughts “to the devil” [printed “lezal”, for “la‘azazel”], seized the clever, sensible, practical ones, and once again got ready to go to the League, and meanwhile thought and pondered again.
Well, from all the cells there began to fly anew brand-new plans, which made a mountain of ash of the earlier ones and proved to me with signs and wonders that I was a beast in human form for having been able to invent such ridiculous, empty plans.
In short, fellow Jews, I came to realise that working constantly with all five parts of the brain is a misfortune; on the contrary — from such a thing you can go out of your mind, and the brain can, may it befall the enemies of Israel, turn completely upside down from constant pondering.
So, although I am no professor, I want to recommend here my latest fully theorised-out theory, which reads as follows:
Thinking is the most harmful thing in the world, for look at us, who do not “use” a full ninety percent of our brain, and what about us, who do use — not even more than ten percent.
If we speak of business, it is agreed that for this you need not think, ponder and investigate. The proof you have from the profits. Some years ago, when abundance flooded everything [“gembult”, from mabul, flood], we thought then that this came from the great wisdom of the generation. The hundreds of millionaires and the enormously great magnates and rich men gave us the impression of geniuses on the field of political economy. The old superstition about luck vanished entirely. Luck? What luck! — the secret of their great successes lay exclusively in their brilliant intellect. And when my friend Shlomo Yoel, “a shteyner” [?], used to come to me and point to his huge earnings, my knees would bend and I wanted to fall deep to the ground before his great wisdom and shrewdness.
Today, however, we see plainly our wild mistake. For as soon as the crisis crept up, all the great heroes of business were left standing like golems and had not the faintest idea how to turn, how to twist so as to tear themselves out of the catastrophe that is chasing over their heads. The crisis tore strips off them, and they had not one crumb of a screw in their brain to understand how to push it back and thrust it away from them. And when my friend Shlomo Yoel came to me a few days before his bankruptcy, he looked like a “runier [?] laymekh” [a hapless fool]. “I am kaput”, he said to me. “Not only have I been wiped out of my capital, I still owe a great deal, they are still demanding that I pay them..”
And when I asked him: Tell me, Shlomo Yoel, how, I beg you, could it happen that a Jew, such a great clever man as you, should let himself be plundered so easily and put up no resistance whatsoever? — when I asked him this question, he answered me with open-hearted simplicity: “Clever? What clever! It is not with my wisdom that I amassed my wealth, nor with my great sharp ideas. The wealth came to me — may I be forbidden if I know how — and now that it has gone I haven't the faintest idea how”.
It follows that the profits came precisely from dullness, from brain-blockage: people stopped investigating and seeking wisdom and took to trading and wheeling-dealing, speculating, swindling, building towers on sand, castles in the air on the clouds — and the business paid off. For there was no one to wrinkle his forehead and think whether perhaps the whole thing was no more than an illusion; and since nobody thought and nobody cast a shadow of doubt on the illusion, it stood firm as reality... and the world enjoyed itself.
But suddenly, it seems, somewhere a fellow turned up [?] who started analysing the profits and examining with his head on what foundations they stand — and this very chap brought about the world calamity. Soon others caught his thinking mood and saw the light of the bitter truth; saw that the great flood of money is absolutely no money at all, but a fantasy.
That is how the crisis came — came from thinking and rethinking, from starting to think, ponder and doubt; once people lose trust in one another, credits stop, lending stops. People start demanding hard cash, and since nowadays there is no cash, there is only paper money or gilt paper — along comes a bankruptcy.
In short, thinking is an unhealthy thing for the community as for the individual. Thinking too much ruins our society, ruins humanity. By thinking a lot, brooding a lot, it thinks its way into every misfortune. It also thinks its way into every baseness — for what are all the wars and bloody conflicts between nations if not the result of excessive over-sharpness? Animals have no intellect, do not think, do not ponder — and they know of no wars, at least not among themselves, not within their own kind.
People and nations, however, have a thinking-apparatus, and that “saddens them”. They keep thinking: what if someone attacks them — and they look for plans and means to attack that someone..
So Germany has now taken it into her head that Poland is sharpening the sword against her, and therefore she must get equality of armaments with all nations. Naturally France does not like the smell of it, and other nations do not like the smell of it either. The result will probably be that instead of reducing the instruments of war they will add to them — and then God knows what may happen.
Yes, my dear readers, all troubles come from thinking. Man's thought is evil from his youth, and the older he gets the worse his thoughts become — if he uses them, nurtures them and cultivates them.
When humanity was young, its thoughts were evil enough; but today, now that it is old, they are utterly unbearable. No small matter — a whole humanity that has been thinking for several thousand years.
Only, as said, it is still a bit of luck that ninety percent of our brain is asleep. Were it not so, there would presumably long ago have been no trace left of us or of the world.
Ploni ve-Kohen.
"Czeba płaciś!" ["You Have to Pay!"] (After the Income-Tax Assessment)

When one looks closely at the attitude of the tax authority towards taxpayers in general and towards the merchant class in particular, one gets the impression that the various offices [urzędy] and chambers [izby, i.e. the treasury chambers] regard the taxpayer as a very low creature who must not be believed by a hair's breadth; and when the merchant in general, and the Jewish merchant in particular, cries out that he is standing at the edge of the abyss, that he is already utterly broken under the heavy burden of taxes — then people laugh at these "false tears," and the tax screw keeps on pressing, because from all the various tax offices one hears only one word: "Czeba płaciś!" [Polish trzeba płacić — "you have to pay!"]
And holding precisely to this "czeba płaciś policy," the income tax has lately been assessed here in Zagłębie.
They pretended not to know that in this last year the crisis is reaching its point of culmination, and that assessing a shopkeeper's income at the same level as last year simply means undermining his existence.
When will there at last be an end to this tactic of taking no account of the merchant's actual situation and clinging only to the one cold [?] word: "Czeba płaciś"!
The Polish Pranaitis and His Incitement against Jews

[Poland — antisemitism; the marriage-law project.] It is astonishing how far the impudence of our home-grown antisemites reaches, and what brazen foreheads they have..
The Jews in Poland now live in extraordinarily hard conditions. And at the same time the enemies of Israel come and ring a great alarm bell: the Polish state is ruled (!) by Jews... Jews set the tone in Polish legislation. And these cunning little Jews, who hold the reins[?] („העזי”) of the Polish state in their hands, have one single aim: to stab Poland in the back...
Poland, the young state, which on its creation took over the valid laws of the former rulers, has lately been carrying out a comprehensive and thorough revision and codification (compilation) of all laws and binding ordinances, in order[?] to lay the foundation for a new, uniform and modern legislation of the state.
It goes without saying that such a grandiose work cannot be carried out by a single individual, and indeed a special commission of learned and famous Polish jurists was created — this is the Codification Commission of 36 persons, among them also two Poles of Jewish origin: Prof. Rappaport and Adv. Litauer, two recognized authorities in the field of legal science.
This Codification Commission has worked out, in one of its sub-commissions, a project for reforming the currently binding law on marriages and divorces.
This sub-commission is entirely free of Jews, even of former Jews..
The project of the Codification Commission provides for a whole series of regulations that stand in glaring contradiction to Jewish law.
For example: the project provides for allowing mixed marriages among Jews too, which are to acquire legal force.
Further we find in the project such proposals as: to allow marrying one's own aunt, to recognize as legal a marriage without chuppah and kiddushin, to be allowed to divorce without a Jewish get, and more such provisions that run absolutely counter to the sanctified customs of the Jewish people.
It would be an injustice to ascribe to the Codification Commission intentions of an anti-Jewish character, for just as it comes out with projects that overturn many sanctified Jewish traditions and ordinances, the project likewise does not stand on ceremony with some provisions of other religions, among them the Catholic one.
And this has caused a great storm in the Catholic world...
The tremendous agitation is to a certain degree understandable, for truly: the whole day-to-day practice in the Polish state so far has been such that Polish society was accustomed to the idea that Poland is a one-hundred-percent Catholic state. The Catholic religion has constantly been privileged, while the needs of other, non-Catholic peoples have been ignored...
The decisions of the Codification Commission, which bases its activity on purely scientific, modern foundations, were indeed bound to produce a powerful effect in the circles of the Catholic clergy[?].
Interesting[?], however, is the manner in which these tone-setters conduct their attack on the recalcitrant „anti-marriage law project”: they are not content to combat the opinions of the Codification Commission from a scientific, or even a religious, standpoint, but chiefly indulge in a wild attack on Jews, on Jewish ethics, on Jewish morality and — on the Talmud...
The tone-bearer of the whole campaign is a well-known Catholic clergyman, a former professor at the theological institute in Petersburg, Stanisław Trzeciak.
This ksiądz [priest], wishing to reduce to ashes and mud the new project for reforming marriage and divorce, came out some time ago with a bombastic brochure under the resounding title: „The Talmud, Bolshevism and the Polish Project on Marriages and Divorces”. So — the Talmud first and foremost!
The conclusion of the said brochure is (in sum!) that Polish legislation lies under the slipper of the Jews, who draw all their nourishment from the Talmud, which is — the basic foundation of Bolshevism...
It goes without saying that this Catholic „scholar” does not speak at all in the tone of a scholar; his brochure rather bears the character of a pamphlet, full of poison and hatred against Jews and everything Jewish.
The essence of Dr. Trzeciak's „work” is a pathetic exclamation: Polish people, wake up, beware of your internal enemies, the Jews, who want to break what you won in struggle with so much blood of your best sons on the battlefields...
This base attack on Jews is peppered and adorned with many verses and quotations from the Talmud and the poskim, naturally twisted and falsified, so as to „illustrate” as vividly as possible the terrible, destructive and annihilating influence of Jewish morality and Jewish ethics.
A proper drubbing the cleric Dr. Trzeciak received from the well-known Jewish jurist Dr. A. Ackerberg: in a book under the same name Dr. Ackerberg pointed out all the shameless falsifications of the so-called „Talmud expert”, exposing his true nature, which is sky-far from healthy patriotism, from scholarship and from the Talmud, which the cleric Trzeciak, poor fellow, does not even begin to know.
Dr. Trzeciak, however, like the whole clerical camp for which he sets the tone, has not given up the campaign as lost; on the contrary, with even more vigour he has now embarked on a new wild incitement against Jews and has even put back on the table his „favourite work”, the Talmud.
For a number of weeks now „Przegląd Katolicki” — the most respected Catholic newspaper in Poland — has been publishing a series of articles by the same Dr. Trzeciak as a reply to Dr. Ackerberg's book. Time and again he fires off quotations from the Talmud and bends over backwards to prove that the Jews are the most dangerous people in the world, because — to this day they live by the precepts of the Talmud, the „kizal and aldas bein”[?].
And if you do not take him at his word, or perhaps have doubts about the accuracy of his Talmud quotations, he brings in his articles proofs also[?] from such „great authorities” as the expert in the Beilis trial Pranaitis, Bialerbek[?] and other persecutors of the Jews...
Naturally the edge of his poisoned sword is directed not so much against the Codification Commission, which dared to include in its membership two apostates (Prof. Rappaport and Adv. Litauer), but chiefly against the „żyd” Dr. Ackerberg, who unmasked him so mercilessly and exposed his ugly intentions.
The noble cleric, the „protector” of Poland against the „Jewish danger”, in his rage and wrath constantly spews blood libels on the Jewish community. He does not stop short of the ugliest accusations — that the Jews are bolshevizing Poland and that even in the Supreme Court in Warsaw Jews have organized a communist „yacheyka” [cell]...
I. Goldinger.
An Important Clarification on Deferments („Odroczenia”) for Sole Breadwinners

[Poland — military service; legal advice.] Until now the practice was that if a father was older than 60 and had no other member of the family able to work, but was dependent exclusively on the earnings of the conscript (poborowy), the latter was granted a deferment (odroczenie) of military service.
The circumstance that such a father nevertheless still worked a little was never regarded as an obstacle to recognizing an „opiekuństwo” [status of provider/carer].
Now the administrative authority [printed „ארמיניסטראטיווע”] has changed its attitude on this point. In all cases where the inspection carried out establishes that the parents entitled to an „opiekuństwo” have some employment, the applications submitted for deferments for their sons are decisively rejected.
Such a manner of dealing with the said matters on the part of the starostwa [county offices] does not, in our opinion, accord with the intent of the law.
From article 58 of the Act (ustawa) on universal military service and from article 267 of the executive ordinance to the said Act it is to be explicitly inferred that in the question of recognizing the right to a deferment on the basis of point 1, article 57 of the cited Act, what decides is not at all the circumstance whether the family member, of whom the conscript concerned claims to be the sole breadwinner, works or not; the matter turns exclusively on whether he is able to work.
As soon as such a person is older than 60, he is already automatically recognized as unfit for work. Since this is so, the circumstance that he does in fact work cannot in any case have any effect on the decision on recognizing an „opiekuństwo”, if only because the work of such an old man cannot be so lasting and sufficient that it should support his family.
The families concerned must by all means demand the said decisions from the starostwa according to the rules indicated.
Y. A-d.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Noach)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Noach
The Portion
—o—
a) "He was perfect in his generations" (Gen. 6:9)
"..And some interpret it to his discredit." Rashi.
From where did those sages conclude that Noah should be interpreted to his discredit? Because the Torah praises him — the only person whom the Torah praises. Of Moses too a praise is written: "Now the man Moses was very meek", but that is not praising, merely telling; only Noah is praised, so many virtues are told of him — and that is somehow not a good sign, when someone takes pains to praise someone as much as possible.. Arvei Nachal.
—o—
b) "The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence."
In the end, only the fear of God is able to hold man back from robbery and plunder. We see how external human morality is trampled even by its own priests when the fear of God is not present alongside it. When "the earth was corrupt before God", there follows as a matter of course "and the earth was filled with violence". Kerem HaTzvi.
• • •
When Moses our teacher saw that the Jews were making themselves a calf — "and he cast the tablets out of his hands (so is the qere)" — he threw away both tablets, even the tablet on which the commandments between man and his fellow were engraved, because without a God those are not kept either.
Rabbi Israel Salanter.
—o—
c) "For the earth is filled with violence through them" (ibid., 13)
"Through them" — they themselves called it violence when it was done to them, but when they did it to others it was honesty and justice... Kiflayim LeTushiya.
—o—
d) "So Noah knew that the waters were abated" (8:1 [sic])
How did he infer that from the olive leaf that the dove had in its mouth?
According to the Midrash, the dove hinted to Noah with the olive leaf that she would rather have food bitter as an olive from God than even sweet food from a human being.
Well, the dove could only be so bold when she knew that she was not dependent on Noah's charity, that outside there was a world. Had she still been dependent on his charity, she would not have spoken so boldly...
Zevach HaShelamim.
• • •
Rabbi Israel Salanter did not want to benefit from any person. But he did not conduct any business, so he had to accept the support that a Kovno [Kaunas] magnate, Hirshl Nachiaszer[?], gave him — but only for bread and water; more than that he would not take.
Once a guest comes to Rabbi Israel, and he treats him and says to him:
— Eat, eat, you are eating kosher food...
The guest is astonished: how so?...
— I will tell you — Rabbi Israel explains to him — in what I eat there is a suspicion of robbery... but what I offer you is for you entirely permitted, for I have already acquired it by a change of deed [shinui ma'aseh]..
—o—
e) "For the imagination of man's heart is evil" (ibid., 21)
All of man's thoughts revolve only around one thing: how to do as much evil as possible.. Shemen HaMor.
• • •
"Though your sins be as scarlet."
Like that merchant who sends his travelling salesman out with goods. All the expenses the salesman incurs on the road are on the merchant's account. One year the salesman brings him an account of very large expenses. The master has the calendars of all the years brought to him, shuffles them in the presence of the salesman and says to him:
— Look, I am shuffling the calendars and I do not see that the earlier years contained more days — so why are this year's expenses larger?
God knew that a person must sin sometimes, so He set aside for it one day of forgiveness — but only "if your sins be as scarlet" [lit. "as years"], if the sins do not exceed the foreseen account; but when "the thoughts of your heart are only evil all the day", when the expenses keep growing, then the balance will not hold out.. Mor VaAhalot.
—o—
f) "And the rain was restrained" (ibid., 2)
A Masorah note:
"And the rain was restrained"
and "So the people were restrained from bringing".
You sometimes see, as it seems, that the situation is getting better, but "clouds and wind without rain" — the horizon darkens again. That is because "the people were restrained from bringing": because the public behaves that way too — promises to give charity and does not give, so in Heaven they do the same: they show a glimmer and pull back... Divrei Yosef.
• • •
Rabbi Yoshe Ber once asks a wealthy man of Brisk [Brześć]:
— What are you making [i.e. how are you doing]?
— Praised be the Blessed Name — the other replies — there is a livelihood, health.
— That God makes — Rabbi Yoshe Ber replies to that — health and livelihood God makes. But I am asking what YOU make? Do you give any charity? Do you do any good? That is what you must make...
—o—
Haftarah.
g) "Lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes" (Isaiah 54)
It is indeed necessary to "lengthen thy cords" — to spread the Jewish tent out into the world, to leave open the windows of the tent of Shem to the winds of Japheth. But at the same time there must be "strengthen thy stakes" — at the same time one must strengthen oneself inwardly, so that the worldly winds do not overturn the tent.
Rabbi Ch. Hirschensohn.
A Gravestone for Moshe Appelbaum!

[Będzin — art and remembrance.] The second anniversary of the death (yortsayt) of the universally beloved and popular artist Moshe Appelbaum [Mojżesz Appelbaum] is approaching. Who did not know him, the true artist-bohemian, the ever life-loving and always cheerful Appelbaum? After all, the various political camps, from right to left, often fought among themselves over whether Appelbaum belonged to this group and not to another; each of them separately said, "upon me shall the righteous man lay his head." Where are they now? Why are they all silent, when two years after his death there is still no gravestone on his grave?
As one of the figures of Jewish, wandering plastic art, he went through the long, painful, thorny road that leads from the small, backward shtetl to the Royal Academy of Art in London, which he completed with distinction. He could have had a secure existence, honour and money among "them", among the gentiles, where there is an understanding for art and artists; but he, to his misfortune, was drawn back to the shtetl, to his Jews, to the workshop, to the milieu of want and misery, from which he created his splendid canvases.
If he had a hard, painful life, he certainly did not think that a few years after his death there would be no gravestone on his grave.
That, unfortunately, can happen only among us, where there is not the slightest understanding for art, where people still look at an artist as at a trickster, whose tricks one may sometimes watch out of curiosity, but in whom nobody need take an interest.
That is the reason why plastic art among Jews is still at a low level, because an artist, like a delicate tropical plant, must have a warm, favourable atmosphere in order to be able to develop; otherwise it must wither and in the end die. But not everyone wants to sacrifice himself on the altar of Jewish art; not in every artist is idealism as strongly developed as in Appelbaum, whose motto was: I do not paint in order to sell, but I sell in order to paint.
And indeed Jewish artists run away into foreign camps and create for foreign cultures, as Frenchmen, Germans, Englishmen, etc.
If we, all Appelbaum's close ones and friends, feel guilty that we have done nothing until today about a gravestone, we especially blame the Będzin kehilla for its complete disregard of the matter.
After all, Appelbaum gave his health and his life so that the Będzin town synagogue should be a work of art — and it truly became a model not only for Poland but also beyond its borders.
True, two more artists took part in painting the synagogue: our Ziegler and Hanft (they will no doubt be wiser and save up for gravestones themselves), but the main nerve, who kept an eye on everything, was Appelbaum. And how was such a colossal work of art paid for? With a ridiculous wage. It is a disgrace to say it, for it would mean profaning art.
He used to work up to 16 hours a day without tiring. In the long, cold winter nights, when the frost scalded the fingers, he stood until late at night on the scaffolding [rusztowanie] by the eastern wall and kneaded the cold clay, until blood even ran from his hands. When I used to tell him to come down already, that the Będzin kehilla would in any case not put up a golden gravestone for him, he answered that his artistic conscience did not allow him to botch the work, and that the synagogue had to be finished by a fixed date.
He, poor man, the unfortunate one, did not foresee that the walls of the synagogue would not yet be properly dry, and he would already be lying in the grave and be forgotten in such a shameful way.
It is therefore the urgent duty of all Appelbaum's acquaintances, close ones and friends, and quite especially of the Będzin Jewish kehilla, to set about at once a large campaign that will still manage to erect a gravestone by the coming yortsayt. A committee must immediately be formed of the representatives of the various societies, institutions and parties, who will take up the matter and bring it to a final result, for from beneath the little mound of earth that covers Appelbaum's grave a voice rises and demands of us a gravestone.
Sz. Rotenberg.
A Victim of the Bookkeeping Decree

[Sosnowiec — slice of life, satire.]
A terrible tale that happened in Zagłębie.
When Feige Sura (read: Frania-Sala) first read in the papers that every merchant would have to keep commercial books, and that otherwise he would be squeezed into the "yoshev beseter" [i.e. jail] for a whole 6 months, she began nagging her hapless[?] husband terribly to introduce bookkeeping in his little shop that very minute.
Chaim Getzl even tried to talk his wife out of her claims. "What on earth do I need bookkeeping for?" — he began pleading with her, as with a robber — "can't I perhaps reckon up my penny takings, so to speak[?], without bookkeeping? Or will the office [Pol. urząd][?] not slap distraints on me every Monday and Thursday even with bookkeeping?"
But all these arguments apparently barely convinced the obstinate[?] Feige Sura. On the contrary, she fell upon[?] poor Chaim Getzl with an even louder racket.
"What," she let loose, "maybe you fancy that I should stay a living widow for a whole 6 months, that people should point at me in the streets: there goes the jailbird's wife, the criminal's wife! No, you won't live to see it! You'd better introduce bookkeeping already!"
Feige Sura tormented her husband so long that he finally agreed to introduce commercial books.
Here a new quarrel broke out between the couple: whom to entrust the bookkeeping to.
"You know what, Feige Surele, I have a poor relative in the family, a laid-off woman bookkeeper. Perhaps it would be right to engage her," her "Moshe Dir" [?] timidly proposes (the phrase "zayn pluntete Moshe dir" is unclear).
"What I dreamt last night and the night before should fall on your head, your hands and feet, your body and life!" Sura Feige came back with a retort. "Just listen, good people, to the talk of this old sinner! Not even a full year has passed since I married him and I'm already too little for him — he fancies taking a girl into partnership. Out of the question! As long as my eyes are open, it won't happen.
If we must take in someone from the family, then mine, I think, is cheaper. As it happens I also have a cousin, a laid-off bookkeeper, who by the way supports sick parents. For my sake he certainly won't charge dearly, and it will simply be a good deed to give someone a chance to earn."
Of course, this time too she won and not he. Feige Sura's candidate was indeed taken on as bookkeeper in Chaim Getzl's little paint shop.
Because of the cramped shop, the bookkeeper did the bookkeeping at Chaim Getzl's home.
For barely three weeks the cousin slaved over Chaim Getzl's books, and who knows how much longer he could have slaved, had it not occurred to him to make a "shma koleinu" [printed: kolgu] — to take flight, and to take with him the lady of the house as well and, first and foremost, the 16 hundred złoty together with the bit of jewellery that lay hidden in the bottom drawer of the wardrobe.
Only then did Chaim Getzl begin to chew over the whole business with the bookkeeping and with the cousin the bookkeeper. But he was so badly shaken by the event that for the first days he did not know what to do.
Later it turned out otherwise. The bookkeeper had deceived Feige Sura too. He had arranged with her to run away together, but he ran off alone, and, taking from her the takings and the few belongings, he left her sitting on the meat-"bench"[?] at a railway station somewhere in a small town.
With great trouble the bedraggled[?] mistress [Pol. kochanka] dragged herself back to Sosnowiec. Now she begs her husband for mercy, to let her back into the house and go on living with her; she swears to be good and pious.
But the husband wants to know nothing more of her and is trying to obtain a divorce (get).
Argus.
Three Humps Taken Off (A Monologue by a Jew Who Has Daughters)

[Feuilleton — humorous monologue; Palestine and emigration.]
— You ask me, Fania, why I have become such an ardent Zionist and so terribly smitten with the Land of Israel? — Why, I ask you in return, shouldn't I be smitten with it and love the Land of Israel, when in such a short time it managed to take three humps off my back? You stare at me? You don't understand, you say, what I mean by that — what is there to understand? I had three unmarried daughters, each a head taller than the next — and all three of them, thanks to the Land of Israel, have got married...
I always went about worried on their account, on account of those girls, didn't sleep nights and kept wondering: what will become of them in the end? Money for a dowry for them I didn't have, for where, I ask you, should a craftsman like me get money, when all in all I barely wear myself out making a living? To marry them off here without a dowry — there was certainly nothing to wait for there either; although all three were not ugly... because, you understand me, any shabby, down-at-heel fellow nowadays wants only money, and God forbid you talk in złotys — only in dollars... Every good-for-nothing, every ne'er-do-well who can't earn a groszy, weighs himself straight away against gold... And here a year goes by after a year, and they, the girls, grow as if on yeast, so that you might as well take all three and lead them to the wedding canopy on a single day... So God indeed saw my sorrow and sent me the cure for the affliction — the Land of Israel!...
All three of them went off to the Land of Israel... But don't think, Fania, that it happens as quickly as it's said. First the eldest girl went there. And she didn't go so easily either. Before that she spent three years as what they call a "chalutza" [pioneer], sitting day and night in the pioneers' "lokal" [clubroom], which for them is a kind of "cheder meyuchad" [special room], where they gather every day; she went to "hachshara" [training], as they named it, that is, getting used to hard, simple labour. She knocked about for six whole months in a sawmill, hauled heavy logs and slaved like a gentile... And only afterwards, when she came back from the "hachshara", that is, when she had already learned to suffer and get blackened by the sun — was she able and allowed to go to the Land of Israel... Only one "trifle" was missing for that: money for travel expenses. Where do you get it? In short, I won't drag it out, Fania: I borrowed, pawned everything, got into debt up to my neck and raised the money for her expenses. She left, and I said the blessing "Blessed be He who has freed me"!
And what became of her there, you ask? — Well, don't rush [?]; that's just what I want to tell you: when she got there, she went straight into a "pardes" [orange grove], as it's called there in their language — and in all her letters she kept writing that she was very content and felt very well there in the Land of Israel. And when barely a year had passed, one day we got a letter from her with a mazel tov. What? She had become engaged. And to whom, do you think?
To a rich young man — the son of a rich colonist [settler-farmer]! And three months later — another mazel tov: she had already married, in a good hour.
That's how it is, Fania: without a penny the Land of Israel took the first and biggest hump off my back!...
Hearing such a story, my second girl thought it over — she too felt like going to the Land of Israel. She, the second one, was already a "shomeret" [member of Hashomer], as they call it, and she too used to spend whole days and nights in their clubroom. What did she do? First of all she too went off to "hachshara". She too knocked about there for half a year, hauled clay and bricks, slaved and toiled like a peasant, and came back coarsened, blackened and sunburnt, so that you couldn't recognise her... And soon after her return from hachshara, the elder daughter sent her a "drisha" [request], as they call the invitation papers there, with 10 pounds for expenses. It didn't take long and she was off. There, like the elder daughter, she too ended up in a "kvutza" [collective] and went to work in an orange grove.
In short, I won't spin it out for you; not even half a year had gone by when suddenly and unexpectedly we received a letter from her saying that, with good luck, she had celebrated her betrothal (tna'im) with a very decent young man, a graduate, a doctor no less, who works together with her in the "kvutza" — and shortly after — another letter: she is already inviting us to the wedding...
And so, as you hear, Fania, the Land of Israel took the second hump off my back as well.
Now I was left with the third hump, that is, the third girl, the youngest, the baby of the family. She in turn was already a real "Poalei-Zionist", as they call themselves (there are among them, you understand, both "Right" and "Left"), and she too used to spend whole evenings in the clubroom. Hearing that the "second" one had also married there, the third began to work at it, so that she too could go to the Land of Israel... She was ready to fly there even by "aeroplane". But there's the trouble — she could by no means get a "certificate", as they call it — and to wait for that paper she would have had to wait until the Messiah comes...
And what miracle does the Holy One, blessed be He, perform? She learns that from Warsaw a whole party of a few hundred people is leaving on an "excursion", as they call it, to the Land of Israel and back. What does she do? She up and signs on to that party, and indeed went off with the party.
To make a long story short, I won't keep you long: a month after she left we got a letter from her that she had already married a technician, if you please. Such a quick "fire" I really didn't expect... barely arrived — and already they set up a wedding canopy!... Such wonders only the Land of Israel can work!...
And so, Fania, without a penny the Land of Israel took off my back, one after another, all three humps...
I tell you — a precious land, this Land of Israel, a golden country! I'd trade ten Americas for it, I tell you!... In America the local girls become old maids, and many of them come down here to look for bridegrooms; in the Land of Israel — a girl from here arrives and they snap her up like a raspberry [i.e. like hot cakes], she gets a bridegroom right away — and what a bridegroom! — not for nothing is it called "a land flowing with milk and honey"!... I'm only sorry that I don't have a couple more girls... You have, I believe, Fania, a daughter too, a girl of marriageable age — take my advice, make the effort and send her over there — and you'll be rid of a hump!..

What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Intervention with the Starosta over the Actions of the District Doctor

[Head of the local page; Będzin — artisans and authorities.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 5 / 5 Cheshvan 5693 — piątek 4 listopada 1932 [Friday, 4 November 1932].)
Będzin
Intervention with the Starosta over the actions of the district doctor.
As our readers know, the present district (powiat) doctor has begun a rigorous campaign against the bakers, confectioners, shopkeepers etc., on whom the doctor imposes large fines, confiscates goods from them and creates other hardships that are unbearable.
The Artisans' Association, which for the time being is the only one dealing with this so painful question, has also turned to the Central Union for help.
On the strength of this appeal the chairman of the executive, Mr. Ch. Rosner, came here and, after acquainting himself with the situation that had arisen, intervened together with the chairman of the Artisans' Association, Mr. Goldsztajn, with the Starosta, Mr. Baksa.
The Starosta received the delegation in a friendly manner and listened with great interest to everything the delegation conveyed to him concerning the wrongs being done by the district doctor, who applies such harsh measures as bring ruin upon hundreds of souls in the present hard times.
The Starosta promised that he would endeavour to influence the doctor to stop the harsh measures applied until now regarding the sanitary regulations.
On Monday evening, in a hall packed full of those concerned, Messrs. Goldsztajn and Rosner reported on the course of their conference with the Starosta.
On Tuesday afternoon the same report was heard by the representatives of all the guilds.
After the report, a series of current artisans' matters was discussed together with the participants, which Mr. Rosner promised the Artisans' Union would settle favourably.
Feeding Campaign at Public School No. 2

[Będzin — education and relief.]
Public School No. 2 has set about feeding the poor pupils of the school.
For this purpose a women's circle has been formed, which is engaged in this campaign.
At the last meeting of the women's circle it was decided, in order to strengthen the fund for the campaign, to organise a "kilo collection" next week.
It is to be hoped that the Jewish population will duly appreciate the value of such a campaign and will receive the collectors with a friendly face.
The Plan Did Not Succeed...

[Będzin — police and prison.]
In connection with the amnesty, about 300 prisoners were released from the local and the Sosnowiec prisons. On this occasion a larger number of police patrols was sent out through the town.
One of the patrols, passing by the Będzin prison, noticed on a telephone pole a rope which was joined to the prison walls.
It did not take long before a prisoner let himself down from a prison window with the help of the rope. But the plan did not succeed, because the first one to welcome the fugitive was a policeman.
Later it turned out that the plan had been a very broad one. From the same room from which the prisoner had wanted to escape, 22 prisoners to whom the amnesty does not apply had prepared themselves, and wanted to be free without the amnesty.

Motion to Express No Confidence in the President of the Kehilla Board.

[Sosnowiec — kehilla.]
Last Sunday the kehilla board met for a session. On the agenda was the new kehilla budget for the year 1933.
Before the agenda is taken up, Mr Nachemia takes the floor; he criticizes the activity of Mr Wendel as kehilla president and proposes electing a new president who would give a guarantee that he will carry out the functions provided for in the budget.
Mr A. Sztyglic is against this, arguing that the point is not on the agenda.

One, Two, Three — and the Couple Is Divorced...

[Sosnowiec — everyday life.]
On Kościelna Street lived the young couple L. Last week a sharp exchange of words broke out between them, which led the husband to say:
— Let's get divorced...
The wife, who would not let anyone "spit in her porridge" (would not be got the better of), agreed at once and declared:
— A divorce — let it be today.
And when the angry couple came to the Będzin rabbinate, they were received like invited guests; no one tried in any way to persuade them to make up; instead, straight away and in great haste, the business was done: the husband paid a hundred and
— the get was given...
Only on coming home did the couple feel regret and see that they had done a great foolishness.
— The proof? The couple is about to remarry...

Music Notes.

[Będzin — music; concert review.] (Concert of the Jewish Song and Music Society in Będzin)
The concert of the Jewish Song and Music Society, promised several weeks ago, aroused broad interest among the Jewish masses, among those who yearn to hear a Yiddish folk song. (Of course, when Cossacks or Petliurists sing, the chief in-laws are only our "intelligentsia"...)
The hall is packed full. The "gallery-goers" make "atmosphere" and, as at a "Khinke Pinke" show, they provide the well-known "attractions"... But the programme too is filled with all sorts of delicacies, and yet another "miracle": the choir conductor had not rehearsed Indian songs, since almost all languages were given equal rights at the concert..
—
The opening with the song "Ikh lib di arbet" ("I love work") was apt: when one loves the work, one can set up[?] such a choir, which measures itself against Peretz's "Meyn nisht, az di velt iz a kretshme" ("Don't think the world is a tavern")... and such a symphony orchestra — Messrs. Prof. Brorakow and S. Lustig truly deserve a great "yasher koach".
The first part of the concert ends to great applause with the "Romance" and "Gypsy Dance", performed by the young talents L. Rechnic (violin) and B. Goldsztajn (piano), who are showered with long-lasting applause and must delight the audience with one more number as an encore ("bis").
—
The soloists' numbers of the second part, and incidentally (also of the first part), we consider superfluous in the programme, because singing merely for singing's sake may be allowed only to professionals; from Jewish amateur singers we want something distinctive. We would gladly give up not just both but all "Grenadiers" for one "Khatskele", even when the "Grenadier singer" is Y. Rotenberg.
A not-bad impression was made by the music numbers performed by the violinist M. Warszawski, accompanied by D. Kagan.
—
The finale was the third part: 1) the performance of the symphony orchestra under the direction of S. Lustig with the tactful[?] accompaniment of Prof. E. Bażykowska, and 2) "Meyn nisht, az di velt iz a kretshme", performed by the choir, at the piano the frequent participant Prof. P. Epsztajn.
On the whole the impression of the first concert is a satisfying one. The society has enough forces and material to continue its activities in the field of song and music.
Finally, a short remark. — The women singers in the first row should not, while singing, look at what is going on in the hall — their eyes should be turned to the notes...
S. L—tsh.
Must Such a Desecration of the Dead Be Tolerated?

[Będzin — burial society; letter to the editor.] (A letter to the editors).
This week, when my family was struck by a heavy misfortune, with the untimely death of our son, I only then learned to what a low level the matter has fallen which was once guarded as a sacred thing.
The matter is as follows.
On the day of the burial, the newly founded society of tailors [shroud-makers], in the persons of S. Bredin, Yekhezkel Proktshvig[?] and P. Pinkus, came to me with a proposal: that I should give them 13 metres of linen for shrouds, despite knowing. Although only 9 metres is sufficient, I gave the linen demanded. But what turned out? That the shrouds were small, oh, that several times they pulled the garments up and down on the dead, and after all this — the disgrace was beyond words...
The audacity of the aforementioned went still further: while the dead lay on the purification board, they stood around me like bailiffs and demanded work-money of no less than 18 gulden [złoty]...
Such lawlessness must, in everyone's opinion, be uprooted, and this compelled me to turn to the esteemed editors, so that the matter, although very painful for me, should be made public.
Moshe Leib Schweitzer.

Anti-Jewish excesses at Warsaw University

[Warsaw — antisemitism.] Anti-Jewish excesses at Warsaw University.
(By telephone from our Warsaw correspondent).
Yesterday the anti-Jewish agitation repeated itself: the incited Endek [National Democrat] hooligan gang threw itself with sticks upon the Jewish youth, sparing not even women.
The events began in this way:
At 1 o'clock midday there arrived at the Museum building at Krakowskie Przedmieście 66, where the first lectures were taking place, a delegation of Endek students from Wilno, which had been specially prepared in Wilno in connection with the first anniversary of the death of the student Wacławski, who fell victim in last year's events in Wilno.
After the lectures a meeting took place with the participation of the Wilno and Warsaw students.
At this meeting the speakers demanded that revenge be taken on the Jews. From words the hooligans passed to deeds: at once a wild hunt began after the Jewish students, sparing not even women, at whom they began throwing stools, sticks and the like.
At first the Jewish students tried to put up resistance, but seeing that they were in the minority, they wanted to withdraw; the Endeks, however, surrounded them on all sides and beat them murderously.
So that the Jews could not turn for help, the hooligans guarded the telephones in the Museum hall.
Later the excesses took on a wild character. Two Jewish women students who had called for help were thrown down the stairs from the first floor. One of them, 19-year-old Irena Buszycka[?], was wounded and a doctor had to be called for her.
With great difficulty the Jewish students managed to get out into the street, thanks to their having been able to alert the Rector, who came at once into the Museum and put an end to the events.
Police came and dispersed the assembled students.
The Pogotowie [emergency ambulance service] gave medical aid to the wounded Jewish students.
In the evening Jewish students, some 2000 strong, held a meeting, at which it was also resolved that a delegation should apply to the Minister of Education.

The Zawiercie Public Runs After "Evil Wonders"...

[Zawiercie — Society.] Zawiercie is boiling as in a kettle over the great "sensation" discovered last week by the carpenter Mr. Wolf Kinres. This carpenter made a table out of wood alone — not a single nail is to be found in this mysterious table, which "answers" various questions.
The "spiritualist séances" are held every evening in the presence of hundreds of people, men, women and children... Seven people sit down around the table and hold their hands on the table's edges for about 35 minutes; then the table rises and, by signs of knocking, the table "answers" all the questions put to it.
It goes without saying that there is no shortage of questions, but the main question that interests everyone at the present time is:
— How long will the crisis last?
The table rose and knocked 2 times, i.e. "the crisis will last another 2 years"...
To the question: when will the Messiah come? the table "declared": "in about 47 years".
As our correspondent writes, the table is a remedy for today's day-to-day troubles: people have nothing to do, so they spend at least a couple of hours at the "spiritualist séances" of Wolf Kinres's table...
An Interesting Trial Before the Dąbrowa Court

[Dąbrowa — Court.] Several months ago a meeting of merchants took place in Dąbrowa in connection with the heavy tax assessments. At the meeting Mr. J. Parasol spoke and said that the Jewish member of the assessment commission is to blame for all these tax injustices. To the question of those assembled: who is the person? Mr. Parasol did not want to say, but one of the merchants, Mr. Kleinman, shouted out:
— The person is Mr. Gutman!
On the basis of the accusation thus thrown out, Mr. Gutman brought a lawsuit against Mr. Kleinman and against a number of persons who had supported the accusation.
Last Monday the trial took place at the Dąbrowa court for the second time already. Some thirty-odd witnesses, Jews and Christians, were summoned.
But this time too the trial was not concluded, because both sides demanded that new witnesses be summoned. Among the new witnesses is also the former head of the tax office, Kozłowski, who today holds the same post in Miechów, and the former [?] official Skocylas.
